嘉靖四十一年進士登科録

玉音

嘉靖四十一年三月初九日，禮部尚書兼翰林院學士臣嚴訥等於大朝門奏，為科舉事：會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩等六十員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光禄大夫、柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩〔乙丑進士〕。
光禄大夫、柱國、少傳兼太子太師、吏部尚書兼武英殿大學士徐階〔癸未進士〕。
榮禄大夫、太子太保、户部尚書兼武英殿大學士袁煒〔戊戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Forty-first Year of Jiajing (1562)

Imperial Words

On the ninth day of the third month of the forty-first year of Jiajing, your servant Yan Na, Minister of Rites and concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others submitted the following memorial at the Dachao Gate concerning the civil-service examinations: “In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm, three hundred candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month this year, we should nominate sixty officials as Readers and other examination functionaries, including Yan Song, Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. The classes of jinshi status shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao: the first class customarily comprises three men; the first receives rank 6b, and the second and third receive rank 7a, all being granted the distinction ‘jinshi with honors.’ Those in the second class receive rank 7b and are granted ‘jinshi status.’ Those in the third class receive rank 8a and are granted ‘status equivalent to jinshi.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Yan Song held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement, Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. 〔Jinshi of the yichou year (1505).〕

Xu Jie held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor [?] and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel concurrently serving as Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. 〔Jinshi of the guiwei year (1523).〕

Yuan Wei held the titles Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Revenue concurrently serving as Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. 〔Jinshi of the wuxu year (1538).〕

translation_en:
Yang Bo held the titles Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian, and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and served as Minister of War. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jichou year.

Guo Pu held the titles Grand Master for Fostering Virtue and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and served as Minister of Personnel and Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Gao Yao held the title Grand Master for Fostering Virtue and served as Minister of Revenue. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Cai Yuncheng held the title Grand Master for Fostering Virtue and served as Minister of Justice. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.

Lei Li held the title Grand Master for Aid in Governance and served as Minister of Works. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Pan En held the title Grand Master for Aid in Governance and served as Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Li Chunfang held the title Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel and Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Dong Fen held the title Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and served as Right Vice Minister of Personnel and Academician of the Hanlin Academy, administering the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

Li Dengyun held the title Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and served as Commissioner of the Office of Transmission. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Wan Cai held the title Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and served as Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Pei Yu held the title Grand Master for Straightforward Service and served as Academician Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, administering the Academy’s affairs. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

Proctors:

Yan Ne held the title Grand Master for Fostering Virtue and served as Minister of Rites and Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

Gao Gong held the title Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and served as Left Vice Minister of Rites. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

Chen Sheng held the title Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and served as Right Vice Minister of Rites. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:

Li Qiu held the title Gentleman for Service in the Scholarly Forest and served as Investigating Censor for the Zhejiang Circuit. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Wang Shaoyuan held the title Gentleman for Service in the Scholarly Forest and served as Investigating Censor for the Guangdong Circuit. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi), a successful Metropolitan Examination candidate, of the xinmao year.

Script Receiving Officials:

Tang Ruji held the title Grand Master for Meritorious Service and served as Right Admonisher in the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent. He was a metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors
On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the forty-first year of Jiajing (1562), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat at the Dachao Gate and personally bestowed the policy question.
On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in court dress in their assigned ranks. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arrayed the imperial ceremonial equipage within the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat at the Dachao Gate. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow proclamation, led out by drums and music, and posted it outside the Chang’an Left Gate. Once it had been posted, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with ceremonial parasols, canopies, and an entourage.
On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
A banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates proceeded to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a girdle were bestowed upon the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of thanks for the imperial favor.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering ceremony (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe their names upon it.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Xu Shixing 徐時行, courtesy name Rumo, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), and was a native of Changzhou County. A county government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhou, his grandfather Qian, and his father Shizhang; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Huang. Grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Shide, Shihua, and Shijie, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xijue 王錫爵, courtesy name Yuanyu, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather Yong, and his father Mengxiang, a National University student; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brother Dingjue was a National University student, and his wife was née Zhu. He ranked fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Youding 余有丁, courtesy name Bingzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Kai and grandfather Xi both held honorary official status conferred for longevity; his father Yonglin was an Assistant Prefect, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Youren, and his wife was née Shui. He ranked fifty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

第二甲八十五名，賜進士出身。

戚元佐〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣匠籍，國子生，治春秋，字希仲，行四，年三十三，七月十六日生〕。曾祖簠，祖澤，父珊，母張氏。慈侍下，兄元宰、元輔〔進士〕、元弼，娶呂氏。浙江鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百六十五名。

項鈳〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉善縣民籍，嘉興縣人，縣學生，治書經，字東客，行一，年三十四，五月二十日生〕。曾祖衡〔贈湖廣按察司副使〕，祖忠〔太子太保、兵部尚書，諡襄毅〕，父經〔右參政〕，母盛氏。具慶下，兄鏞〔錦衣衞千戶〕、鎧〔指揮同知〕、銓〔尚寶司丞〕、鎮〔監生〕、錫〔南京光祿寺卿〕，弟鏜、銀、鈄、鎖，娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第九名，會試第八名。

陸允端〔貫直隸松江府上海縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字仲履，行二，年三十七，四月十四日生〕。曾祖虞〔贈都察院右僉都御史〕，祖奎〔日照縣丞，累贈都察院左都御史〕，父恩〔都察院左都御史〕，前母包氏〔贈淑人〕，母曹氏〔封淑人〕。永感下，兄允祚〔冠帶生員〕，弟允穆、允修〔監生〕、允亨〔中書舍人〕、允咸、允徵、允達〔監生〕、允謙、允襄、允復，娶莫氏，繼娶顧氏。應天府鄉試第五名，會試第二百十一名。
translation_en:
Second Class: eighty-five men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Qi Yuanzuo was registered in an artisan household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Xizhong and was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Ze; his father, Shan; and his mother, née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanzai, Yuanfu (a metropolitan graduate), and Yuanbi. He married a woman née Lü. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Ke was registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Jiaxing County. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Dongke and was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Heng, was posthumously granted the title of Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Huguang; his grandfather, Zhong, was Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with the posthumous name Xiangyi; his father, Jing, was Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; and his mother was née Sheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yong (Battalion Commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard), Kai (Vice Commander), Quan (Assistant Director of the Office of Imperial Seals), Zhen (an Imperial University student), and Xi (Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in Nanjing). His younger brothers were Tang, Yin, Dou, and Suo. He married a woman née Shen. He placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yunduan was registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Zhonglü and was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather, Yu, was posthumously granted the title of Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather, Kui, was Vice Magistrate of Rizhao County and received successive posthumous titles culminating in Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; and his father, En, was Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father's former wife, née Bao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (shuren); his mother, née Cao, was granted the same title during her lifetime. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yunzu (a government student granted the cap and sash of official status). His younger brothers were Yunmu, Yunxiu (an Imperial University student), Yunheng (a Secretariat Drafter), Yunxian, Yunzheng, Yunda (an Imperial University student), Yunqian, Yunxiang, and Yunfu. He married a woman née Mo and subsequently a woman née Gu. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

佘立〔貫廣西柳州衛官籍，柳州府馬平縣人，府學增廣生，治詩經，字季禮，行五，年二十六，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖幹〔進士〕，祖崇鳳〔知州〕，父勉學〔按察使〕，嫡母羅氏〔封孺人〕，生母孫氏。慈侍下，兄齊〔監生〕、亹〔推官〕、玄〔通判〕、方，娶劉氏。廣西鄉試第一名，會試第二百四十四名。

張廷臣〔貫廣東廣州府番禺縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯鄰，行一，年三十五，十月初六日生〕。曾祖璡，祖祐，父宰〔南京刑部郎中〕，嫡母吳氏，生母冼氏。永感下，兄大本，弟廷士，娶林氏。廣東鄉試第十三名，會試第十七名。

陳洙〔貫福建福州府長樂縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字伯訓，行八，年二十六，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖則安〔教授，封戶部主事，贈按察司僉事〕，祖時憲〔按察司僉事〕，父錠〔府同知〕，嫡母林氏，生母丘氏。慈侍下，兄濟、涇，弟滙、濱，娶潘氏。福建鄉試第二十三名，會試第九十五名。

郭文和〔貫金吾左衛匠籍，山西太原府陽曲縣人，國子生，治易經，字宥臣，行五，年二十七，正月十三日生〕。曾祖聰，祖智〔封禮部員外郎〕，父俊〔運司副使，前禮部郎中〕，母張氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄文輔〔州判官，前監察御史〕、文度、文弼、文壽，弟文愷，娶焦氏，繼娶王氏。順天府鄉試第二名，會試第七十四名。
translation_en:
She Li, courtesy name Jili, was registered in an official household of Liuzhou Guard, Guangxi, and was a native of Maping County, Liuzhou Prefecture. An expanded-quota student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was fifth in family order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Gan was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his grandfather Chongfeng was a Department Magistrate; and his father Mianxue was a Provincial Surveillance Commissioner. His father's principal wife, née Luo, received the title Lady for Nurture (ruren); his birth mother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Qi, an Imperial University student; Wei, a Prefectural Judge; Xuan, an Assistant Prefect; and Fang. He married a woman née Liu. He placed first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tingchen, courtesy name Bolin, was registered in a civilian household of Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in family order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather was You; and his father Zai was a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice. His father's principal wife was née Wu, and his birth mother was née Xian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Daben, and his younger brother was Tingshi. He married a woman née Lin. He placed thirteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhu, courtesy name Boxun, was registered in a civilian household of Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was eighth in family order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ze'an was a Prefectural School Instructor, received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His grandfather Shixian was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his father Ding was a Vice Prefect. His father's principal wife was née Lin, and his birth mother was née Qiu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Ji and Jing, and his younger brothers were Hui and Bin. He married a woman née Pan. He placed twenty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Wenhe, courtesy name Youchen, was registered in an artisan household of the Jinwu Left Guard and was a native of Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was fifth in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather Zhi received the honorary title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites; and his father Jun was a Vice Commissioner of a Salt Distribution Commission, formerly a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites. His mother, née Zhang, received the title Lady of Suitability (yiren). His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Wenfu, a Department Judge and former Investigating Censor; Wendu; Wenbi; and Wenshou. His younger brother was Wenkai. He married a woman née Jiao and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

朱潤身，貫應天府江寧縣民籍，直隸揚州府泰興縣人，國子生，治詩經，字德光，行一，年三十三，八月二十日生。曾祖達，祖俯，父鐶，母賈氏。永感下，弟敬身，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第一百三名，會試第一百二十四名。

徐作，貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字汝念，行三，年二十三，十二月二十日生。曾祖子明，祖仲文，父顯良，前母蕭氏，母陳氏。具慶下，兄侃、俁，弟偉，娶陳氏，繼娶李氏。江西鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百一十六名。

鄭惇典，貫福建福州府侯官縣軍籍，府學附學生，治易經，字君敕，行五，年三十，七月三十日生。曾祖晅〔封左長史〕，祖閭〔左長史，進階中憲大夫〕，父元善，母張氏。慈侍下，兄國興，娶陳氏，繼娶曾氏、薛氏。福建鄉試第六十六名，會試第八十六名。

蔡一楠，貫福建漳州府漳浦縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字廷用，行二，年三十一，九月初四日生。曾祖坦〔歲貢生〕，祖鉞，父瀚，母薛氏。重慶下，兄一椿，弟一梓、一梧、一橋、一檀、一桂、一梴、一槐，娶熊氏。福建鄉試第二十九名，會試第七十六名。
translation_en:
Zhu Runshen, courtesy name Deguang, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Taixing County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Da, his grandfather Fu, his father Huan, and his mother Lady Jia. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Jingshen, and he married Lady Chen. He placed 103rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zuo, courtesy name Runian, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ziming, his grandfather Zhongwen, and his father Xianliang; his father's former wife was Lady Xiao, and his mother was Lady Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kan and Yu, and his younger brother was Wei. He married Lady Chen and subsequently Lady Li. He placed 29th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Dundian, courtesy name Junchi, was registered in a military household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the thirtieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, honorarily appointed Left Administrator; his grandfather was Lü, Left Administrator, promoted to the rank of Grand Master for Constitutional Service; his father was Yuanshan, and his mother Lady Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Guoxing. He married Lady Chen and subsequently Lady Zeng and Lady Xue. He placed 66th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 86th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Yinan, courtesy name Tingyong, was registered in a military household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tan, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Yue, his father Han, and his mother Lady Xue. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Yichun, and his younger brothers were Yizi, Yiwu, Yiqiao, Yitan, Yigui, Yichan, and Yihuai. He married Lady Xiong. He placed 29th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 76th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Cai, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an added-quota student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Mengcheng. Sixth in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yugao; his grandfather, Wanping, was granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his father, Sui, was Minister of War at Nanjing. His mother, née Lai, was granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother, née Yan, the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jia, De (an Imperial University student), Ge (Assistant Commander), Hang, De (an Imperial University student), Xiang (a jinshi of the same examination cohort), and Du (a military provincial graduate). The transcription of the elder brothers’ names appears doubtful, including the repeated De [?]. His younger brothers were [name transcribed as ット, unreadable][?] (an Imperial University student), Ci and Shu (both government-school students), and Zhen. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Tu. He ranked ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Junmin, registered in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Bozhang. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the thirtieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Xuan, was posthumously awarded, through successive grants, the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of War. His grandfather, Zhan, served as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in Sichuan and received the same successive posthumous titles. His father, Bo, was Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel. His mother, née Duan, was granted the title Lady of the First Rank. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Junshi and Junyan (both students admitted by virtue of official family status), Junqing (a regular Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard), and Junchen. He married a woman née Shi. He ranked fortieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Lin, registered in Xinzhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingqi. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Tianxi, was a Prefectural School Instructor; his grandfather, Kang, was an Imperial University student; and his father, Chaoxuan, was a Consort of an Imperial Clanswoman. His father's principal wife was the Lady of the Township of Langqing [?], and his birth mother was née Yin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhen (a tribute scholar), Pei, and Ni. He married a woman née Zhao. He ranked twenty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shan, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanfu. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Binong (𢌿濃; reading uncertain [?]); his grandfather was Ruizhe; his father was Zhangyu; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shen and Dai. He married a woman née Kang. He ranked thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Tingyan, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in the civilian registration category, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuezhong, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bichang; his grandfather, Guangzai, was granted the title of Magistrate; his father, Yuxin, was Governor-general of Grain Storage at Nanjing and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; and his mother, née Xiao, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). His parents and at least one grandparent were living; his younger brothers were Tingxuan, Tingbin, Tingshi 廷實, Tingshi 廷試, Tingyin, Ting’an, and Tingyi; he married a woman née Zou, and placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yongjian, registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, in the civilian registration category, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Kexian, he ranked thirty-second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Jiang; his father, Wei; his legal mother, née Zhang; and his birth mother, née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Yonggui and Yongguang, the latter a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works; his younger brothers were Yongqian, Yongxiu, Yongxiang, Yongwei, Yongyi, Yongdeng, and Yongci; he married a woman née Zheng, and placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yi, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in the civilian registration category, was an additional student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shixing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan’er; his grandfather, Jufu; his father, Juan, a Magistrate; and his mother, née Shu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living; his elder brother was Zuo, and his younger brothers were Wei, Jun, Jie, Bin, Huan, Cai, and Yu; he married a woman née Lu, and placed fifty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yifan, registered in Suichang County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in the civilian registration category, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chengshu, he ranked twenty-sixth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao; his grandfather, Kui; his father, Hongyuan; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Yisheng, Yifen, and Yifang, and his younger brothers were Yifeng and Yizhen; he married a woman née Huang, and placed fifty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

閔繼禹〔貫四川敘州府南溪縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字叔敬，行一，年三十，四月初四日生〕。曾祖爵〔縣主簿〕，祖守萬，父濟，母楊氏。具慶下，兄時泰，弟師禹，娶帥氏。四川鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百六十名。

鍾振〔貫廣東廉州府合浦縣民籍，歲貢生，治詩經，字玉甫，行一，年三十一，正月初二日生〕。曾祖默，祖信，父文，母李氏。具慶下，弟揚、撰、掄、捷，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第二十五名，會試第五十七名。
translation_en:
Xu Yuanqi, registered in the scholar household category in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruhe, he ranked second in family order, and he was thirty years old, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Fang, a Steward (dianshan); his father was Qu, a County Registrar; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuance, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brothers were Yuanqi, Yuandi, Yuanxiang, Yuanxuan, Yuantai, Yuanzhen 元禎, Yuanzhi, Yuanze, Yuankai, Yuanzhen 元禛, Yuanli, and Yuanzhu. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dazhang, registered in the civilian household category in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zuyao, he ranked thirty-sixth in family order, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, a Prefectural Registrar; his grandfather was Xuan, an honorary official; his father was Fan; his father's former wife was née Dong, and his mother was née Chai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dashao and Daxia, and his wife was née Wu. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Min Jiyu, registered in the civilian household category in Nanxi County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shujing, he ranked first in family order, and he was thirty years old, born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue, a County Registrar; his grandfather was Shouwan; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shitai, his younger brother was Shiyu, and his wife was née Shuai. He placed sixty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Zhen, registered in the civilian household category in Hepu County, Lianzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yufu, he ranked first in family order, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mo; his grandfather was Xin; his father was Wen; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yang, Zhuan, Lun, and Jie, and his wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

董原道〔貫四川重慶府巴縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字性之，行一，年三十五，三月初八日生〕。曾祖文昱〔縣丞〕，祖溥〔學正〕，父誥，母母氏，繼母張氏。永感下，弟明道，娶梁氏，繼娶楊氏。四川鄉試第四十八名，會試第二十九名。

沈玄華〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣民籍，嘉興縣人，縣學生，治書經，字瑞伯，行十一，年二十四，十月十三日生〕。曾祖玟，祖璧〔贈知縣〕，父銓〔右長史〕，嫡母張氏〔封孺人〕，生母李氏。慈侍下，兄元華〔監生〕、大華、茂發〔監生〕、茂飛、華聲、華德、敷華，弟秀華、茂宗，娶彭氏。浙江鄉試第五十五名，會試第一百十五名。

史櫃〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣民籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字子美，行九，年二十八，十二月十二日生〕。曾祖吉，祖鈿，父淮，母潘氏。具慶下，兄桂〔中書舍人〕、木〔監生〕、本，弟栻、梓、機、集，娶曹氏。浙江鄉試第二十七名，會試第一百七十名。

林烴〔貫福建福州府閩縣儒籍，國子生，治春秋，字貞耀，行二，年二十三，九月初六日生〕。曾祖元美〔知府，贈南京吏部尚書，加贈太子太保〕，祖瀚〔南京兵部尚書，贈太子太保，謚文安〕，父庭機〔南京禮部右侍郎〕，母李氏〔累封淑人〕。具慶下，兄炫〔通政司右參議〕、烺〔知府〕、燦〔工部員外郎〕、熑〔翰林院修撰〕、爚、炯、焻、煠，弟熖、爔、燆，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第一百十五名，會試第一百九十五名。
translation_en:
Dong Yuandao, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, under civilian registration, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xingzhi; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Wenyu, an Assistant Magistrate; his grandfather was Pu, a School Instructor; and his father was Gao. His mother was Lady Mu [?; the transcription reads 母氏], and his stepmother was Lady Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Mingdao. He married Lady Liang and subsequently Lady Yang. He placed forty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Xuanhua, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian registration and originally from Jiaxing County, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruibo; he ranked eleventh in his family and was aged twenty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather was Bi, posthumously appointed Magistrate; and his father was Quan, a Right Chief Administrator. His father's principal wife, Lady Zhang, held the title Lady (Ruren); his birth mother was Lady Li. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Yuanhua, an Imperial University student; Dahua; Maofa, an Imperial University student; Maofei; Huasheng; Huade; and Fuhua. His younger brothers were Xiuhua and Maozong. He married Lady Peng. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Gui, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian registration, was a supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zimei; he ranked ninth in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather was Dian; his father was Huai; and his mother was Lady Pan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gui, a Central Drafting Office Secretary; Mu, an Imperial University student; and Ben. His younger brothers were Shi, Zi, Ji, and Ji. He married Lady Cao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Ting, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, under scholar registration, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhenyao; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-three, born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanmei, a Prefect, posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel at Nanjing and additionally granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. His grandfather was Han, Minister of War at Nanjing, posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the name Wen'an. His father was Tingji, Right Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing; his mother was Lady Li, repeatedly granted the title Lady of Virtue (Shuren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Right Councilor in the Office of Transmission; Lang, a Prefect; Can, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; Lian, a Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy; Yue; Jiong; Chang; and Zha. His younger brothers were Yan, Xi, and Qiao. He married Lady Chen. He placed one hundred fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Tingfu, courtesy name Liangqing, was registered in a civilian household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was twenty-fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruzheng, his grandfather Qingzhong, his father Wensheng, and his mother née Hou. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Tingxiang, and his wife was née Li. He ranked forty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jingwei, courtesy name Daofu, was registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student at the Nanchang County school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was ninth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanjing, his grandfather Zongzheng, his father Wu, and his mother née Jin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Jinglun, Jingji (Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments), Jingbang, and Jingshi; his younger brother was Jingming. His wife was née Zhou. He ranked ninety-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shihua, courtesy name Maocheng, was registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourteenth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ling (a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title), his grandfather Jie (a Subprefectural Judge), his father Dagang (posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice), and his mother née Shao (posthumously granted the title Lady of Tranquility). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shifang (a Prefect) and Shiying; his younger brothers were Shimei and Shifan. His wife was née Shao. He ranked seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Yu, courtesy name Junming, was registered in a civilian household in Rugao County, Taizhou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Lin, his father Fei (a County Registrar), and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were En and Zhi (an Imperial University student), and his wife was née Sun. He ranked fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Fuyuan, courtesy name Mengzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongming; his grandfather, Fu; his father, Song; and his mother, née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Daoyuan, Zhiyuan, and Xingyuan, and his wife was née Shu. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xuezeng, courtesy name Rulu, was registered in a military household of Dongsheng Right Guard and was a native of Yangcheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A government student of Zunhua County, Shuntian Prefecture, specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ding, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, Ming, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Cong, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Feng. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Xueshi, Xueli (an annual tribute student), Xueyi, Xueshu, and Xuekong; his younger brother was Xuemeng; and his wife was née Li. He placed fifty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Fan, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in an official household of Chengtian Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged fifty-one, and born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Gong, was a Vice Commander; his grandfather, Xun, was a District Magistrate; his father was Hui; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Lu. His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Zhong (a Battalion Commander) and He; his younger brothers were Bing and Yue; and his wife was née Cong. He placed thirty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Zideng, courtesy name Yijian, was registered in a military household of Xingzhou Rear Garrison Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ding, was an Imperial Physician; his grandfather, Kui, was a Clerk in the Imperial Medical Academy; his father, Yinglong, held the conferred title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Huang, held the conferred title of Lady of Peace. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Zichao (a Prefect), Liangfu, Zihe, and Zibang; his younger brothers were Ziliang, Zixue, Zijin, Zijin, and Zipin (the two names rendered Zijin are 子覲 and 子晉 respectively); and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Feng Mingong, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuanqing; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Jun, was a magistrate; and his father, Rubi, was a prefectural vice prefect, formerly a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works. His mother, née Tu, received the title of Lady (ruren); his stepmother was née Xu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Minde, Minshi, Minxue, and Minqiu; his younger brothers were Minxun, Minxiao, Mindao, and Minsheng. His wife was née Cao. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tongzan, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Fangfu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather, Gang; his father, Shuzhong; and his mother, née Shi. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Tongren, Tongyi, Tonghua, Tonglun, Tongren, and Tongyan (同仁、同議、同化、同論、同任、同儼). His wife was née Tang. He placed eightieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Sijiao, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenda; his grandfather, Kuang, was an erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing; his father was Lian; and his mother was née Dai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Siming, Sicong, and Simin; his younger brothers were Sizheng, Sishao, and Simu. His wife was née Zhu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Hao, registered in the Hangzhou Right Guard, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a Hangzhou prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yangzheng; he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Hong; his father, Kui; and his mother, née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Shen. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳有年〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字登之，行三十七，年三十二，二月初九日生〕。曾祖孟昻〔贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖巨理〔贈都察院右副都御史〕，父克宅〔都察院右副都御史〕，母虞氏〔封淑人〕。慈侍下，兄有勳〔監生〕、有濟、有孚〔監生〕，娶邵氏。順天府鄉試第二名，會試第八十一名。

張允濟〔貫順天府固安縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字愛甫，行六，年二十七，九月十九日生〕。曾祖璽，祖志〔府同知〕，父佳運〔州吏目〕，嫡母李氏，繼母李氏、王氏，生母朱氏。慈侍下，兄允承、允升、允立、允諧、允熈，弟允繼、允修，娶金氏。順天府鄉試第五十六名，會試第二百三十六名。
translation_en:
Lü Huo, courtesy name Chenqing, was registered in a civilian household in Lingling County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was sixth in family order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a county Registrar; his grandfather was Hong, a National University student; his father was Diaoyang; and his mother was née Deng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jie, Zhi, Hui, and Lan, and his younger brothers were Zao and Ping. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Zhongyin, courtesy name Benxie, was registered in a civilian household in Zunhua County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was originally from Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in family order, aged thirty, and born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather was Shan, who received the honorary title of County Magistrate; and his father was Ying, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His legal mother was née Li, posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his stepmother was née Li, granted the title Lady (ruren); and his birth mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zhongqi and Zhongyan, and his younger brothers were Zhongyi, Zhongchan, and Zhongjing. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Younian, courtesy name Dengzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was thirty-seventh in family order, aged thirty-two, and born on the ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Meng'ang and his grandfather was Juli, both posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Kezhai, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and his mother was née Yu, granted the title Lady (shuren). His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Youxun, a National University student, Youji, and Youfu, also a National University student. He married a woman née Shao. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yunji, courtesy name Aifu, was registered in a civilian household in Gu'an County, Shuntian Prefecture. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was sixth in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xi; his grandfather was Zhi, a Prefectural Vice Prefect; and his father was Jiayun, a subprefectural Clerk. His legal mother was née Li, his stepmothers were née Li and née Wang, and his birth mother was née Zhu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yuncheng, Yunsheng, Yunli, Yunxie, and Yunxi, and his younger brothers were Yunji (允繼) and Yunxiu. He married a woman née Jin. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

史詡〔貫江西吉安府永新縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字克敏，行一，年三十五，九月初二日生〕。曾祖文莊，祖晉，父珎，母賀氏。具慶下，弟訓、講，娶王氏。江西鄉試第四十八名，會試第五十名。

translation_en:
Wang Ximing 王錫命 was registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, his courtesy name was Tianyu; he ranked first in family order and was aged twenty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Pin, his father Luan, and his mother née Zhong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Li and Lin, and his wife was née Qian. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Guze 馬顧澤 was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Wu County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, his courtesy name was Shiqing; he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Wenyu, his father Yin, his mother née Gu, and his stepmother née Yi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Guzhou, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Xu 史詡 was registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, his courtesy name was Kemin; he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-five, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhuang, his grandfather Jin, his father Zhen, and his mother née He. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xun and Jiang, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xueyi 陳學伊 was registered in a civilian household in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, his courtesy name was Erpin; he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Zuo, his father Duanlang, an Instructor of Medicine, and his mother née Zhuang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xuekong, Xuemeng, Xuekui, Xueliang, and Yan [the division of the last two names is uncertain: 學良言]; his younger brothers were Xuezhu, Xuecheng, and Xuegao. His wife was née Huang. He placed fortieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Qiaoxiang, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tinghan; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty, and was born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Puqin, and his father Cheng; his father's principal wife was née Zheng, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Qiaocai, and his younger brothers were Qiaosen and Qiaozhu. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Kexian, registered in a civilian household in Cheng'an County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziqi; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twelfth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was He, his grandfather Guo, and his father Shaoxian, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Kejiao, was a prefectural Judge, and his younger brother was Kejiu. He married a woman née Wu. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhuo, registered in a civilian household in Bin Subprefecture, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, and originally from Shanglin County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Chunbo; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daoying, his grandfather Neng, and his father Bangzhu, a School Instructor; his mother was née Shi. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Tun. He married a woman née Liao. He placed fifth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Yingyuan, registered in a military household in Zunhua County, Shuntian Prefecture, and originally from Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and sash under provisions for imperial favor; his grandfather was Rong, his father Xiang, and his mother née Fu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingwen, Yingkui, and Yinghong. He married a woman née Gao. He placed forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Ye, registered in a military household in Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guangyu; he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Ang; and his father was Liangxiang, a prefectural clerk. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Chang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Lian, Huan, and Huang, and his wife was née Long. He placed fiftieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Bai, registered in a military household in Pucheng County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shouqing; he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wenmao; his grandfather was Ximian; and his father was Xian, who held an honorary official title for longevity. His legal mother and his birth mother were both née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Sen and Liang, and his wife was née Su. He placed sixty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wen, registered in an official household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongqi; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-seven years old, and was born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Peng; his grandfather was Mu, a station master; and his father was Deng. His father's former wife was née Bian, and his mother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Pan, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brother was Wei. His wife was née Wu. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xuegu, registered in a civilian household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, and originally from Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Youhuo; he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, a granary supervisor; his grandfather was Hong, who held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father was Liang. His mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shanggu, Xiangu, and Chonggu, and his wife was née Wu. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hong Xin, registered in a military household in Puzhou, Shanxi, and a native of Dingliao Guard, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shouqing, he ranked third in family order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingwen; his grandfather, Xi; and his father, Jiuchou, a Director of Delicacies. His father's former wife was née Guo, his mother née Feng, and his stepmother also née Feng. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Bu, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and Wei; his younger brother was Yue. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Yao. He placed eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuzhi, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Daqing, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather, Xiwen, was granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Ting, was Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing. His father's former wife, née Chen, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his mother, née Yang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Heng, Hong, Xuan, and Chen; his younger brothers were Weizhi, Jizhi, Suizhi, Jizhi, Buzhi, and Xianzhi. He married a woman née Yong. He placed thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fei Yaonian, registered in a civilian household in Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xizhi, he ranked third in family order, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Fan, was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, Junior Guardian concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. His grandfather, Wan, was formerly a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works; his father, Maowen, was a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Henian and Guinian, and his younger brother was Changnian. He married a woman née Wei. He placed thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Fei, registered in a military household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and a native of Panyu County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Duzhou, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Zheng; his father, Dazhi, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Liang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Pan, a tribute student, and Su. He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently another woman née Zhao. He placed sixty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ye Shibin, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shangbin; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tiyi, posthumously appointed Right Administration Vice Commissioner; his grandfather was Zhong, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Rites and subsequently Right Administration Vice Commissioner; and his father was Heng, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner. His legal mother was née Chen, granted the title Lady of Virtue (shuren), and his birth mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shiyuan, Shileng, Shiqing, Shixu, Shirong (士容), Shikui, and Shiding; his younger brothers were Shirong (士榮), Shizhi, Shijun, Shiyin, and Shizhen. He married née Yao. He placed seventy-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Yingbi, registered in a civilian household in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weizhang; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yi (𨓜), his grandfather was Sigong, and his father was Dong, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his mother was née Gui. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brother was Yingbin. He married née Qu and subsequently née Han. He placed twenty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ruyun, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weiming; he ranked thirteenth in birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zifu; his grandfather, Weiqing, and his father, Yongshi, both held honorary official status conferred for longevity. His legal mother was née Wu and his birth mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rubin; Ruli, an official [?]; Rudong, Steward of Provisions; Ruduan, an Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Ruyan, a Department Vice Magistrate; Ruzhang, a student of the Directorate of Education; Runan, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; Ruqian; and Rubi. His younger brother was Ruyi. He married née Qin. He placed sixty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xi, registered in a civilian household in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a department school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yiji; he ranked seventh in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather was Lian, and his father was Dalin, granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and belt under provisions for imperial favor. His mother was née Yuan and his stepmother was née Zhu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Hu, Yin, Qi, a County Magistrate, Zhi, and Zuo, a tribute student. He married née Zhang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Cha 諸察, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he ranked eighteenth in family birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, a prestige official of the seventh rank; his grandfather was Wenshi, a district magistrate; his father was Shi, and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yin and Wan; his younger brothers were Hui, Guan, Ding, Ning, Yi, and Yan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Feng 王俸, registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional-quota student of the prefectural school in Xiushui County [?] and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Lianfu; he ranked first in family birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the thirtieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather was Yu, his father was Zhou, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hua and Yan. He married a woman née Gu. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dazhong 張大忠, registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Pinghu County, was a county-school student and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Guozhen; he ranked first in family birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Lei, his grandfather was Xie, his father was Zaidao, an Imperial University student, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Daya, an Imperial University student, and Dakui; his younger brothers were Daxiao, Daquan, Feng'ao, Fengyi, Fengming, Dalun, Dabin, Dazhang, Daheng, Daqi, and Dacai. He married a woman née Yao. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Jixun 游季勲, registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maofu; he ranked second in family birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Bi, an administrator; his grandfather was Qian, a department magistrate; his father was Ben, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Gan. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Mengyan, Qingyan, Zhongyan, and Shuyan; his younger brothers were Jingyan, Zongyan, and Jiyan. He married a woman née Deng. He placed twenty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Yingshi, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a military household of the Left Yulin Guard and was a native of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Xiang; and his father, Shizeng, a Secretariat Drafter. His mother was née Chen, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingdeng, Yingqi, Yingzhao, and Yingsu; his younger brothers were Yingnian, Yingshou, and Yingyang. He married a woman née Liang. He ranked thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yingyuan, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in an official household of Chengtian Guard, Huguang. A student of the Chengtian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, an official with a prestige title; his grandfather, Da; and his father, Jing. His father's former wife was née He, and his mother was née Qin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingheng and Yingshi. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Zhang. He ranked fifty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Nan, courtesy name Zhongmu, was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, posthumously granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather, Pei, a Prefect; and his father, Ruwei. His mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Yin. He ranked eighth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiuge, courtesy name Zhongyi, was registered in a military household in Caozhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Subprefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youxian; his grandfather, Wenju; and his father, Tianxu, a Steward. His mother was née Du; his stepmothers were née Chu and née Gua. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Jiude, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brother was Jiugong. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked forty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫坤〔貫河南歸德府睢州民籍，州學生，治書經，字順夫，行五，年三十一，六月初四日生〕。曾祖銘〔知縣〕，祖憲文，父守中〔典膳〕，前母朱氏，母劉氏。永感下，兄塘、塏、坦、域〔貢士〕，娶劉氏。河南鄉試第十四名，會試第一百六名。
translation_en:
Chen Jun 陳俊, courtesy name Yanwu, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xibao; his grandfather, Qing; his father, He; and his mother, née Yao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xun, and his wife was née Guo. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Kongxing 吳孔性, courtesy name Cuiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Suichang County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ting; his grandfather, Su; his father, Wenyuan; and his mother, née Zheng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kai and Ti, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked eighty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Gang 梁綱, courtesy name Lifu, was registered in a Confucian scholar household in Jishan County, Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhu, was a Police Chief; his grandfather, Pu, was an Administrator, posthumously conferred the title Grand Master for Governance; his father, Ge, was a Supervising Secretary in the Nanjing Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs; and his mother, née Hao, was granted the title Lady. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother, Ji, and younger brother, Wei, were both government-stipended students. His wife was née Hao; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He ranked first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Kun 孫坤, courtesy name Shunfu, was registered in a civilian household in Suizhou, Guide Prefecture, Henan. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ming, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Xianwen; and his father, Shouzhong, was a Provisioner. His father's former wife was née Zhu, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tang, Kai, Tan, and Yu, the last a tribute student. His wife was née Liu. He ranked fourteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Bo, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a military household of Chenzhou Guard, Henan, and was a student of the Chenzhou prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Shangru, his father Weiyue, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Jian and his younger brother Han; his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xizhao, courtesy name Yunan, was registered in a military household of Gaoyuan County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiju, his grandfather Pan, and his father Xu; his father's former wife was née Cui and his mother née Dong. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xiyin, Xiji (a county school student), and Xilong; his wife was née Wang. He placed seventieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xian, courtesy name Ziji, was registered in a civilian household of Cangxi County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. Third in birth order, he was aged forty-two and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Jie, his father Zhongcai, and his mother née Luo; both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenren and his younger brother Zhi; his wife was née Huang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Yijing, courtesy name Zizheng, was registered in a civilian household of Guichi County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the eleventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Xi, his father Guichang, and his mother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Yidong; his younger brothers were Yiming, Yian, Yigui, Yixiang, and Yiru. His wife was née Fu. He placed 124th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Nanjin, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Guoliang. He ranked first in birth order, was aged forty-four, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zong, his grandfather Cong, and his father Huai, a commissioner of an unspecified office [?]. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Jiang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Nanyang, Nanyong, and Nandu. He married a woman née Song and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tingshou, registered in Chun'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shouzhi. He ranked fifth in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Huan, his father Ye, and his mother née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Tingyong and Tingshen. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Zhensun, registered in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xingru. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yue, his grandfather Yongquan, and his father Rui, an assistant prefect; his mother was née Luo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Gengsun, and his younger brothers were Qisun, Sisun, Yansun, and Shusun. He married a woman née Liang. He placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xian Bangheng (佡邦衡; surname uncertain [?]), registered in Qianjiang County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhiyi. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the fifteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xian, a county registrar; his grandfather was Yingkui, an assistant instructor; and his father was Zi, an instructor. His mother was née He. Both parents were living. He married a woman née He. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.
