□□ Shou (the first two characters of his name are illegible) was registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Xiushui County. A prefectural government school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixin, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-one sui, born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Gang, was a County Magistrate; and his father, Quan, was an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial. His father's principal wife was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yuangong, was a Recorder in the Directorate of Imperial Parks; his younger brother, Yuanbian, was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Mengxian was registered in a civilian household in Hukou County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county government school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruyu, and he ranked sixth in birth order. He was thirty-five sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhonghou, his grandfather was Gui, and his father was Luan. His father's former wife was née Cao, and his mother was née Mei. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Mengxuan, Mengfu, and Mengzhuang, the last a Subprefectural Assistant Judge; his younger brother, Rufang, was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Rao. He placed seventy-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

杜輅〔貫山東兖州府泗水縣匠籍，縣學生，治詩經，字從殷，行二，年二十七，六月初五日生〕。曾祖盛〔壽官〕，祖錫〔縣丞〕，父學詩〔府通判〕，母呂氏。重慶下，兄時，弟冕，娶孔氏。山東鄉試第八名，會試第四十名。

王乾章〔貫浙江金華府東陽縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字順卿，行一百五十，年三十四，九月初二日生〕。曾祖得志，祖垿〔教諭〕，父寛〔教諭〕，母蔡氏。慈侍下，兄頤章、樂章、惠章、孝章、廷章，弟大章、建章，娶郭氏，繼娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第三十六名，會試第九十二名。
translation_en:
Third Class: 211 men, granted the status of having an equivalent background to metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Cai Shukui, courtesy name Yujian, was registered in a military household of the Weihui Guarding Battalion in Henan and was a native of Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Weihui Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first in his family’s birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Run, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Jingyu, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Yangjin, an Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Yang, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shumai, Shulin, and Shujin. He married a woman née Jiao. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Lu, courtesy name Congyin, was registered in an artisan household in Sishui County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second in his family’s birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Xi, a County Vice Magistrate; and his father was Xueshi, an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Lü. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Shi, and his younger brother was Mian. He married a woman née Kong. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qianzhang, courtesy name Shunqing, was registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked 150th in his family’s birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dezhi; his grandfather was Xu, a School Instructor; and his father was Kuan, also a School Instructor. His mother was née Cai. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yizhang, Lezhang, Huizhang, Xiaozhang, and Tingzhang; his younger brothers were Dazhang and Jianzhang. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Chonglun, registered in Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zichang, and he ranked second among his brothers. His age and birth-date entry is garbled (〇〇四十一月十九日生), apparently recording birth on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month [?]. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Bofu, his father Yunqiong, and his mother Lady Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chongshi, and he married Lady Chen. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Zhao, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tinglun, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-eight, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongkai, his grandfather Cui, and his father Zongyuan, a Chief Clerk. His father’s former wives were Lady Chen and Lady Liu; his mother was Lady Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother Jian was a District Magistrate. He married Lady Mai. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Conglü, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an supplementary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Maohe, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Yuanyuan, his father Yi, and his mother Lady Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Congzheng and Congyan, and he married Lady Qian. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Lian, registered in Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ximao, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Xian, an Assistant Instructor, and his father Kai, an annual tribute student. His mother was Lady Yang, and his stepmother Lady Shan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xun and Ting, and he married Lady Chen. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

崔鏞〔貫陝西綏德衞官籍，直隸鳳陽府潁上縣人，榆林衞學生，治詩經，字汝洪，行二，年三十三，八月二十日生〕。曾祖岩〔千戶，贈都指揮僉事〕，祖林〔千戶，贈都指揮僉事〕，父經〔都指揮僉事〕，母柳氏〔贈淑人〕，繼母王氏〔封淑人〕。具慶下，兄鎭，弟鑰、鉊，娶蘇氏。陝西鄉試第三十名，會試第二十二名。
translation_en:
Ji Datong, courtesy name Bocong, was registered in an artisan household in Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the departmental school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather, Chen, received the honorary title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Cheng, was Grand Coordinator of Liaodong and Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Right in the Censorate. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his stepmother, née Li, was granted the same title. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Dashao, Daxia, Dawu, Dazhuang, Daguan, Dalin, Dabin, Dashun, and Daning. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yizhong, courtesy name Zongxian, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather, Huai; his father, Jing; and his mother, née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yiyuan, Fengming, Yiheng, Yilan, and Yihua. He married a woman née Fu. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Tingguan, courtesy name Binqing, was registered in a civilian household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather, Luan; his father, Kexue; and his mother, née Wen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingwang, and his younger brothers were Tingdui and Tingmo. He married a woman née Zhuang and subsequently a woman née Gu. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Yong, courtesy name Ruhong, was registered in a military officer household in Suide Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Yingshang County, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Yulin Guard school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yan, and grandfather, Lin, were both Battalion Commanders posthumously granted the title of Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; his father, Jing, was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His mother, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title Lady (shuren), and his stepmother, née Wang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhen, and his younger brothers were Yue and Zhao. He married a woman née Su. He placed thirtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Tai, courtesy name Junzuo, was registered in Shouchang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Kezheng, was a County Registrar; his grandfather, Tingqi, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father, Ao, was a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Xiang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, and his younger brothers were Du and Xu. His wife was née Xu. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhen, courtesy name Zongyan, was registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An attached student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengren; his grandfather, Jianchang; his father, Bingxin; and his mother, née Fu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brother was Mei. His wife was née Yu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Xiang, courtesy name Mengliang, was registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, and was a native of Xiushui County. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Liang; his father, Gao, an annual tribute student; and his mother, née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fen and Wu. His wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ai Qi, courtesy name Zizheng, was registered in Mizhi County, Suide Subprefecture, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Wenji, was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Hui, was posthumously granted the title of Secretary and subsequently that of Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father was Xiqing, and his mother was née Gao. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhen, a student of the Directorate of Education; Jia, a Vice Battalion Commander; and Wei, an annual tribute student. His younger brothers were Zi, an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; Shu, credited with frontier military merit; Cong; Si; Luo; Lai; and Chengdao. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Mo 王謨 was registered in a military household of Yingchuan Guard, Henan, and was a native of Dongping Subprefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tiwen; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Mian, and his father Bangyi, who held an honorary title for longevity; his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xun, Gao, and Wenjiong, an Usher. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Weijing 吳維京 was registered in a military household of Xiaofeng County, Anji Subprefecture, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shuji; he ranked seventeenth among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, who held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather Song was granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Personnel. His father Lin was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Exemplary Service. His father's former wives were a woman née Wang, posthumously granted the title Lady, and another woman née Wang; his mother was née Fang, posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Weiyue, a Surveillance Commissioner; Wei[?] (維𡹘), an Imperial University student; and Weixia, also an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Weicheng, followed in the small-character annotation by Weiyu, Weijun, Weikai, Weiji, Weishan, and Weibang. He married a woman née Pu. He placed fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhimeng 劉之蒙 was registered in a civilian household of Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shuzheng; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, who held an honorary title for righteousness; his grandfather Sui held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father Wei was a County Registrar; his mother was née Ren and his stepmother née Zhang. His father alone was living. His younger brother was Qimeng. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Kong. He placed one hundred twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yiqin 吳一琴 was registered in a civilian household of Cheng'an County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziqing; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sen, his grandfather Ze, who held an honorary title for longevity, and his father Mao; his mother was née Liu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Yilin and Yigui, and his younger brothers Yicheng and Yihe. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently women née Li and née Yang. He placed one hundred thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Aizhong 范愛衆, courtesy name Tongren, was registered in a military household of Dongsheng Right Guard and was a native of Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Zunhua County School in Shuntian Prefecture, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Cong, and his father Gong; his father's former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née Yuan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuzhong and Yuzhong (御衆 and 與衆). He married a woman née Gao. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yiren 孫以仁, courtesy name Xueyuan, was registered in a banner household of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangneng, his grandfather Long〔a Professor〕, and his father Rang; his mother was née Cai. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Yihua. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently women née Cong and née Zhao. He placed twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Sanjie 袁三接, courtesy name Bangtai, was registered in a military household of Xiangshan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An attached student of the Panyu County School, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kui, his grandfather Zusheng, and his father Jingsheng; his mother was née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shaoji and Sande, and his younger brothers Sansheng, Sanwei, and Sanxi. He married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lie 陳烈, courtesy name Sishao, was registered in a civilian household of Jian'an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun〔an Assistant Instructor〕, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Nan〔an annual tribute student〕; his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhao, Xi, Weiqian, Tao, Shu, Heng, Jing, Jian, Li, Rang, Peng, Xiong, and He. He married a woman née Tong. He placed fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Tongdao 王同道, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a military household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenkai, granted the title of County Magistrate; his grandfather was Lin, a County Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Tinghuai, a Secretary. His father's principal wife was née Hu, and his birth mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tonghe, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Tong’en, Tongyuan, and Tongsheng; his younger brothers were Tonghui, Tonggui, Tonglun, Tongchen, and Tongqing. He married a woman née Guo. He placed thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Weiguan 李惟觀, courtesy name Dongke, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiong; his grandfather was Zongsheng, an annual tribute student; and his father was Ao, a County Magistrate. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Weiqiao, a School Instructor, Weiduan, Weisu, Weida, and Weikang; his younger brothers were Weiyin and Weixing, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi). He married a woman née He. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Zi 嚴鎡, courtesy name Yingshi, was registered in a cook household attached to the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was a native of Fengrun County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen, his grandfather was Jin, and his father was Xiong. His mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Cong, and his younger brothers were Zhen and Ming. He married a woman née He and subsequently a woman née Lu. He placed 124th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Hui 馬會, courtesy name Yuanming, was registered in a civilian household in Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziwang; his grandfather was Yong; and his father was Mengshe, a County Vice Magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Li, and his birth mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shi, an annual tribute student; Zhongyuan, an Administrative Assistant in a Regional Military Commission; Xiao; Shu; Yao; Jin, an Assistant Instructor; Bian; and Dan, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His younger brother was Bing, also a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Sun. He placed forty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Liang, courtesy name Fuwu, was registered in a civilian household in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather Jian, his father Zhen, and his mother née Zhuang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Ji, Hao, and Qian; he married a woman née Zheng. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yiben, courtesy name Zhongli, was registered in a military household of Mianyang Guard, Huguang. An added-quota student at the Mianyang Subprefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Jing, and his father Xian, an Instructor; his mother was née Yang and his stepmother née Xiang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yidong, and his younger brothers were Yizhen, Yicai, and Yishi; he married a woman née Yang. He placed seventy-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Bangyan, courtesy name Xianzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural-school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benshan, his grandfather Huan, and his father He; his legal mother was née Liang and his birth mother née Bu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Bangxian; he married a woman née Zhao. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Renyuan, courtesy name Zishan, was registered in a military household in Wanquan County, Puzhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Yu, an honorary official, his father Chaozhong, and his mother née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Renheng and Fuyuan; he married a woman née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

秦崢〔貫直隸大名府開州長垣縣，匠籍，國子生，治易經，字思謙，行一，年三十六，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖浩，祖忠，父佐，母朱氏。慈侍下，弟岍，娶顧氏。順天府鄉試第七十三名，會試第二百八十名。
translation_en:
Huang Wenwei, registered in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name was Dehua. He ranked third among his brothers, was twenty-two years old, and was born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rixin, his grandfather Yuqing, and his father Jirong; his mother was née Feng and his stepmother née Peng. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Wensui and Wenyao, and his wife was née Wu. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shizeng, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name was Yinfu. He ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, granted the title of Assistant Administration Commissioner; his grandfather was Henian, an Administration Vice Commissioner; his father was Qiyuan and his mother née Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiji, Shishang, Shizhe, Shitan, Shijie, Shixuan, Shifang, Shide, Shirong, Shimao, and Shizhen. His wife was née Huang. He placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Shoushen was registered in an official household of Huaiqing Guard, Henan, and was a native of Yunmeng County, De'an Prefecture, Huguang. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes (Shijing); his courtesy name was Shangben. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather was Rui, an Official for Righteousness; his father was Luan, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shoumo, an Assistant Commander; Shouji, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong; Shouyu; Shoubi, a Department Magistrate; Shoudao; Shouxing; Shoukui; Shoujie; Shoushan; Shoujing; Shoulong; Shoupan; and Shouyi. He placed twenty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Zheng, registered in Changyuan County, Kai Department, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name was Siqian. He ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Zuo; his mother was née Zhu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brother was Qian, and his wife was née Gu. He placed seventy-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Yu, registered in a civilian household in Anyi County, Jiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a supplementary student at the school of the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zida; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Wen, and his father Jide; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Dang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chong, Ning, and Yin, and his wife was née Hu. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jiamo, registered in a civilian household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Rui, and his father Chaoyong, a Police Chief; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiaji, Jiaqing, and Jiayou, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Ji, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a supplementary student at the county school and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ruoheng; he ranked tenth in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiliang, his grandfather Zhengfu, a Station Master, and his father Shizi; his father’s former wife was née Zuo and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yue and Shi, and his wife was née Tian. He placed eighty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Donghai, registered in a civilian household in Shizhou Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a supplementary student at the subprefectural school and specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruguan; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhang, an honorary official, his grandfather Xuan, a Steward, and his father Jinchao; his mother was née Wen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dongzhou, Donglu, and Dongwu, and his wife was née Feng. He placed forty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

彭富〔貫雲南大理衛官籍，直隸廬州府合肥縣人，國子生，治詩經，字中禮，行三，年二十八，七月初三日生〕。曾祖英〔百戶〕，祖海〔百戶〕，父舉〔百戶〕，母朱氏。具慶下，兄榮〔百戶〕、華，弟魁、冠、憲，娶蔣氏。雲南鄉試第二名，會試第二百五十一名。

王嘉祥〔貫山東東昌府莘縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字兆興，行一，年三十五，十二月十六日生〕。曾祖琮〔知縣〕，祖緯，父聘，母任氏〔旌表貞節〕。慈侍下，娶虞氏。山東鄉試第六十九名，會試第一百五名。
translation_en:
Li Xuedao, registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ruzhi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mi, his grandfather Qiong, his father Siming, and his mother née Lu. His parents and grandparent generation were living. His younger brothers were Xueshi, Xueyi, Xueshu, Xuemeng, Xuewen, Xueyuan, and Xueshen; his wife was née Du. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Yingqian, registered in a civilian household in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Bofu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zeng, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather Rui, an Assistant Instructor; his father Li, an honorary official for public beneficence; and his mother née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zizhong; his wife was née Zhao. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fu, registered in an official household of Dali Guard, Yunnan, was a native of Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongli; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ying, grandfather Hai, and father Ju were all Company Commanders; his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rong, a Company Commander, and Hua; his younger brothers were Kui, Guan, and Xian. His wife was née Jiang. He placed second in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiaxiang, registered in a military household in Shen County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhaoxing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, a District Magistrate; his grandfather Wei; his father Pin; and his mother née Ren, who received an official commendation for chastity and fidelity. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

薛德統〔貫福建福州府福清縣，鹽籍，縣學生，治詩經，字守正，行五，年三十八，十一月初四日生〕。曾祖士亘〔封戶部主事〕，祖世暊，父尚飛〔衛經歷〕，前母郭氏，母石氏。永感下，兄德緒、德忠〔訓導〕、德王、德琯、德珫〔義官〕、德璩、德璲、德佐〔封刑科給事中〕，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百十名。

舒應龍〔貫廣西桂林府全州，民籍，賓州人，州學增廣生，治禮記，字時見，行二，年二十二，十一月十二日生〕。曾祖綱〔教諭〕，祖文奎〔知縣〕，父烈，母袁氏。具慶下，兄應蘭，弟應元、應麟、應鳳、應蕙，娶蔣氏。廣西鄉試第十三名，會試第十二名。

劉早〔貫山東萊州府膠州，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字思舜，行九，年四十二，九月十二日生〕。曾祖福，祖紀，父瑤〔府司獄〕，母王氏。具慶下，娶欒氏。山東鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百四十四名。
translation_en:
Tian Chengfa, courtesy name Zixian, was registered in a civilian household in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one [?; the transcription has 生 in place of the expected 年], and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was You; his grandfather, Jing; his father, 𡉙 [reading uncertain], an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Chang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Chengfu. He married a woman née Feng and subsequently a woman née Yu. He ranked eighteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Detong, courtesy name Shouzheng, was registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shigen, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Shixu; and his father, Shangfei, a Guard Registrar. His father's former wife was née Guo, and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dexu, Dezhong (an Assistant Instructor), Dewang, Deguan, Dechong (an Honorary Official), Dequ, Desui, and Dezuo (granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice). He married a woman née Zheng. He ranked thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Yinglong, courtesy name Shijian, was registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, and was originally from Binzhou. An expanded-quota student at the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Gang, an Instructor; his grandfather, Wenkui, a District Magistrate; his father, Lie; and his mother, née Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yinglan, and his younger brothers were Yingyuan, Yinglin, Yingfeng, and Yinghui. He married a woman née Jiang. He ranked thirteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zao, courtesy name Sishun, was registered in a military household in Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was ninth in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Ji; his father, Yao, a prefectural Prison Warden; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Luan. He ranked forty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Zhu, registered in a civilian household in □□ County, Qianzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Boshi, he ranked ninth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Rang, his father Ruzhen (Prefectural School Professor), and his mother née Kang; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yingzhong, Yingxiang, Zhu [?—the same given name as the candidate], Yingqi, Yingfu (County School Instructor), Yingyou (Secretary), Yinghe, and Gao; his younger brothers were Quan (a provincial graduate, juren) and Qin. He married née Fei and subsequently née Yan. He placed thirty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Tingwang, registered in a military household in Xinhua County, Baoqing Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Daowu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Fuzan, his grandfather Minhui, his father Chuxi, and his mother née Zeng; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingzhao and Tinggao. He married née Sun. He placed fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yizheng, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guanfu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Feng (County Registrar, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of War), his father Maoyi (Left Administration Vice Commissioner), and his mother née Gui (granted the title Lady of Suitability); his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Yisu; his younger brothers were Yizhong, Yida, Yiming, Yizhen, Yishan, Yijian, and Yiqing. He married née Wang. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Pei, registered in a civilian household in Yu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xiangde, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Bao, his grandfather Bin, his father Yuan, and his mother née Wen; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bi, Zhang, and Huan. He married née Zhao. He placed fourteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊成名〔貫福建建寧府建安縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字志完，行一，年三十三，二月二十三日生〕。曾祖旦〔吏部尚書〕，祖京〔太僕寺寺丞〕，父謙，母滕氏。慈侍下，娶倪氏，繼娶黃氏。福建鄉試第四十五名，會試第二百七十八名。

趙應元〔貫浙江杭州府仁和縣，民籍，直隸六安州學訓導，治易經，字子貞，行一，年三十二，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖善，祖宣，父文遠，母王氏。永感下，兄奎、麟、鑾、森，弟相、卿、宰、材，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第十名，會試第二百六十四名。

劉翾〔貫四川成都府內江縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治春秋，字惟翰，行一，年三十六，十月二十八日生〕。曾祖時和，祖綵〔教授，贈布政司參議〕，父望之〔左布政使〕，前母田氏〔贈恭人〕，母張氏〔封恭人〕。嚴侍下，兄三正〔按察司僉事〕、涵〔府通判〕、潭、克讓，弟〔羽貢士〕䎉、翊、翉、詡、翧，娶蕭氏。四川鄉試第五名，會試第一百四十七名。
translation_en:
Li E 李鶚, registered in Lingshou County, Zhending Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Lingqiu, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Jing, and his father Xun; his legal mother was née Chen and his birth mother née Nie. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was He, and his younger brothers were Fengming, Fengteng, Feng’ao, Fenghuang, and Fengyi. His wife was née Peng. He placed ninety-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Chengming 楊成名, registered in Jian’an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhiwan, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Dan, Minister of Personnel; his grandfather was Jing, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his father was Qian and his mother née Teng. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Ni and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed forty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yingyuan 趙應元, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and served as Assistant Instructor at the subprefectural school of Lu’an in the Metropolitan Region, specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zizhen, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Xuan, his father Wenyuan, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kui, Lin, Luan, and Sen, and his younger brothers Xiang, Qing, Zai, and Cai. His wife was née Wang. He placed tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xuan 劉翾, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weihan, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shihe; his grandfather was Cai, a Professor posthumously appointed Assistant Provincial Administration Commissioner; his father was Wangzhi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner. His father’s former wife, née Tian, was posthumously granted the title of Respectful Lady; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the same title. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Sanzheng, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; Han, an Assistant Prefect; Tan; and Kerang. His younger brothers were Yu, a tribute student [?—the annotation is unclear], Xu 䎉, Yi 翊, Ben 翉, Xu 詡, and Xuan 翧. His wife was née Xiao. He placed fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李寅賓〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字于暘，行二，年三十三，六月二十日生〕。曾祖永昌，祖思川，父德全，母汪氏。永感下。兄用賓，弟三賓、彥賓〔儒士〕、禮賓、應賓、太賓、尚賓、朝賓。娶程氏。應天府鄉試第三十名，會試第一百五十一名。

周詠〔貫河南開封府延津縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字思養，行四，年三十，四月二十日生〕。曾祖鑑〔壽官〕，祖鹗〔典膳〕，父宜〔典膳〕，前母楊氏，母韓氏。慈侍下。兄讓〔監生〕、訥，弟讜、諗、詵、調、詡、護、託、試。娶李氏。河南鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百八十四名。

王宗載〔貫湖廣承天府京山縣，軍籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字時厚，行三，年二十七，十月十三日生〕。曾祖希旦〔按察司僉事〕，祖大有〔都司都事〕，父宋，母聶氏。慈侍下。兄宗可、宗望，弟宗衡。娶劉氏，繼娶鍾氏。湖廣鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百三十三名。

陳三綱〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，杭州府錢塘縣人，縣學附學生，治禮記，字振道，行三，年三十，三月十四日生〕。曾祖嗣先，祖廷言，父琪，嫡母龔氏，生母程氏。慈侍下。兄一經〔典史〕、二綬，弟四維、五箴、六紀。娶戴氏。浙江鄉試第五十七名，會試第二百七十三名。
translation_en:
Li Yinbin was registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuyang; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang; his grandfather, Sichuan; his father, Dequan; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yongbin; his younger brothers were Sanbin, Yanbin (a Confucian scholar), Libin, Yingbin, Taibin, Shangbin, and Chaobin. His wife was née Cheng. He ranked thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yong was registered in Yanjin County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Siyang; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twentieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jian (an honorary official in recognition of longevity); his grandfather, E (Director of Food Service); and his father, Yi (Director of Food Service). His father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Han. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Rang (a student of the Directorate of Education) and Ne; his younger brothers were Dang, Shen, Shen, Diao, Xu, Hu, Tuo, and Shi. His wife was née Li. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongzai was registered in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. An added-quota student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shihou; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xidan (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner); his grandfather, Dayou (Office Manager in a Regional Military Commission); his father, Song; and his mother, née Nie. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zongke and Zongwang; his younger brother was Zongheng. His wife was née Liu; his subsequent wife was née Zhong. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Sangang was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, and was a native of Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhendao; he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Sixian; his grandfather, Tingyan; and his father, Qi. His legal mother was née Gong, and his birth mother was née Cheng. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Yijing (a county Chief Clerk) and Ershou; his younger brothers were Siwei, Wuzhen, and Liuji. His wife was née Dai. He ranked fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Shijie, courtesy name Yixue, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jieyou; his grandfather, Boyang; his father, Tingshan; and his mother, née Xiao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shizhu, Shilong, Shibi, Shiji, Shizhi, Shigao, and Shixie. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Rumei, courtesy name Dehe, was registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, Commissioner of a Transport Office; his grandfather, Tianzhang; his father, Tinggui, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother, née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Rushu, Ruji, and Rulin. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Nan, courtesy name Zilin, was registered in a civilian household in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Shu; his father, Yong; and his mother, née Hu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Wu and Jia. He married a woman née Dai. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Wenming, courtesy name Zhongmo, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weichang; his grandfather, Yongzhong, a County Registrar; his father, Rurui, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his mother, née Xiong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Wenwei and Qi, the latter a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Bao, Ao, Pan, Gui, Xun, Wenmei, Wenxie, Wenyu, and Wenjiong. He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Pan 劉泮, courtesy name Ruhua, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and was a native of Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziduan; his grandfather, Ren; his father, Wenxin; his mother, née Wang; and his stepmother, née Xiao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han and Bin, and his younger brothers were Pu and Guan. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiayan 王嘉言, courtesy name Junmo, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and was a native of Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shi, and grandfather, Hu, held prestige titles; his father, Lu, was a subprefectural vice magistrate; and his mother was née Sun. His father was living, and his mother had died. His elder brothers were Lian and Jiamou, and his younger male cousins in the paternal line were Jiashan, Sanchong, and Sance. He married a woman née Gong and subsequently a woman née Fan. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuanxiang 王原相, courtesy name Shaozhi, was registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yao; his grandfather, Chuan, was a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; and his father, Jiankui, was a secretary in the Ministry of Justice. His legal mother, née He, had been granted the title Lady of Peace (anren), and his birth mother was née Zheng. His father had died, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Yuange, and his younger brothers were Yuanxiao, Yuanxi, Yuanmo, and Yuanpu. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rui 趙睿, courtesy name Ruosi, was registered in a civilian household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengyuan; his grandfather, Huan, was an assistant prefect; his father was Qi; and his mother was née Wang. His father had died, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Fu, Du, Yu, Lin, and Ying. He married a woman née Shen. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Zhida, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruwei, and he ranked fourth among his brothers. He was twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong was a department magistrate, posthumously granted the title of vice director in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather Ying was a ceremonial usher; his father was Tongwen, and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhiyuan, and his wife was née Dan [?]. He placed 116th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Gong, registered in Tongxiang County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shiyong, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Da held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Tai, and his mother was née Shen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother Guan was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his younger brother was Lai. His wife was née Tang. He placed 79th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Yuguo, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhongfu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menglin; his grandfather was Jingchang; his father was Huang; his mother was née Yan, and his stepmother was née Wu. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yumin and Yudao. His wife was née Yang; he subsequently married women née Lin and née Shen. He placed 82nd in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ai Kejiu, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Dezheng, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Qin was a student of yin-yang studies; his grandfather Hong was a judge in a Regional Military Commission; his father was Yuanmei, and his mother was née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Kequan, and his wife was née Yang. He placed 24th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王以纁〔貫順天府霸州文安縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字伯聘，行六，年二十七，三月初五日生〕。曾祖能〔縣主簿〕，祖詔〔縣主簿〕，父楫，母温氏。具慶下，兄以緒〔倉副使〕、維、經〔監生〕、紳〔監生〕、繒〔監生〕、纘〔守備〕、訓、綵、織、絡、繕、統，弟緘、練、綡、縕，娶段氏。順天府鄉試第三十六名，會試第二百九十名。

蔚元康〔貫河南宣武衛軍籍，山西孝義縣人，祥符縣學附學生，治春秋，字良甫，行一，年三十五，十二月初八日生〕。曾祖仲祥，祖寛，父海，前母郭氏，母張氏。慈侍下，娶吳氏。河南鄉試第十七名，會試第一百七十四名。
translation_en:
Lin Zi, registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rucai, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xiu (holder of an honorary longevity title), his grandfather was Luan, his father was Qi, and his mother was née Zhang; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mao (an Imperial University student), Si, Nian (an Imperial University student), Lü, and Shu, and his younger brothers were Xi, Yang, and Yu; his wife was née Li. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ze, registered in a military household of Yanshan Front Guard and originally from Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was an additional student of the Shuntian prefectural school who specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ziren, he ranked second in his family, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather was Jin, his father was Yong, and his mother was née Li; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Run; he married a woman née Su and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yixun, registered in a civilian household in Wen’an County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a county school student who specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bopin, he ranked sixth in his family, and he was twenty-seven years old, born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Neng (a county Registrar), his grandfather was Zhao (a county Registrar), his father was Ji, and his mother was née Wen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yixu (a granary Vice Commissioner), Wei, Jing (an Imperial University student), Shen (an Imperial University student), Zeng (an Imperial University student), Zuan (a Commandant), Xun, Cai, Zhi, Luo, Shan, and Tong, and his younger brothers were Jian, Lian, Liang, and Yun; his wife was née Duan. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Yuankang, registered in a military household of Xuanwu Guard in Henan and originally from Xiaoyi County, Shanxi, was an additional student of the Xiangfu county school who specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Liangfu, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxiang, his grandfather was Kuan, his father was Hai, his father’s former wife was née Guo, and his mother was née Zhang; his father was deceased and his mother was living. His wife was née Wu. He placed seventeenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉寅〔貫直隸保定府博野縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字宗夏，行三，年三十三，十月初十日生〕。曾祖政，祖春，父文強，母馬氏。具慶下，兄孟、仲，弟卯、午，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第□□名，會試第二百四十三名。

translation_en:
Cao Dangmian 曹當勉, courtesy name Kexian, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hong 鋐, an Assistant Prefect; his grandfather was Ang; his father was Qian; and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Dangxing, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked sixty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shiju 王時舉, courtesy name Jinqing, was registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather was Ji; his father was Yi; his mother was née Li; and his stepmothers were née Zhang and née Cen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiyong and Shizhong. His wife was née He; his subsequent wives were also née He and née Dong. He ranked 104th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yin 劉寅, courtesy name Zongxia, was registered in a civilian household in Boye County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Wenqiang; and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Meng and Zhong, and his younger brothers were Mao and Wu. His wife was née Wang. His rank in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination is illegible (□□); he ranked 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo □□ 羅□□, whose given name is illegible, had the courtesy name Zixu and was a native of Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather was Chaogang; his father was Bi, who held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother was née Nie. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Pengxiao, a Registrar of a Guard, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ren Weitang, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyang; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Qing; his father, Mian, a prefectural assistant; and his mother, née Li. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Weijun, an assistant surveillance commissioner; his younger brothers were Weijian, Weiyue, and Weixuan. He married a woman née Jian. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Nayan, registered in a military household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather, Shu; his father, Dong, a county registrar; and his mother, née Tang. Both parents were still living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengxu, registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boyu; he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing’e, granted the honorary title of vice director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather, Rui; his father, Wei; and his mother, née Zhu. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Chengxun, Chengfang, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Chengye, Chengyi, and Chengzhong, a Secretariat drafter; his younger brothers were Chengdu, Chengchong, Chenglie, and Chengyong, a student of the Imperial University. He married a woman née Long. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Shixuan was registered with the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yiren, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-three years old, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under provisions of imperial grace; his grandfather, Yue; his father, Luan, a prefectural school instructor; and his mother, née Mao. Both parents were still living. His elder brother was Shijin; his younger brothers were Shipin, Shitong, Shida, and Yinglin. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née He. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

慈侍下　兄諤〔壽官〕訒讃　弟謙謹詰　娶郭氏
山西鄉試第四十六名　會試第二百五十六名
===
祝尚義貫騰驤左衛軍籍直隸淮安衛人　國子生
治詩經字質甫行二年三十三四月二十五日生
曾祖瓛　祖英〔訓導〕　父舜卿　母王氏
慈侍下　兄祿尚禮弟尚忠尚質尚文尚信尚行尚德娶劉氏
順天府鄉試第一名　會試第二百八十二名
柴宗義貫山西平陽府解州安邑縣民籍　縣學生
治詩經字子集行一年三十二月初三日生
曾祖肇祀　祖順　父梅　前母賈氏　母賈氏
具慶下　弟宗禮　宗信　娶李氏
山西鄉試第十五名　會試第二百二十七名
punctuated:
皮汝謙〔貫雲南蒙化衛軍籍，直隸廬州府英山縣人，河南羅山縣學教諭，治春秋，字子揚，行四，年三十五，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖守忠，祖成，父清，前母陳氏，母周氏。慈侍下，兄弁、冕、汝懋，弟汝修，娶宗氏，繼娶趙氏。雲南鄉試第三十三名，會試第二百五十二名。

丁誠〔貫山西平陽府安邑縣民籍，河東運司學生，治易經，字子成，行二，年三十，正月十二日生〕。曾祖安，祖彥方，父良弼，母趙氏。慈侍下，兄諤〔壽官〕、訒、讚，弟謙、謹、誥，娶郭氏。山西鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百五十六名。

祝尚義〔貫騰驤左衛軍籍，直隸淮安衛人，國子生，治詩經，字質甫，行二，年三十三，四月二十五日生〕。曾祖瓛，祖英〔訓導〕，父舜卿，母王氏。慈侍下，兄祿、尚禮，弟尚忠、尚質、尚文、尚信、尚行、尚德，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第一名，會試第二百八十二名。

柴宗義〔貫山西平陽府解州安邑縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子集，行一，年三十，二月初三日生〕。曾祖肇祀，祖順，父梅，前母賈氏，母賈氏。具慶下，弟宗禮、宗信，娶李氏。山西鄉試第十五名，會試第一百二十七名。
translation_en:
Pi Ruqian, courtesy name Ziyang, was registered in a military household of Menghua Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Yingshan County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was Instructor at the county school of Luoshan, Henan, and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Fourth in family order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouzhong; his grandfather, Cheng; and his father, Qing. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Bian, Mian, and Rumao, and his younger brother was Ruxiu. He married a woman née Zong and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-third in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Cheng, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Anyi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a student at the school of the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission and specialized in the Book of Changes. Second in family order, he was thirty years old and was born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather, Yanfang; his father, Liangbi; and his mother, née Zhao. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were E, who held an honorary rank for longevity, Ren, and Zan; his younger brothers were Qian, Jin, and Gao. He married a woman née Guo. He placed forty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shangyi, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a military household of Tengxiang Left Guard and was a native of Huai'an Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. Second in family order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather, Ying, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Shunqing; and his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Lu and Shangli; his younger brothers were Shangzhong, Shangzhi, Shangwen, Shangxin, Shangxing, and Shangde. He married a woman née Liu. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chai Zongyi, courtesy name Ziji, was registered in a civilian household in Anyi County, Jiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a county school student and specialized in the Book of Odes. First in family order, he was thirty years old and was born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhaosi; his grandfather, Shun; and his father, Mei. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Jia. Both his parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongli and Zongxin. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
郜永春〔貫直隸大名府長垣縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字子元，行二，年三十，正月二十一日生〕。曾祖果，祖信，父壬，母邵氏。慈侍下，兄永年，娶苗氏。順天府鄉試第九十六名，會試第一百七十八名。

蹇達〔貫四川重慶衛，官籍，重慶府學生，治書經，字汝上，行二，年二十一，八月十七日生〕。曾祖洪，祖廷相〔贈兵部主事〕，父來譽〔按察司僉事〕，母王氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄逵，弟遷、遵、迒，娶許氏。四川鄉試第八名，會試第二百六十三名。

段繡〔貫山西蒲州守禦千戶所，軍籍，臨汾縣人，州學附學生，治易經，字弘憲，行六，年二十八，四月十六日生〕。曾祖清，祖銘〔義官〕，父子素，母盧氏。慈侍下，兄紹、繼、統、綱、紳，弟綸、繹、紡、綵，娶楊氏，繼娶張氏。山西鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百五十三名。

劉田〔貫河南南陽衛，官籍，國子生，治易經，字仲龍，行一，年四十四，八月初三日生〕。曾祖翰〔指揮使〕，祖哲，父繼先，母高氏。慈侍下，娶楊氏。河南鄉試第四十一名，會試第一百十三名。
translation_en:
Gao Yongchun 郜永春, registered in Changyuan County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyuan, he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guo, his grandfather Xin, his father Ren, and his mother née Shao; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brother was Yongnian, and his wife was née Miao. He placed ninety-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jian Da 蹇達, registered in Chongqing Guard, Sichuan, in an official household, was a Chongqing prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Rushang, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-one, and born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather Tingxiang was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of War; his father Laiyu was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Kui, his younger brothers Qian, Zun, and Hang, and his wife was née Xu. He placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Xiu 段繡, registered in the Puzhou Defense Battalion, Shanxi, in a military household and originally from Linfen County, was an attached student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Hongxian, he was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Ming held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness, his father was Zisu, and his mother was née Lu. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Shao, Ji, Tong, Gang, and Shen, and his younger brothers Lun, Yi, Fang, and Cai; he married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tian 劉田, registered in Nanyang Guard, Henan, in an official household, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhonglong, he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Han was a Commander, his grandfather was Zhe, his father Jixian, and his mother née Gao; his father was deceased and his mother living, and his wife was née Yang. He placed forty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

具慶下　兄齊〔醫官〕　弟壽箕符虎隨夏芴弟發晉晨鼎廷箴簽萬昱紘籍䕫英聞錫爵　娶袁氏
湖廣鄉試第八十四名　會試第五十二名
===
黃學海貫廣西左衛官籍直隸常州府無錫縣人　衛學生
治春秋字宗于行三年二十八七月十七日生
曾祖萱　祖坤〔贈監察御史〕　父正色〔前監察御史〕　母蕭氏〔封孺人〕繼母薛氏
嚴侍下　兄學孝學道學孟學顏學詩學易　弟學禮學憲學初學古學書學顏學舜學堯

郭夢得貫福建泉州府同安縣鹽籍　縣學附學生
治詩經字南卿行一年二十七十一月初十日生
曾祖尚正〔壽官〕　祖世仰　父榜　前母葉氏　母吳氏
具慶下　兄仁春　娶劉氏
□鄉試第八十三名　會試第九十一名
punctuated:
侯思古〔貫浙江台州府臨海縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字士睿，行一，年四十三，三月二十日生〕。曾祖鐸，祖鰲〔訓導〕，父璧〔監生〕，母戴氏。慈侍下，弟師古、好古、宗古、恩古、光古。娶沈氏，繼娶劉氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第一百四十二名。

王篆〔貫湖廣荆州府夷陵州民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝文，行十五，年三十一，六月十五日生〕。曾祖傑〔府同知〕，祖燧〔左長史，進階通議大夫〕，父良策，嫡母張氏，生母玉氏。具慶下，兄篇〔監生〕、簿、籌、笙、符、篪、簡、策、笏，弟笑、管、簽、筵、筀、籍、箕、範、箴、筍。娶良氏。湖廣鄉試第八十四名，會試第五十二名。

黃學海〔貫廣寧左屯衛軍籍，直隸常州府無錫縣人，衛學生，治春秋，字宗于，行三，年二十八，七月十七日生〕。曾祖萱，祖坤〔贈監察御史〕，父正色〔前監察御史〕，母蕭氏〔封孺人〕，繼母薛氏。嚴侍下，兄學充、學道、學文〔貢士〕、學詩、學易、學禮、學憲、學初、學古、學書、學顏。娶余氏。順天府鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百十四名。

郭夢得〔貫福建泉州府同安縣鹽籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字甫卿，行二，年二十七，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖尚正〔壽官〕，祖世仰，父榜，前母葉氏，母吳氏。具慶下，兄仁春。娶劉氏。福建鄉試第八十三名，會試第九十一名。
translation_en:
Hou Sigu, registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shirui; he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-three, born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather, Ao, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Bi, was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Dai. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Shigu, Haogu, Zonggu, Engu, and Guanggu. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhuan, registered in a civilian household in Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruwen; he ranked fifteenth in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Jie, was a Prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather, Sui, was Left Chief Secretary, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Thorough Counsel. His father was Liangce; his father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Pian, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Bu, Chou, Sheng, Fu, Chi, Jian, Ce, and Hu; his younger brothers were Xiao, Guan, Qian, Yan, Gui, Ji, Ji, Fan, Zhen, and Sun. He married a woman née Liang. He placed eighty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xuehai was registered in a military household of the Guangning Left Garrison Guard and was a native of Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the guard school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zongyu; he ranked third in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Kun, was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Zhengse, was a former Investigating Censor. His mother, née Xiao, was granted the title of Lady; his stepmother was née Xue. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Xuechong, Xuedao, Xuewen, a tribute scholar, and Xueshi, Xueyi, Xueli, Xuexian, Xuechu, Xuegu, Xueshu, and Xueyan. He married a woman née Yu. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Mengde, registered in a salt-producing household in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Fuqing; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Shangzheng, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Shiyang, and his father was Bang. His father's former wife was née Ye, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Renchun. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eighty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
