喬應春〔貫武驤左衛勇士籍，河南彰德府安陽縣人，順天府學生，治詩經，字仁卿，行一，年二十七，八月十三日生〕。曾祖顯，祖琮，父文〔知州〕，前母徐氏，母沈氏。具慶下，弟應時、應節、應光，娶郭氏。順天府鄉試第五十一名，會試第一百八十一名。
translation_en:
Hu Jia 胡價, registered in a military household in Yicheng County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shizhong; he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Qi, an honorary official for philanthropy; his father was Zhenpei, a Guard Registrar; and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wei, Jie 价, and Zhuo, and his wife was née Gong. He placed fourteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Wenlong 史文龍, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yinglin; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather was Lun, his father was Shangcheng, and his mother was née Jiang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Wenfeng, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Tianfu 莫天賦, registered in a military household in Haikang County, Leizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuliang, his grandfather was 𠇗 [?], his father was Ao, and his mother was née Tang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Tianxi and Tianmin, and his younger brother was Tianran. His wife was née Chen; he subsequently married another woman née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Yingchun 喬應春 was registered as a warrior in the Wuxiang Left Guard and was a native of Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. He was a student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Renqing; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather was Cong, and his father was Wen, a Department Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingshi, Yingjie, and Yingguang, and his wife was née Guo. He placed fifty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

王學古，貫陝西西安府同州朝邑縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字子獲，行一，年三十六，四月初五日生。曾祖文美，祖燮〔府照磨〕，父來召，母梁氏。重慶下，兄學詩〔貢士〕，弟學孟、學謨〔俱省祭官〕、學閔、學䦐、學闡、學闢、學洛、學淵。娶李氏。陝西鄉試第六十名，會試第六十八名。

張璇，貫浙江昌國衛官籍，寧波府象山縣人，縣學生，治易經，字伯祥，行一，年二十八，十一月初三日生。曾祖壽〔百戶〕，祖澤〔百戶〕，父模〔百戶〕，母王氏。具慶下，弟璘。娶湯氏。浙江鄉試第六十八名，會試第一百十一名。

李復聘，貫陝西西安府盩厔縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字守珍，行四，年二十八，正月初三日生。曾祖方，祖璣，父備，母楊氏，繼母田氏。永感下，兄深、淵、來聘、渾，弟炳然、煥然、復初。娶劉氏。陝西鄉試第九名，會試第一百三十六名。

李橡，貫江西南昌府豐城縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字孟栗，行三，年三十四，二月十五日生。曾祖與鎬，祖萬平〔封刑部郎中〕，父選〔監生〕，母鄧氏。永感下，兄槓〔惠州府推官〕、格〔監生〕、樟〔合州判官〕、杭〔監生〕、悳〔監生〕，弟栻〔貢士〕、材〔同科進士〕、楠〔監生〕、柲、樞〔俱庠生〕、榛。娶熊氏。應天府鄉試第五十三名，會試第一百八十九名。
translation_en:
Wang Xuegu 王學古 was registered in an artisan household in Chaoyi County, Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zihuo, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-six sui old, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenmei; his grandfather was Xie, a prefectural Records Examiner; his father was Laizhao; and his mother was née Liang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Xueshi, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His younger brothers were Xuemeng and Xuemo, both provincial sacrificial officials [?], and Xuemin, Xueting 學䦐 [?], Xuechan, Xuepi, Xueluo, and Xueyuan. His wife was née Li. He placed sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xuan 張璇 was registered in an officer household of Changguo Guard, Zhejiang, and was a native of Xiangshan County, Ningbo Prefecture. He was a county school student and specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Boxiang, and he ranked first in birth order. He was twenty-eight sui old, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Shou, grandfather Ze, and father Mo were all Company Commanders; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lin. His wife was née Tang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Fupin 李復聘 was registered in a civilian household in Zhouzhi County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shouzhen, and he ranked fourth in birth order. He was twenty-eight sui old, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang; his grandfather was Ji; his father was Bei; his mother was née Yang; and his stepmother was née Tian. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shen, Yuan, Laipin, and Hun; his younger brothers were Bingran, Huanran, and Fuchu. His wife was née Liu. He placed ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xiang 李橡 was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Mengli, and he ranked third in birth order. He was thirty-four sui old, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yugao; his grandfather was Wanping, granted the honorary title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Xuan, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Deng. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gang, a Judge of Huizhou Prefecture; Ge, a student of the Directorate of Education; Zhang, an Assistant Prefect of Hezhou; and Hang and De, both students of the Directorate of Education. His younger brothers were Shi, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Cai, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort; Nan, a student of the Directorate of Education; Bi and Shu, both government school students; and Zhen. His wife was née Xiong. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳應春〔貫福建福州府長樂縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字有暉，行三，年二十八，二月二十六日生〕。曾祖德基，祖銓，父夢達，母卓氏，繼母劉氏。具慶下，兄應秋，弟應夏、應試、應兆，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第六十五名，會試第一百二十名。
translation_en:
Zong Hongxian, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jinfu. Second in family order, he was thirty years old and was born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue; his grandfather, Ren, was an Office Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father, Mu, was an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Hongzao, Hongyuan, Hongshu, Hongxuan, and Hongdi; his younger brothers were Hongqian and Hongxun. He married a woman née Xu. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Shangyi, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziren. Second in family order, he was thirty years old and was born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hu; his grandfather was Zhiren; and his father was Ruxian. His father's former wife was née Wang, his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmothers were née Wu and née Ju [?]. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chong, and his younger brother was Shangzhou. He married a woman née Mei. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hua Qizhi, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Licheng. Third in family order, he was thirty years old and was born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Kai, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, En, was posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Shunqin, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Qian, was invested with the title Lady of Repose. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qizhong, and his younger brother was Qiduan. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yingchun, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Youhui. Third in family order, he was twenty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deji; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Mengda; his mother was née Zhuo; and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingqiu; his younger brothers were Yingxia, Yingshi, and Yingzhao. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

任春元〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治春秋，字長卿，行一，年三十二，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖澤，祖佐，父正，母潘氏。慈侍下，弟春和，娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第二十二名，會試第二十五名。

鄭欽〔貫直隸寧國府涇縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字堯卿，行一，年二十九，八月十七日生〕。曾祖途，祖昌，父玨，母汪氏。具慶下，弟釴、銳、鑛、銘、鐺、鉞、鎮、鑒，娶洪氏。應天府鄉試第一百十七名，會試第一百四十名。
translation_en:
Xi Shangzhen, courtesy name Daipin, was from Nanzheng County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, and registered in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Menghua; his father, He; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Bai and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Dengying, courtesy name Zideng, was from Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, and registered in an artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was tenth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongsheng, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather, Chongde, an honorary official for charitable service; his father, Ming, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Ji. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Cang and Zi. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Gong. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Chunyuan, courtesy name Changqing, was from Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. An additional student of the county government school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ze; his grandfather, Zuo; his father, Zheng; and his mother, née Pan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Chunhe. He married a woman née Huang. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Qin, courtesy name Yaoqing, was from Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tu; his grandfather, Chang; his father, Jue; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yi, Rui, Kuang, Ming, Dang, Yue, Zhen, and Jian. He married a woman née Hong. He placed one hundred seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Congxian, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an supplementary student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Weishi. He ranked third in family seniority, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Dao, his grandfather Jian, and his father Xiyuan; his mother was née Lin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Congyin, and his younger brothers were Congde and Congkuan. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Pengqiu, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Daoyuan. He ranked fourth in family seniority, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Xian was posthumously appointed Registrar of a Guard; his grandfather Hui was Registrar of a Guard and was posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Works. His father Gun was a Prefect, advanced to the prestige rank of Yazhong dafu. His father's principal wife, née Zheng, received the title Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Penglai, Registrar of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Penghan; Pengliang; and Pengxin, a medical official. His younger brother Pengcai was a Battalion Commander. He married a woman née Che and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xie, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dali. He ranked thirty-first in family seniority, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yue, his grandfather Jin, and his father Geng; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wei and Yi, and his younger brother was Jiang. He married a woman née Xu. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Guoqian, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a supplementary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Erguang. He ranked second in family seniority, was aged thirty, and was born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Maocheng, his grandfather Ying, and his father Zhongxian; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guoheng and Guoqian (國乾), and his younger brothers were Guoyi and Guolü. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

龍光〔貫湖廣長沙衛，軍籍，長沙府學增廣生，治詩經，字國華，行一，年三十四，二月初一日生〕。曾祖霄，祖世聰，父添鑾，母易氏。慈侍下，弟見，娶湯氏。湖廣鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百四十九名。

translation_en:
Zhou Shixuan, registered in a civilian household in Gucheng County, Jingzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region (Zhili), was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenxian; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-one years old, and was born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jia, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Liangzuo; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Xia. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Shimao, and his wife was née Huang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qi, registered in a military household in Xiajin County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zideng; he ranked third among his brothers, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Zhang, and his father Jie; his mother was née Xiao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Jiao and She, and his younger brothers were Zhi and 𥚻 [reading uncertain]; his wife was née Gao. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Guang, registered in a military household of Changsha Guard, Huguang, was an additional student of the Changsha prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guohua; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiao, his grandfather Shicong, and his father Tianluan; his mother was née Yi. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Jian, and his wife was née Tang. He placed seventy-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Shouyue, registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chongyao; he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hu, his grandfather Dayong, and his father Wengong; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shouchen, a prestige official, and Shouzeng; his younger brother was Shoumeng, and his wife was née Niu. He placed forty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Shiqiu, registered in an officer household of Pengcheng Guard and a native of Baodi County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yifu; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Zhong, grandfather Feng, and father Chengzong were all Assistant Commanders; his mother, née Wang, was invested with the title Lady of Respect, and his stepmother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shichun, an Assistant Commander, and Shixia; his wife was née Ni. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Guanghu, registered in a military household in Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongdu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Yue, and his father Zhenzong, a student of the Directorate of Education; his legal mother was née Yao, and his birth mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guangzuo, Guangzhen, Guangxiang, and Guangzhi; his wife was née Li. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Biao, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yisheng; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was De, his father Run, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Liang, and his wife was née Li. He placed twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Mo, registered in a civilian household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zijia; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Mengchun, his grandfather Ke, his father Zhongzai, and his mother née Chai. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Jian, and his wife was née Hu. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Kerong, courtesy name Rucong, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan, and was originally from Fengcheng County, Chang Prefecture [?], Jiangxi. An additional student at the department school, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was third in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yicheng; his grandfather, Cong, was a District Magistrate; his father was Yuanzhong; his mother was née Pang, and his stepmothers were née Wang and née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kejian and Kequan. He married a woman née Qiao and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Song. He placed sixty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Cai, courtesy name Jifu, was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student at the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was ninth in family order, aged twenty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather, Xie, held an honorary title conferred for longevity; his father was Qi, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Zao, Mai (an official), Kui, Feng, Shang, and Dao; his younger brothers were Shu, Zheng, and Yu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Chengzu, courtesy name Keshao, was registered in a military household of the Chengdu Left Escort Guard, Sichuan. A student at the Chengdu prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he was second in family order, aged thirty, and born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dachang; his grandfather was Song; his father was Yue, and his mother was née Jin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chengye, and his younger brother was Chengsi. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently married another woman née Wang. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Guoyan, courtesy name Xizai, was registered in a military household in Handan County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he was fourth in family order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan; his grandfather was Teng; his father, Xiu, held an honorary title conferred for longevity. His father’s former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guoyan (a titular official), Guochen, and Guoshi. He married a woman née Wei. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhai Xiuchang, registered in a military household in Wenxi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Ruzhong, he ranked first in birth order, and he was twenty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Chong, and his father Hua; his mother was née Ma and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was still living. His elder brother was Jiao, and his wife was née Li. He placed eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Sijin, registered in a civilian household in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuren, he ranked third in birth order, and he was twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fuzu; his grandfather Bangkan was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father Zan was a Prefect; and his mother, née Qiu, held the conferred title Woman of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sike and Sitong, and his younger brothers were Sishu, an Imperial University student, and Sirang. His wife was née Hong. He placed thirty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wenmo, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xianqing, he ranked third in birth order, and he was thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Fang was a County Vice Magistrate, his grandfather Yu was a Postal Station Master, his father was Gui, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenyu, a Prefect; Jing, Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals; Wenyan; Maoyi, an Administration Vice Commissioner; and Wenyi. His younger brothers were Wenyue and Maoli, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His wife was née Sun. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Jiyuan, registered in a civilian household in Tongxiang County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Renqing, he ranked first in birth order, and he was thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ding, his grandfather Yun was a County Vice Magistrate, and his father De was an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Zhao and his stepmother née Shi. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Jiheng and Jihe, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cheng Wenzhu, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Meizhong, and he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sisheng, his grandfather Zhenqi, his father Tingji, and his mother Lady Wang 汪. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenzhang and Wenyuan, and his younger brothers Wenzhen and Wenyun. He married Lady Wang 汪. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xiwen, registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zongzhou, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingfu, his grandfather Zhen, his father Yaoqing, and his mother Lady Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiwu. He married Lady Sha. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shangxian, registered in Yongqing County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Junjin, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Jing, his father Bo, and his mother Lady He. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shangdeng, Shangke, and Shangxue. He married Lady Yuan. He placed 117th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kejiu, registered in Yangcheng County, Zezhou Subprefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhide, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, an honorary official in recognition of longevity; his grandfather was Sizhong, posthumously granted the title of Magistrate; his father was Zhi, Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Right; and his mother was Lady Liang, granted the title of Lady for Service (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Keda and Kejiao. He married Lady Wang 王. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xiao Daheng, courtesy name Xiaqing, was registered in a civilian household in Tai’an Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and was a native of Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xujing, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Qian; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Hai and Dayuan. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shugao, courtesy name Yangde, was registered in a salt-producing household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather Zheng was honorarily appointed Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission. His father Che was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of a Provincial Administration Commission and was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Court Discussion. His mother, née Pan, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Pure Virtue; his stepmother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shumao, an Office Assistant in the Court of State Ceremonial, and Shuguo, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of a Provincial Administration Commission. His younger brother Shuben was a student admitted by imperial grace. He married a woman née Lü and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chengfang, courtesy name Keji, was registered in a military household in Ningqiang Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Liquan County, Xi’an Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Hong, and his father Yi; his mother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Weibin. His wife was née Yan. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qing, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in a military household in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An additional-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather Shen was a Battalion Commander; and his father Xiao was a County Registrar. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, an Imperial University student, and Qian, a tribute scholar. His wife was née Liu. He placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lei Dazhuang, courtesy name Qinlü, was registered in a civilian household in Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Tai, Director of a School of Yin-Yang Studies; his father was Ping; and his mother was née Tian. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Dayou, Daxu, and Daqian, and his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Chongdao, courtesy name Weizheng, was registered in a civilian household in Fei County, Yizhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked ninth in birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyou, posthumously appointed a Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Qi, a Guard Registrar; and his father was Shen, a Department Magistrate. His legal mother was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Yan. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Chongru, Chongxin, Chonggui, Chongxue (an Imperial University student), Chongli, and Chongyue (a tribute student); his younger brothers were Chongwen (an Imperial University student) and Chongwu. His wife was née Dong. He placed forty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhen, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in a military household of the Tengxiang Left Guard and was a native of Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student at the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Xi; his father was Sicheng; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Duo, Qin, and Lan, and his younger brother was Qian. His wife was née Wang. He placed 112th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xuesi, courtesy name Kedao, was registered in a civilian household in Yizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was You, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Mu; his father was Guan, a Professor; and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Xueyan and Xuezeng, and his younger brother was Xuemeng. His wife was née Zhao. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Daisong, registered in a military household of Qinzhou Guard, Shaanxi, was a native of Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, and a student of the Qinzhou school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingyue, and he ranked first in family order. He was thirty-three years old, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hua, his grandfather Gao, his father Shixiang, and his mother Lady Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Cen, and he married Lady Zheng. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhiyuan, registered in an artisan household of Xincheng County, Ji’nan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ershi, and he ranked second in family order. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu; his grandfather Lin was a Confucian School Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father Chongguang was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother, Lady Liu, held the conferred title of Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Zhihan was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Zhigan, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi), Zhicheng, Zhiyou, and Zhidong. He married Lady Yu. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zishi, registered in a civilian household of Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongfu, and he ranked first in family order. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jian was a Department Judge; his grandfather was Wei, his father Shili, and his mother Lady Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zicheng, and his younger brothers were Ziming and Zitong. He married Lady Li. He placed 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Zhenyuan, registered in a military household of Yingshan County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chunfu, and he ranked fifth in family order. He was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Banghou, his father Lin, and his mother Lady Dai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengyuan, Cuiyuan, Zhaoyuan, and Bingyuan; his younger brothers were Shiyuan and Minyuan. He married Lady Pei. He placed ninetieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Xidan, registered in a civilian household in Jingde County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was an auxiliary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rulu, he ranked first in family order, and he was thirty years old, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boliang, his grandfather Zhide, his father Shilu, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Xiwang, Xizhao, Xigao, and Xikui, his wife was née Guo, and he placed 132nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 99th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Jianchen, registered in a military household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zizhong, he ranked first in family order, and he was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Xuan, his father Tang, and his mother née Xi; both parents were living, his elder brother was Zechen and his younger brothers Fuchen and Shichen, his wife was née Xu, and he placed 42nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 37th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jisi, registered in a military household in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an auxiliary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Mingqing, he ranked second in family order, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongben, his grandfather Damu, his father Mei, and his mother née He; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brother was Bangsi and his younger brothers Longsi, Zhisi, Zusi, and Shensi, his wife was née Huang, and he placed sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Teng Bolun, registered in a military household in Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruzai, he ranked fifth in family order, and he was thirty-four years old, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Shu (a department vice magistrate), his father Heling (an assistant prefect), and his mother née Chen; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Botang, his wife was née Yang, and he placed 59th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Minmo, courtesy name Zixiao, was registered in a military household in Xiangyang County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked second in birth order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Wenxue; his father, Hong, a school instructor; and his mother, née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Minji, and his younger brothers were Mindong, Minge, and Minzhen. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed thirty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shan Ne, courtesy name Xiren, was registered in a military household in Zaoqiang County, Jizhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second in birth order, and was aged forty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, an honorary official distinguished for longevity; his grandfather, Fu; and his father, Tong, a prefectural examiner. His father's former wife was née Zheng, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Wen. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Wei. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yujie, courtesy name Yunsheng, was registered in a military household of Dongsheng Right Guard and came from Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked second in birth order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Li; and his father, Cong, a student of the Directorate of Education. His father's former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née Guo. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Yuting, and his younger brother was Yubi, a ceremonial official in a princely establishment. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Jike, courtesy name Yili, was registered in an official household of Lulong Guard, Zhili, and came from Xiangtan County, Huguang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked second in birth order, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Jie, a county registrar; his father, Zitai, a subprefectural clerk; and his mother, née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xingke, a student of the Directorate of Education; Xianke, a Metropolitan Examination graduate awaiting the Palace Examination; and Shangke, an official of yin-yang studies. His younger brothers were Jinke, Shike, Jianzai, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Jianneng. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed eighty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Guozhen, of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Junzhi. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xuanchuan; his grandfather, Anqi, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Cheng. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jun, an Assistant Administration Commissioner; Yongbin, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Cai, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His younger brothers were Guoxiang, Guoyu, Guozuo, and Guoxi. His wife was née Wang. He placed forty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xian, of Laiyang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Xiyuan. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xiong; his grandfather was Yan; his father was Dazuo; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Chong; his younger brothers were Bao and Rong, the latter an official awaiting selection for appointment. His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yushan, of Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bocong. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Gang, was Director-General of Grain Transport and Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather, Guan, was a Records Keeper in a Provincial Surveillance Commission. His father was Xiaoxian, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yuli, Yuquan, Yuyan, Yuxue, Yuzhi, You, and Yuxian. His wife was née Yang; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Biao, of Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zichen. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather was Shiyong; his father was Yingkui; and his mother was née He. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shi, Ci, and Jiao. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王廷簡〔貫四川邛州，民籍，州學生，治詩經，字汝迪，行一，年三十二，五月初十日生〕。曾祖大端，祖禮〔冠帶壽官〕，父聘〔監生〕，嫡母李氏，繼母劉氏、彭氏，生母李氏。慈侍下，弟廷符、廷節、廷筳。娶徐氏，繼娶姚氏、余氏。四川鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百十二名。

陳大壯〔貫直隸揚州府通州，民籍，州學生，治詩經，字思立，行二，年二十八，二月二十九日生〕。曾祖純德，祖尚忠〔贈工部主事〕，父冠〔七品散官〕，母王氏。重慶下，兄大震，弟大科〔貢士〕、大益、大乾、大器、大升。娶成氏。應天府鄉試第六十九名，會試第二百八名。

李勳〔貫旗手衛，軍籍，山東德州衛人，國子生，治詩經，字世臣，行一，年三十三，八月初四日生〕。曾祖貴，祖龍，父鸞，母邵氏。慈侍下，兄安〔百戶〕，弟默。娶張氏，繼娶王氏、郊氏。順天府鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百八十三名。

張應福〔貫直隸大名府魏縣，民籍，山西潞安府襄垣縣人，縣學生，治春秋，字子承，行一，年三十五，十二月二十三日生〕。曾祖奉，祖武，父惟高〔壽官〕，母常氏。具慶下，弟應祿、應禎、應祚。娶崔氏，繼娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第十名，會試第二百九十九名。
translation_en:
Wang Tingjian, registered in Qiongzhou, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the department school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rudi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daduan; his grandfather, Li, held an honorary longevity title with cap and girdle; and his father, Pin, was a student of the Directorate of Education. His father's principal wife was née Li; his stepmothers were née Liu and née Peng; his birth mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Tingfu, Tingjie, and Tingyan. He married a woman née Xu, then successively women née Yao and née Yu. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dazhuang, registered in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the department school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Sili; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chunde; his grandfather, Shangzhong, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father, Guan, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his mother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Dazhen; his younger brothers were Dake, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Dayi, Daqian, Daqi, and Dasheng. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xun, registered in the Standard Bearer Guard in a military household, was a native of Dezhou Guard, Shandong, and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shichen; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Long; his father, Luan; and his mother, née Shao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was An, a Company Commander, and his younger brother was Mo. He married a woman née Zhang, then successively women née Wang and née Jiao. He placed eighty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yingfu, registered in Wei County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Xiangyuan County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a student of the county school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather, Wu; his father, Weigao, who held an honorary longevity title; and his mother, née Chang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yinglu, Yingzhen, and Yingzuo. He married a woman née Cui and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
鍾崇文，貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，府學生，治《詩經》，字仲謨，行二，平三十五，正月二十一日生。曾祖叔顯，祖光，父任，母田氏。永感下。弟崇武〔刑部主事〕。娶萬氏。江西鄉試第三十一名，會試第八十二名。

饒仁侃，貫湖廣武昌府崇陽縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治《禮記》，字近剛，行七，年三十八，九月初十日生。曾祖慶壽，祖孟釗，父蒼，母孫氏。永感下。兄仁備、仁佳、仁俸、仁价、仁仕、仁倌，弟仁佾。娶徐氏。湖廣鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百八名。

楊愈茂，貫陝西慶陽府安化縣民籍，西安府三原縣人，國子生，治《詩經》，字伯榮，行三，年三十，十月二十三日生。曾祖敖，祖彪，父仲臣〔聽選官〕，前母折氏，母何氏。慈侍下。兄愈高〔典史〕、愈喬，弟愈暢、愈盛。娶何氏。陝西鄉試第六十名，會試第二百三名。

鍾穀，貫浙江紹興府上虞縣匠籍，縣學附學生，治《易經》，字心卿，行三，年二十六，六月十五日生。曾祖韶，祖珎，父祥，前母沈氏，母張氏。具慶下。兄德華、德俊〔俱聽選官〕、德周、德良、德成，弟德盛、德茂。娶顧氏。浙江鄉試第九十名，會試第一百四名。
translation_en:
Zhong Chongwen, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongmo, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five [?—the transcription reads 平 rather than 年], born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuxian, his grandfather Guang, his father Ren, and his mother née Tian; his parents and grandparents were deceased; his younger brother Chongwu was a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; he married a woman née Wan and placed thirty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rao Renkan, registered in a military household in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Jingang, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qingshou, his grandfather Mengzhao, his father Cang, and his mother née Sun; his parents and grandparents were deceased; his elder brothers were Renbei, Renjia, Renfeng, Renjie, Renshi, and Renguan, and his younger brother was Renyi; he married a woman née Xu and placed thirty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yumao, registered in a civilian household in Anhua County, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, and originating from Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Borong, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ao, his grandfather Biao, and his father Zhongchen, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father’s former wife was née She and his mother née He; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Yugao, an Unranked Assistant, and Yuqiao, and his younger brothers were Yuchang and Yusheng; he married a woman née He and placed sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Gu, registered in an artisan household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xinqing, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shao, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Xiang; his father’s former wife was née Shen and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Dehua and Dejun, both officials awaiting selection for appointment, Dezhou, Deliang, and Decheng, and his younger brothers were Desheng and Demao; he married a woman née Gu and placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳廷芝〔貫忠義後衞，軍籍，山東登州府黃縣人，順天府學附學生，治詩經，字季馨，行二，年二十八，二月初八日生。〕曾祖貴〔縣主簿〕，祖宗，父雄，嫡母孫氏，生母劉氏。慈侍下。兄廷蘭。娶歐氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十五名，會試第三百名。

張崌〔貫直隸大名府開州，民籍，國子生，治書經，字子靜，行三，年三十五，二月初十日生。〕曾祖魯，祖傑，父元善，母孫氏，繼母章氏。嚴侍下。兄岐、嶓，弟崙、峒。娶陳氏。順天府鄉試第四十一名，會試第二百六十一名。

朱泰〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字良甫，行十七，年三十八，正月二十六日生。〕曾祖詵，祖旭，父銳，母范氏。永感下。娶范氏。浙江鄉試第八十九名，會試第一百六十三名。
translation_en:
Niu Yinglong was registered in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shijian, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-nine years old, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather, Fu, was an Instructor in the Yin-yang School; and his father, Kongchang, was a County Assistant Magistrate. His mother was née Zheng, and his stepmothers were née Zhao and née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Youlong, a student of the Directorate of Education; Yingjiao; Yulong, also a student of the Directorate of Education; Tengjiao; Panlong; and Ruilong. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Tingzhi was registered in the Zhongyi Rear Guard in a military household and was a native of Huang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An additional student of the Shuntian Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jixin, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Gui, was a County Registrar; his grandfather was Zong, and his father was Xiong. His legal mother was née Sun, and his birth mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Tinglan. He married a woman née Ou. He placed 135th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ju was registered in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zijing, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather was Jie, and his father was Yuanshan. His mother was née Sun, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His mother was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving father. His elder brothers were Qi and Bo, and his younger brothers were Lun and Dong. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tai was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Liangfu, and he ranked seventeenth among his brothers. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather was Xu, and his father was Rui. His mother was née Fan. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Fan. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

===
周思充
貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍　縣學生
治書經字道可行十一年二十九八月十五日生
曾祖澐　祖景〔贈監察御史〕　父如斗〔巡撫應天都察院右僉都御史〕　母毛氏〔贈孺人〕　繼母張氏〔封孺人〕
具慶下　兄思齊〔貢士〕　弟思彥〔監生〕　思彰〔監生〕　思章〔生〕　思顔　思曜　思亭　娶夏氏

劉繼文
貫直隸鳳陽府宿州靈璧縣民籍　國子生
治易經字永謨行一年三十二五月二十三日生
曾祖通〔遞運所大使〕　祖鎔　父貞　母黃氏
慈侍下　娶王氏　繼娶王氏
□天府鄉試第一百二名　會試第一百二十三名
punctuated:
丘騰，貫湖廣承天府沔陽州軍籍，州學生。治書經，字子雲，行二，年二十六，四月二十九日生。曾祖思賢，祖容，父福，前母湯氏，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄鵬、勝，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百九十四名。

譚啟，貫四川夔州府大寧縣民籍，縣學生。治易經，字繼之，行二，年三十五，七月初五日生。曾祖春〔衛經歷〕，祖珩，父廷傑，母李氏。永感下，兄光，弟介，娶鄭氏。四川鄉試第四十五名，會試第一百七十三名。

周思充，貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，縣學生。治書經，字道可，行十一，年二十九，八月十五日生。曾祖澐，祖璟〔贈監察御史〕，父如斗〔巡撫應天都察院右僉都御史〕，母毛氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母張氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄思齊〔貢士〕，弟思彥〔監生〕、思彰〔監生〕、思顏、思曜、思亭，娶夏氏。浙江鄉試第五名，會試第一百六十六名。

劉繼文，貫直隸鳳陽府宿州靈璧縣民籍，國子生。治易經，字永謨，行一，年三十二，五月二十三日生。曾祖通〔遞運所大使〕，祖鎔，父貞，母黃氏。慈侍下，娶王氏，繼娶王氏。□天府鄉試第一百二名，會試第二百二十三名。
translation_en:
Qiu Teng was registered in a military household in Mianyang Subprefecture, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ziyun. He ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sixian, his grandfather Rong, and his father Fu; his father's former wife was née Tang, and his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Peng and Sheng, and his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Qi was registered in a civilian household in Daning County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jizhi. He ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chun (Registrar of a Guard), his grandfather Heng, and his father Tingjie; his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Guang and his younger brother Jie; his wife was née Zheng. He placed forty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Sichong was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Daoke. He ranked eleventh among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Jing (posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor), and his father Rudou (Grand Coordinator of Yingtian and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate). His mother was née Mao (posthumously granted the title of Lady, ruren), and his stepmother was née Zhang (granted the title of Lady, ruren). His father and stepmother were both living. His elder brother was Siqi (a tribute scholar, gongshi); his younger brothers were Siyan and Sizhang (both students of the Imperial University), Siyan, Siyao, and Siting. His wife was née Xia. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jiwen was registered in a civilian household in Lingbi County, Su Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yongmo. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Tong (Chief Officer of a Transport Office), his grandfather Rong, and his father Zhen; his mother was née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was also née Wang. He placed 102nd in the Provincial Examination of □tian Prefecture [?] and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
張守中〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州，民籍，國子生，治書經，字叔原，行五，年三十六，二月十一日生。〕曾祖俊，祖昇，父綎〔知州〕，母王氏，繼母吳氏。慈侍下。兄銓、鈞、膽〔監察御史〕，弟守謙、守正、守復、守泰、同甫。娶孫氏，繼娶王氏。應天府鄉試第九十七名，會試第一百二十六名。

鄧宗孔〔貫廣西太平府崇善縣，民籍，府學生，治書經，字惟時，行一，年三十五，十月初四日生。〕曾祖褒，祖政，父召高〔監生〕，母歐氏，繼母方氏。慈侍下。娶岑氏。廣西鄉試第十六名，會試第二百七十五名。

齊康〔貫直隸廣平府永年縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字太和，行一，年三十七，六月二十八日生。〕曾祖盤，祖復勝，父祥，母陳氏。具慶下。弟唐、賡。娶張氏，繼娶季氏。順天府鄉試第二十八名，會試第七十名。

張應治〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣，民籍，嘉興縣人，府學生，治書經，字體徵，行二，年二十九，四月初十日生。〕曾祖正，祖世華〔壽官〕，父用，母王氏。具慶下。兄應潮，弟應源、應浚、應濂、應滂。娶錢氏。浙江鄉試第二十四名，會試第八十五名。
translation_en:
Zhang Shouzhong 張守中 was registered in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Shuyuan and ranked fifth among his brothers; he was thirty-six years old, born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Ting, a subprefect; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Quan, Jun, and Dan, the last a censor; his younger brothers were Shouqian, Shouzheng, Shoufu, Shoutai, and Tongfu. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed ninety-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Zongkong 鄧宗孔 was registered in Chongshan County, Taiping Prefecture, Guangxi, in a civilian household. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Weishi and ranked first among his brothers; he was thirty-five years old, born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Bao, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Zhaogao, an Imperial University student; his mother was née Ou and his stepmother née Fang. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Cen. He placed sixteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Kang 齊康 was registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Taihe and ranked first among his brothers; he was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Pan, his grandfather Fusheng, his father Xiang, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tang and Geng. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Ji. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yingzhi 張應治 was registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, and was a native of Jiaxing County. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tizheng and ranked second among his brothers; he was twenty-nine years old, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Shihua, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity, his father Yong, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingchao; his younger brothers were Yingyuan, Yingjun, Yinglian, and Yingpang. He married a woman née Qian. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

凌琯〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字惟和，行一，年四十，閏四月初八日生〕。曾祖祐，祖社孫，父相，母蔣氏。嚴侍下，弟煥、琓、焅、烱、烺，娶章氏，繼娶洪氏。應天府鄉試第十六名，會試第一百三十八名。

趙岩〔貫浙江嘉興府崇德縣民籍，直隸蘇州府長洲縣縣學增廣生，治詩經，字維石，行一，年三十三，七月初五日生〕。曾祖海，祖盛，父聰，母沈氏。嚴侍下，弟崶、崗、崙，娶潘氏。浙江鄉試第六十五名，會試第一百六十八名。

張問明〔貫山西平陽府猗氏縣鹽籍，縣學生，治書經，字子明，行二，年三十，八月初二日生〕。曾祖能，祖儒〔縣主簿〕，父嘉會，母衛氏。具慶下，兄問行，弟問士、問政、問道、問達，娶何氏，繼娶鄭氏。山西鄉試第二十六名，會試第二百十七名。

仇炅〔貫山西潞安府長治縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字文綱，行七，年四十二，十一月十七日生〕。曾祖鏞〔七品散官〕，祖鴻，父桓〔監生〕，母李氏。永感下，兄勳〔旌表孝子〕、煥、熈、丙、烺、皇、焸〔火醫〔省一火〕〕、烺，娶李氏。□□鄉試第五名，會試第一百八十五名。
translation_en:
Ling Guan 凌琯, courtesy name Weihe, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Southern Zhili. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the eighth day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather Shesun, his father Xiang, and his mother Lady Jiang; his father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Huan, Wan, Kao, Jiong, and Lang. He married Lady Zhang and subsequently Lady Hong. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yan 趙岩, courtesy name Weishi, was registered in a civilian household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an added-quota student at the county school of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Zhili. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Sheng, his father Cong, and his mother Lady Shen; his father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Feng, Gang, and Lun. He married Lady Pan. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenming 張問明, courtesy name Ziming, was a county-school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, registered in a salt-producing household in Yishi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Neng, his grandfather Ru (a county Registrar), his father Jiahui, and his mother Lady Wei; both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenxing, and his younger brothers were Wenshi, Wenzheng, Wendao, and Wenda. He married Lady He and subsequently Lady Zheng. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Jiong 仇炅, courtesy name Wengang, was a National University student specializing in the Record of Rites, registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi. He ranked seventh among his brothers, was aged forty-two, and was born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yong (a seventh-rank prestige official), his grandfather Hong, his father Huan (a National University student), and his mother Lady Li; both parents were deceased. The elder brothers listed are Xun (officially honored for filial piety), Huan, Xi, Bing, Lang, Huang, [name unclear: 焸, annotated 火醫 with the further note “omit one 火”], and Lang [?; the sequence of names is garbled]. He married Lady Li. He placed fifth in the Provincial Examination of □□ [place illegible] and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:

translation_en:
Wang Jiabin, courtesy name Guoguang, was from Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and registered in a military household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Mei, his father Tianxu, and his mother née Cheng; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuanbin and Libin, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wenchen, courtesy name Zhengshu, was from Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ze, his grandfather Yi, his father Ming, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenren, Wenru, and Wenchong. He married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Wenwei, courtesy name Zhongtao, was from Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and registered in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Ji, his father Hui, and his mother née Men; both parents were deceased. His wife was née Guo. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Lian, courtesy name Chunzhi, was registered in an official household of Changde Guard, Huguang. A student of the Changde prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuqian, his grandfather Xi, his father Qie 洯, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhu and Kuang, and his wife was née Hu. He placed eighty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Tianqi, courtesy name Dazheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jiong, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Bin; his father was Yuangao; and his mother was née Qiu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Tianxiang and Zongcheng, the latter a tribute student; his younger brothers were Tianlang and Zonglun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shang, courtesy name Zhibo, was registered in a military household in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Dezhong; his grandfather was Yuezu; his father was Xing; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Laixiang. He married a woman née Zeng. He placed thirty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Mingmo, courtesy name Junxian, was registered in a civilian household in Guangping County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Renci, a school instructor; and his mother was née Pan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Mingdian and his younger brother Mingming. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Chongsi, courtesy name Chengfang, was registered in a civilian household in Feixiang County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a prefect posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Central Rectitude; his grandfather was Fu, an investigating censor; his father was Dong; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Chongdeng, a medical official, and his younger brother was Chongjiao. He married a woman née Bai. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Song, registered in a civilian household in Dacheng County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was an added student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zijie; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Huai, a County Registrar; his mother was née Jiao and his stepmother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Pei. He placed 210th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lun Wen, registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shaozhou; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jilin, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Kesheng; his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were She and Yu, and his wife was née Ou. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 67th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Jinkui, registered in a civilian household in Guichi County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenzheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhang, his grandfather Lun, and his father Si; his mother was née Jiang and his stepmother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Jinlin and Jinqiao, and his wife was née He. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 42nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Zeyi, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruqian; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenjian, his grandfather Jiyao, a Prefectural Judge, and his father Qixin, a District Magistrate; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zedui and Zexun, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brother was Zeyi (則頤), and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.
