translation_en:
Xiang Dushou 項篤壽 was registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Xiushui County. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zixin and ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-one years old and was born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Gang, was a County Magistrate; and his father, Quan, was an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial. His legal mother was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yuanqi was a Clerk in the Directorate of Imperial Parks, and his younger brother Yuanbian was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Mengxian 段孟賢 was registered in a civilian household in Hukou County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Ruyu and ranked sixth in birth order. He was thirty-five years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhonghou; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Luan. His father's former wife was née Cao, and his mother was née Mei. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Mengxuan, Mengfu, and Mengzhuang, the last a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate; his younger brother Rufang was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Rao. He placed seventy-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third Class: 211 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Cai Shuda, courtesy name Zijian, was registered in a military household of the Weihui Defense Battalion in Henan and was a native of Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Weihui prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Run, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Jingyu, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father was Yangjin, an Administration Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Yang, held the title Lady (ruren) by imperial patent. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shumai, Shulin, and Shujin, and his wife was née Jiao. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Lu, courtesy name Congyin, was registered in an artisan household in Sishui County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Xi, an Assistant Magistrate; his father was Xueshi, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Lü. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Shi, his younger brother was Mian, and his wife was née Kong. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qianzhang, courtesy name Shunqing, was registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked 150th in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Dezhi; his grandfather was Yin, a School Instructor; his father was Kuan, also a School Instructor; and his mother was née Cai. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Xian, Po, Lezhang, Xianzhang, Xiaozhang, and Yanzhang; his younger brothers were Taizhang and Jianzhang. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Chonglun, registered in Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zichang, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was forty-one years old, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Bofu, his father Yunqiong, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chongshi, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Zhao, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tinglun, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongkai, his grandfather Cui, and his father Zongyuan, Chief Clerk. His father’s former wives were née Chen and née Liu; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother Jian was a District Magistrate, and his wife was née Mai. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Conglü, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Maohe, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Yuanchen, his father Yi, and his mother née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Congzheng and Congyan, and his wife was née Qian. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Lian, registered in Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ximao, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three years old, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Xuan, an Assistant Instructor, and his father Tang, an annual tribute student. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Shan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xun and Ting, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ji Datong, registered in Kai Prefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bocong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather, Chen, received the honorary title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Cheng, was Grand Coordinator of Liaodong and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady for Attending (ruren); his stepmother, née Li, was granted the same title. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Dashao, Daxia, Dawu, Dazhuang, Daguan, Dalin, Dabin, Dashun, and Daning. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 118th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yizhong, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongxian; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Huai, his father Jing, and his mother née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yiyuan, Fengming, Yiheng, Yilan, and Yihua. He married a woman née Fu. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Tingguan, registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Binqing; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Luan, his father Kexue, and his mother née Wen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingwang, and his younger brothers were Tingdui and Tingmo. He married a woman née Zhuang and subsequently a woman née Gu. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Yong, registered in Suide Guard, Shaanxi, belonged to an official household and was a native of Yingshang County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a Yulin Guard school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruhong; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Yan, and grandfather, Lin, were both Battalion Commanders posthumously granted the title of Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His father, Jing, was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His mother, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Virtue (shuren); his stepmother, née Wang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhen, and his younger brothers were Yue and Ming. He married a woman née Su. He placed thirtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Tai, registered in Shouchang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Junzuo. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kezheng, a County Registrar; his grandfather was Tingling, a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Ao, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Xiang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, and his younger brothers were Du and Xu. His wife was née Xu. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhen, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongyan. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengren, his grandfather was Jianchang, his father was Bingxin, and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brother was Mei. His wife was née Yu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Xiang, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Xiushui County. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Mengliang. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather was Liang, his father was Hao, an annual tribute student, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guai and Wu. His wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ai Qi, registered in Mizhi County, Suide Subprefecture, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zizheng. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenji, posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Hui, posthumously appointed Secretary and subsequently granted the additional posthumous title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Xiqing, and his mother was née Gao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Zhen, a Vice Commander of a Police Office, and Xun, an annual tribute student. His younger brothers were Zi, an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; Shu, Registrar of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Jia, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in Sichuan; and Chengdao. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Mo, courtesy name Tiwen, was registered in a military household of Yingchuan Guard, Henan, and was a native of Dongping Subprefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Mian; and his father, Bangyi, who held an honorary title for longevity. His mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xun, Gao, and Wenjiong, the last a Ceremonial Assistant. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Weijing, courtesy name Shuji, was registered in a military household of Xiaofeng County, Anji Subprefecture, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked seventeenth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, who held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather, Song, who was honorifically appointed Director of a bureau in the Ministry of Personnel; and his father, Lin, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, posthumously awarded the prestige title Zhongxian dafu. His father's former wives were two women née Wang, the first posthumously granted the title Lady for Service; his mother was née Fang, posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Weiyue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Weiting, an Imperial University student; and Weixia, also an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Weicheng, Weiyu, Weijun, Weikai, Weiji, Weijun, Weishan, and Weijiong. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhimeng, courtesy name Shuzheng, was registered in a civilian household of Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, who held an honorary title for righteousness; his grandfather, Sui, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his father, Wei, was a County Registrar. His mother was née Ren, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Qimeng. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Kong. He placed 121st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yiqin, courtesy name Ziqing, was registered in a civilian household of Cheng'an County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sen; his grandfather, Ze, who held an honorary title for longevity; and his father, Mao. His mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yilin and Yigui, and his younger brothers were Yicheng and Yihe. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently women née Li and née Yang. He placed 123rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Aizhong 范愛衆, courtesy name Tongren, was registered in a military household of Dongsheng Right Guard and was a native of Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Zunhua County school in Shuntian Prefecture, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather, Cong; and his father, Gong. His father's former wife was Lady Sun, and his mother was Lady Yuan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuzhong and Yuzhong (御衆 and 與衆). He married Lady Gao. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yiren 孫以仁, courtesy name Xueyuan, was registered in a banner household of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shangneng; his grandfather, Long, was an instructor; and his father was Rang. His mother was Lady Cai. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Yihua. He married Lady Gu and subsequently Ladies Cong and Zhao. He placed twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Sanjie 袁三接, courtesy name Bangbiao, was registered in a military household of Xiangshan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An attached student of the Panyu County school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-four, born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Kui; his grandfather, Zusheng; and his father, Jingsheng. His mother was Lady Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shaoji and Sande; his younger brothers were Sansheng, Sanwei, and Sanxi. He married Lady Li. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lie 陳烈, courtesy name Sishao, was registered in a civilian household of Jian'an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Jun, was an assistant instructor; his grandfather was Xu 湏 [?]; and his father, Nan, was an annual tribute student. His mother was Lady Ye. Both parents were living. His younger brothers are recorded as Zhao, Shu, Weiqian, Tao, Shu, Ye, Jing, Pao, Huang, Dang, Peng, Pao, and He [the transcription and division of this list of names are doubtful]. He married Lady Tong. He placed fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

嚴鎡〔貫光祿寺廚籍，順天府豐潤縣人，國子生，治易經，字應時，行二，年三十三，十月十七日生〕。曾祖文，祖瑾，父雄，母周氏。慈侍下。兄鏓，弟鎮、錦。娶何氏，繼娶陸氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十四名，會試第二百九十一名。

馬會〔貫四川保寧府南部縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字元明，行五，年三十二，十一月初三日生〕。曾祖自旺，祖庸，父孟舍〔縣丞〕，嫡母李氏，生母諶氏。慈侍下。兄時〔監生〕、中元〔都司都事〕、曉、曙、曜、晉〔訓導〕、暠、旦、頃，弟昺、頃。娶孫氏。四川鄉試第四十四名，會試第一百六十七名。
translation_en:
Wang Tongdao, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a military household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Wenkai received the honorary title of County Magistrate; his grandfather Lin was a County Magistrate and was posthumously granted the title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father Tinghuai was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his father's principal wife was née Hu, and his birth mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tonghe, Tongen, Tongyuan, and Tongsheng; his younger brothers were Tonghui, Tonggui, Tonglun, Tongchen, and Tongqing. His wife was née Yuan. He placed thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Weiguan, courtesy name Dongke, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan. A department-school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiong; his grandfather Zongsheng was an annual tribute student; and his father Ao was a County Magistrate. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Weiqiao, Chief Seal Keeper, Weiduan, Weisu, Weijiao, and Weikang; his younger brothers were Weilong and Weixing. His wife was née He. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Zi, courtesy name Yingshi, was registered in a kitchen-service household of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was a native of Fengrun County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen, his grandfather Jin, and his father Xiong; his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Cong, and his younger brothers were Zhen and Jin. His first wife was née He; he subsequently married a woman née Lu. He placed 124th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Hui, courtesy name Yuanming, was registered in a civilian household in Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziwang, his grandfather Yong, and his father Mengshe, a County Vice Magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Li, and his birth mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shi, an Imperial University student; Zhongyuan, a Registry official in a Regional Military Commission; Xiao; Shu; Yao; Jin, an Assistant Instructor; Gao; Dan; and Qing [?]. His younger brothers were Bing and Qing [?]. His wife was née Sun. He placed forty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Liang, courtesy name Fuwu, was registered in a civilian household in Hui'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather, Jian; his father, Zhen; and his mother, née Zhuang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Ji, Hao, and Qian, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yiben, courtesy name Zhongli, was registered in a military household of Mianyang Guard, Huguang. An additional student of the Mianyang Subprefectural Government School specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Xian, an Instructor. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Xiang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yishu, and his younger brothers were Yizhen, Yicai, and Yishi. His wife was née Yang. He placed seventieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Bangyan, courtesy name Xianzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Record of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benshan; his grandfather, Yue; and his father, He. His legal mother was née Liang, and his birth mother was née Bu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Bangxian, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Renyuan, courtesy name Zishan, was registered in a military household in Wanquan County, Puzhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Yu, an honorary official; his father, Chaozhong; and his mother, née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Renheng and Fuyuan, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉世曾〔貫四川重慶府巴縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字胤甫，行一，年三十一，二月十六日生〕。曾祖相〔封參議〕，祖鶴年〔參政〕，父起元，母羅氏。具慶下。弟世箕、世賞〔貢士〕、世偉、世卿、世選、世芳、世德、世榮、世懋、世珍。娶黃氏。四川鄉試第三名，會試第八十名。

蕭守身〔貫河南懷慶衛，官籍，湖廣德安府雲夢縣人，國子生，治詩經，字尚本，行四，年三十二，九月初一日生〕。曾祖禮，祖銳〔義官〕，父鸞〔監生〕，母何氏。永感下。兄國勳〔都司經歷〕、守善〔典膳〕、守業〔引禮〕、守愚、守厚、守高，弟守忭、守忰、守舍、守珍、守美、守敬、守慶、守盛、守養。河南鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百九十四名。

秦崢〔貫直隸大名府開州長垣縣，匠籍，國子生，治易經，字思謙，行一，年三十六，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖浩，祖忠，父佐，母朱氏。慈侍下。弟岍。娶顧氏。順天府鄉試第七十三名，會試第二百八十名。
translation_en:
Huang Wenwei, courtesy name Dehua, was registered in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An additional-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rixin; his grandfather, Yuqing; his father, Jirong; his mother, née Feng; and his stepmother, née Peng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Wensui and Wenyao, and his wife was née Wu. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shizeng, courtesy name Yinfu, was registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, honorifically appointed Assistant Administration Commissioner; his grandfather, Henian, was an Administration Vice Commissioner; his father was Qiyuan; and his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiji, Shishang (a tribute scholar), Shiwei, Shiqing, Shixuan, Shifang, Shide, Shirong, Shimao, and Shizhen. His wife was née Huang. He placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Shoushen, courtesy name Shangben, was registered in Huaiqing Guard, Henan, in an official household and was a native of Yunmeng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Rui, held honorary official status; his father, Luan, was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guoxun (a Registry Manager in a Regional Military Commission), Shoushan (a Steward of Delicacies), Shouye (an Usher), Shouyu, Shouhou, and Shougao; his younger brothers were Shoubian, Shoucui, Shoushe, Shouzhen, Shoumei, Shoujing, Shouqing, Shousheng, and Shouyang. He placed twenty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Zheng, courtesy name Siqian, was registered in Changyuan County, Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in an artisan household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Zhong; his father, Zuo; and his mother, née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Qian, and his wife was née Gu. He placed seventy-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

蔣機〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字若衡，行十，年三十二，六月初三日生。〕曾祖集良，祖正馥〔驛丞〕，父世滋，前母左氏，母李氏。具慶下，弟楙、拭，娶田氏。江西鄉試第八十三名，會試第二百四十二名。

薛東海〔貫山西太原府石州，民籍，州學附學生，治易經，字汝觀，行一，年三十四，十一月二十七日生。〕曾祖章〔義官〕，祖玹〔典膳〕，父近朝，母温氏。具慶下，弟東周、東魯、東吳，娶馮氏。山西鄉試第四十六名，會試第十八名。
translation_en:
Wang Yu 王宇, registered in a civilian household in Anyi County, Jie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a supplementary student at the school of the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Zida, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Wen, and his father Jide; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Dang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chong, Ning, and Yin, and his wife was née Hu. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jiamo 胡嘉謨, registered in a civilian household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Zizhong, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Rui, and his father Chaoyong, a Police Chief; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiaji, Jiaqing, and Jiayou, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Ji 蔣機, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a supplementary student at the county school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Ruoheng, ranked tenth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiliang, his grandfather Zhengfu, a Station Master, and his father Shizi; his father’s former wife was née Zuo, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mao and Shi, and his wife was née Tian. He placed eighty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Donghai 薛東海, registered in a civilian household in Shi Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a supplementary student at the subprefectural school; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Ruguan, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhang, an honorary official; his grandfather was Xuan, a Director of Food Services; his father was Jinchao, and his mother was née Wen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dongzhou, Donglu, and Dongwu, and his wife was née Feng. He placed forty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Xuedao, registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruzhi; he ranked thirty-second among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mi, his grandfather Qiong, his father Siming, and his mother née Lu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Xueshi, Xueyi, Xueshu, Xuemeng, Xuewen, Xueyuan, and Xueshen; his wife was née Du. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Yingqian, registered in a civilian household in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bofu; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-two years old, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zeng, an honorary official honored for longevity; his grandfather Rui was an Assistant Instructor; his father Li held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zizhong, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fu, registered in an official household of Dali Guard, Yunnan, was a native of Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zhongli, ranked third among his brothers and male cousins, and was twenty-eight years old, born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ying, grandfather Hai, and father Ju were all Company Commanders; his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rong, a Company Commander, and Hua; his younger brothers were Chong (𠖥) [?], Guan, and Xian. His wife was née Jiang. He placed second in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiaxiang, registered in a military household in Shen County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhaoxing; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-five years old, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Cong was a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Wei, his father Pin, and his mother née Ren, who had received an official commendation for widowly chastity. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

薛德統〔貫福建福州府福清縣，鹽籍，縣學生，治詩經，字守正，行五，年三十八，十一月初四日生〕。曾祖士亘〔封戶部主事〕，祖世暊，父尚飛〔衛經歷〕，前母郭氏，母石氏。永感下，兄德績、德忠〔訓導〕、德王、德璋、德充〔鹽運司知事〕、德瑑、德璲、德佐〔封刑科給事中〕，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百十名。

舒應龍〔貫廣西桂林府全州，民籍，賓州人，州學增廣生，治禮記，字時見，行二，年二十二，十一月十二日生〕。曾祖綱〔教諭〕，祖文奎〔知縣〕，父烈，母袁氏。具慶下，兄應蘭，弟應元、應麟、應鳳、應蕙，娶蔣氏。廣西鄉試第十三名，會試第十二名。

劉早〔貫山東萊州府膠州，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字思舜，行九，年四十二，九月十二日生〕。曾祖福，祖紀，父瑤〔府司獄〕，母王氏。具慶下，娶欒氏。山東鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百四十四名。
translation_en:
Tian Chengfa, registered in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zixian; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was You; his grandfather, Jing; his father, Xi, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Chang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Chengfu. He married a woman née Feng and subsequently a woman née Yu. He placed eighteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Detong, registered in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shouzheng; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shigen, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Shixu; and his father, Shangfei, a Guard Registrar. His father's former wife was née Guo, and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Deji; Dezhong, an Assistant Instructor; Dewang; Dezhang; Dechong, a Clerk in a Salt Distribution Commission; Dezhuan; Desui; and Dezuo, granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Yinglong, registered in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Binzhou. He was an additional student in the subprefectural school, specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shijian; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-two, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, an Instructor; his grandfather, Wenkui, a County Magistrate; his father, Lie; and his mother, née Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yinglan, and his younger brothers were Yingyuan, Yinglin, Yingfeng, and Yinghui. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed thirteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zao, registered in Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Sishun; he ranked ninth in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Ji; his father, Yao, a Prefectural Prison Warden; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Luan. He placed forty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

張鏄〔貫陝西西安府乾州武功縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯始，行九，年四十六，十一月十六日生〕。曾祖海，祖讓，父儒珍〔教授〕，母康氏。慈侍下，兄應中、應祥、鑄、應祺、應福〔教諭〕、應和、鎬，弟〔陳州同知〕〔主事〕。娶費氏，繼娶李氏。陝西鄉試第三十一名，會試第二百九十六名。

鄒廷望〔貫湖廣寶慶府新化縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字道吾，行三，年三十三，四月十五日生〕。曾祖伏瓚，祖旻輝，父楚錫，母曽氏。具慶下，兄廷詔、廷誥，娶孫氏。湖廣鄉試第十五名，會試第二十七名。

陳頤正〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字觀甫，行二，年二十八，五月二十一日生〕。曾祖倫，祖鳳〔縣主簿，贈兵部郎中〕，父茂義〔左參政〕，母桂氏〔封宜人〕。重慶下，兄頤素，弟頤忠、頤大、頤明、頤震、頤善、頤健、頤慶，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第三十一名，會試第二百三十三名。

劉珮〔貫山西太原府盂縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字象德，行四，年三十，七月十二日生〕。曾祖寶，祖斌，父元，母溫氏。永感下，兄碧、璋、環，娶趙氏。山西鄉試第十四名，會試第二百二十六名。
translation_en:
Zhang Bo, registered in a civilian household in Wugong County, Qian Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boshi; he ranked ninth in birth order, was forty-six years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Rang, and his father Ruzhen, a Prefectural School Instructor; his mother was née Kang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yingzhong, Yingxiang, Zhu, Yingqi, Yingfu (a County School Instructor), Yinghe, and Gao. The text then reads “younger brother,” followed by annotations identifying an Associate Prefect of Chenzhou and a Secretary, whose names or placement are unclear [?]. He married a woman née Fei and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed thirty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Tingwang, registered in a military household in Xinhua County, Baoqing Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daowu; he ranked third in birth order, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Fuzan, his grandfather Minhui, and his father Chuxi; his mother was née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingzhao and Tinggao, and he married a woman née Sun. He placed fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yizheng, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guanfu; he ranked second in birth order, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-first day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather Feng was a County Registrar, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of War. His father Maoyi was a Left Administration Vice Commissioner, and his mother, née Gui, held the title Lady of Suitability. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brother was Yisu, and his younger brothers were Yizhong, Yida, Yiming, Yizhen, Yishan, Yijian, and Yiqing. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Pei, registered in a civilian household in Yu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiangde; he ranked fourth in birth order, was thirty years old, and was born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bao, his grandfather Bin, and his father Yuan; his mother was née Wen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bi, Zhang, and Huan, and he married a woman née Zhao. He placed fourteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊成名〔貫福建建寧府建安縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字志完，行一，年三十三，二月二十三日生〕。曾祖旦〔吏部尚書〕，祖京〔太僕寺寺丞〕，父謙，母滕氏。慈侍下，娶倪氏，繼娶黃氏。福建鄉試第四十五名，會試第二百七十八名。

趙應元〔貫浙江杭州府仁和縣，民籍，直隸六安州學訓導，治易經，字子貞，行一，年三十二，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖善，祖宣，父文遠，母王氏。永感下，兄奎、麟、鑾、森，弟相、卿、宰、材，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第十名，會試第二百六十四名。

劉翾〔貫四川成都府內江縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治春秋，字惟翰，行一，年三十六，十月二十八日生〕。曾祖時和，祖綵〔教授，贈布政司參議〕，父望之〔左布政使〕，前母田氏〔贈恭人〕，母張氏〔封恭人〕。嚴侍下，兄薖〔按察司僉事〕、涵〔府通判〕、潭、克讓，弟剽〔貢士〕、翩、翊、詡、翓、翃，娶蕭氏。四川鄉試第五名，會試第一百四十七名。
translation_en:
Li E, registered in Lingshou County, Zhending Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Lingqiu. Listed as first in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Jing, and his father Xun; his legal mother was née Chen and his birth mother née Nie. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was He, and his younger brothers were Fengming, Fengteng, Feng'ao, Fenghuang, and Fengyi. His wife was née Peng. He ranked ninety-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Chengming, registered in Jian'an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhiwan. Listed as first in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the twenty-third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Dan, Minister of Personnel; his grandfather was Jing, Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud; his father was Qian, and his mother was née Teng. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. He married a woman née Ni and subsequently a woman née Huang. He ranked forty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yingyuan, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and served as Assistant Instructor at the school of Liu'an Subprefecture in the Metropolitan Region. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zizhen. Listed as first in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Wenyuan; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kui, Lin, Luan, and Sen, and his younger brothers were Xiang, Qing, Zai, and Cai. His wife was née Wang. He ranked tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xuan, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weihan. Listed as first in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shihe; his grandfather was Cai, a Prefectural School Instructor posthumously awarded the title of Assistant Administration Commissioner; and his father was Wangzhi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner. His father's former wife, née Tian, was posthumously awarded the title of Lady of Respect; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the same title. His mother was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving father. His elder brothers were Ke, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; Han, a Prefectural Assistant Magistrate; Tan; and Kerang. His younger brothers were Piao, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Pian; Yi; Xu; Xie; and Hong. His wife was née Xiao. He ranked fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yinbin, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuyang. He ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang, his grandfather Sichuan, and his father Dequan; his mother was née Wang 汪. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yongbin; his younger brothers were Sanbin, Yanbin (an Assistant Instructor), Rubin, Yingbin, Dabin, Shangbin, and Chaobin. His wife was née Cheng. He placed thirty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yong, registered in Yanjin County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Siyang. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jian (an honorary official for longevity), his grandfather Bing (a Steward of Foodstuffs), and his father Yi (a Steward of Foodstuffs). His father's former wife was née Yang; his mother was née Han. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Rang (a student of the Directorate of Education) and Ne; his younger brothers were Dang, Shen, Shen 詵, Tiao, Xu, Hu, Tuo, and Shi. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongzai, registered in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shihou. He ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xidan (an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner), his grandfather Dayou (an Office Manager in a Regional Military Commission), and his father Song; his mother was née Nie. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Zongke and Zongwang; his younger brother was Zongheng. His first wife was née Liu, and his subsequent wife was née Zhong. He placed twenty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Sangang was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, and was a native of Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture. He was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zhendao. He ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Sixian, his grandfather Tingyan, and his father Qi. His legal mother was née Xi 襲, and his birth mother was née Cheng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yijing (a Chief Clerk) and Ershou; his younger brothers were Siwei, Wuyu, and Liuji. His wife was née Dai. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Shijie, courtesy name Yixue, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jieyou; his grandfather, Boyang; his father, Tingshan; and his mother, née Xiao. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shizhu, Shilong, Shisheng, Shijin, Shizhi, Shinuo, and Shigao. His wife was née Xiao. He placed fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Rumei, courtesy name Dehe, was registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, Commissioner of a Transport Office; his grandfather, Tianzhang; his father, Tinggui, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother, née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Rushu, Ruji, and Rulin. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Nan, courtesy name Zilin, was registered in a civilian household in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Shu; his father, Yong; and his mother, née Hu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Wu and Gang. His wife was née Dai. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Wenming, courtesy name Zhongmo, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weichang; his grandfather, Yongzhong, a County Registrar; his father, Rurui, a Deputy Office Chief in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his mother, née Xiong. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Wenguan and Wenlin, the latter an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Wenbao, Wen’ao [?], an Imperial University student, Wengui, a tribute scholar, Wenmei, Wenxie, Wenyu, and Wenjiong. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王原相〔貫廣東廣州府番禺縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字召之，行二，年二十八，九月初二日生〕。曾祖瑤，祖傳〔舉人，贈刑部主事〕，父漸逵〔刑部主事〕，嫡母何氏〔封安人〕，生母鄭氏。慈侍下，兄原格，弟原校、原析、原模、原朴，娶趙氏。廣東鄉試第三十四名，會試第一百九十八名。

趙睿〔貫直隸寧國府涇縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字若思，行一，年三十，二月二十八日生〕。曾祖孟緣，祖渙〔府通判〕，父栴，母王氏。慈侍下，弟膚、虔、𧆑、虞、瑩，娶沈氏。應天府鄉試第六十五名，會試第三十五名。
translation_en:
Liu Pan 劉泮, courtesy name Ruhua, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was originally from Fengxin County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziduan; his grandfather, Ren; and his father, Wenxin. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Xiao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han and Bin, and his younger brothers were Pu and Guan. His wife was née Zhu. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiayan 王嘉言, courtesy name Junmo, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was originally from Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shi and grandfather Hu both held prestige titles; his father Lu was a Vice Prefect. His mother was née Sun. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Lian, Jiamou, and Liu; his younger brothers were Jiashan, Sanchong, and Sance. His wife was née Gong, and his subsequent wife was née Fan. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuanxiang 王原相, courtesy name Shaozhi, was registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yao. His grandfather Chuan was a provincial graduate (juren), posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father Jiankui was a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. His legal mother was née He, granted the title of Lady of Repose (anren), and his birth mother was née Zheng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Yuange; his younger brothers were Yuanxiao, Yuanxi, Yuanmo, and Yuanpu. His wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rui 趙睿, courtesy name Ruosi, was registered in a civilian household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengyuan; his grandfather Huan was an Assistant Prefect; and his father was Zhan. His mother was née Wang. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Fu, Qian, 𧆑 [reading uncertain], Yu, and Ying. His wife was née Shen. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

錢貢〔貫浙江嘉興府桐鄉縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字時庸，行二，年三十七，八月二十二日生〕。曾祖達〔壽官〕，祖瑛，父泰，母沈氏。慈侍下，兄貫〔監生〕，弟賚，娶唐氏。浙江鄉試第七十九名，會試第一百五十六名。

translation_en:
Jiang Zhida, registered in a military household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruwei; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong was a Department Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather Ying was a Ceremonial Usher; his father was Tongwen, and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhiyuan, and his wife was née Yun. He placed 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Gong, registered in a civilian household in Tongxiang County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiyong; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Da held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Tai, and his mother was née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Guan was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his younger brother was Lai. His wife was née Tang. He placed seventy-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Yuguo, registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menglin; his grandfather was Jingchang; his father was Huang; his mother was née Yan, and his stepmother was née Wu. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yumin and Yudao. He married a woman née Yang, and subsequently women née Lin and née Shen. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ai Kejiu, registered in a military household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dezheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Qin was posthumously granted the title of Judge; his grandfather Hong was a Judge in a Regional Military Commission; his father was Yuanmei, and his mother was née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Kequan. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Zi, registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student at the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rucai. He ranked first in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Luan; his father was Qi; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mao, an Imperial University student, Si, Nian, an Imperial University student, Lü, and Jia; his younger brothers were Que, Zhi, and Yu. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ze was registered in a military household of the Yanshan Front Guard and was a native of Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. He was an additional student at the Shuntian prefectural Confucian school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ziren. He ranked second in birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Yong; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Run. His wife was née Su; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yixun, registered in a civilian household in Wen’an County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student at the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bopin. He ranked sixth in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Neng and grandfather Zhao were both county registrars. His father was Ji, and his mother was née Wen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun, assistant prefect of Gongchang Prefecture; Wei, a tribute scholar; Ji and Shen, both Imperial University students; Jing; Si, a government student; Cai; Chun, a tribute scholar; Xun; Lü; Zhi; Luo; Shan; and Tong. His younger brothers were Yu, Lian, Mian, and Yun. His wife was née Duan. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Yuankang was registered in a military household of the Xuanwu Guard in Henan and was a native of Xiaoyi County, Shanxi. He was an additional student at the Xiangfu county Confucian school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Liangfu. He ranked first in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxiang; his grandfather was Kuan; and his father was Hai. His father’s former wife was née Guo, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Wu. He placed seventeenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cao Dangmian, courtesy name Kexian, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, an assistant prefect; his grandfather was Ang; his father was Qian; and his mother was née She. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Dangxing, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked sixty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shiju, courtesy name Jinqing, was registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather was Ji; his father was Yi; his mother was née Li; and his stepmothers were née Zhang and née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiyong and Shizhong. His wife was née He; his subsequent wives were née He and née Dong. He ranked 104th in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yin, courtesy name Zongxia, was registered in a civilian household in Boye County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Wenqiang; and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Meng and Zhong, and his younger brothers were Mao and Wu. His wife was née Wang. He ranked sixteenth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Qingxiao, courtesy name Zixu, was a native of Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Chaogang; his father was Bi, an honorary official honored for longevity; and his mother was née Nie. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Pengxiao, a guard registrar, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李承緒〔貫江西吉安府永新縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字伯餘，行十五，年三十五，九月初一日生〕。曾祖景諤〔封禮部員外郎〕，祖瑞，父位，母朱氏。慈侍下，兄承勛、承芳、承業、承易、承重〔知縣〕，弟承度、承寵、承烈、承敬〔監生〕，娶龍氏。江西鄉試第十六名，會試第五十三名。

盛時選〔貫錦衣衛籍，直隸蘇州府吳縣人，國子生，治易經，字以仁，行二，年三十三，八月二十日生〕。曾祖芳〔恩例冠帶〕，祖玥，父巒〔教授〕，母毛氏。具慶下，兄時進，弟時聘、時通、時達、應霖，娶王氏，繼娶何氏。順天府鄉試第十九名，會試第二百六十七名。
translation_en:
Ren Weitang, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyang; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six (the transcription contains an extraneous は here [?]), born on the seventeenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Qing, and his father Mian, an Assistant Prefect; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Weijun, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his younger brothers were Weijian, Weiyue, and Weixuan. He married a woman née Jian. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Nayan, registered in a military household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jian, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Shu; and his father was Dong, a County Registrar. His mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengxu, registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boyu; he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jing'e, granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Rui; and his father was Wei. His mother was née Zhu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Chengxun, Chengfang, Chengye, Chengyi, and Chengzhong, a County Magistrate; his younger brothers were Chengdu, Chengchong, Chenglie, and Chengjing, a student of the Imperial University. He married a woman née Long. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Shixuan, registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yiren; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fang, granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under provisions of imperial grace; his grandfather was Yue; and his father was Luan, a Prefectural School Instructor. His mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shijin, and his younger brothers were Shipin, Shitong, Shida, and Yinglin. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née He. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

皮汝謙〔貫雲南蒙化衛軍籍，直隸廬州府六安縣人，河南羅山縣學教諭，治春秋，字子撝，行四，年三十五，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖守忠，祖成，父清，前母陳氏，母周氏。慈侍下。兄弁、冕、汝懋，弟汝修。娶宗氏，繼娶趙氏。雲南鄉試第三十三名，會試第二百五十二名。

柴宗義〔貫山西平陽府解州安邑縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子集，行一，年三十二，二月初三日生〕。曾祖肇祀，祖順，父梅，前母賈氏，母賈氏。具慶下。弟宗禮、宗信。娶李氏。山西鄉試第十五名，會試第一百二十七名。
translation_en:
Pi Ruqian, registered in a military household of Menghua Guard, Yunnan, was a native of Liu'an County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and served as Instructor in the county school of Luoshan, Henan. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zihui, and he ranked fourth in his family. He was thirty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouzhong, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Qing; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Bian, Mian, and Rumao, and his younger brother was Ruxiu. He married a woman née Zong and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-third in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Cheng, registered in a civilian household of Anyi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student at the school of the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zicheng, and he ranked second in his family. He was thirty, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Yanfang, his father Liangbi, and his mother née Zhao. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were E, an honorary official, Ren, and Zan; his younger brothers were Qian, Jin, and Gao. He married a woman née Guo. He placed forty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shangyi, registered in a military household of the Tengxiang Left Guard, was a native of Huai'an Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhifu, and he ranked second in his family. He was thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Ying, an Assistant Instructor, his father Shunqing, and his mother née Wang. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Lu and Shangli; his younger brothers were Shangzhong, Shangzhi, Shangwen, Shangxin, Shangde (尚得), and Shangde (尚德). He married a woman née Liu. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chai Zongyi, registered in a civilian household of Anyi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziji, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty-two, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhaosi, his grandfather Shun, and his father Mei; his father's former wife and his mother were both née Jia. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongli and Zongxin. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Yongchun, registered in Changyuan County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guo, his grandfather Xin, his father Ren, and his mother née Shao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yongnian, and his wife was née Miao. He placed ninety-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jian Da, registered in Chongqing Guard, Sichuan, belonged to an official household and was a Chongqing prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rushang; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-one years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather Tingxiang was posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of War; his father Laiyu was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Wang, held the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brothers were Qian, Zun, and Qiu. His wife was née Xu. He placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Xiu, registered in the Puzhou Defense Battalion, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a native of Linfen County. He was an attached student at the subprefectural school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Hongxian; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Ming held the honorary designation of Official of Righteousness, his father was Zisu, and his mother was née Lu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shao, Ji, Tong, Gang, and Shen; his younger brothers were Lun, Yi, Fang, and Cai. His wife was née Yang, and he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tian, registered in Nanyang Guard, Henan, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhonglong; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-four years old, born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Han was a Guard Commander, his grandfather was Zhe, his father Jixian, and his mother née Gao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Yang. He placed forty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王篆〔貫湖廣荊州府夷陵州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝文，行十五，年三十一，六月十五日生〕。曾祖傑〔府同知〕，祖璲〔左長史，進階通議大夫〕，父良策，嫡母張氏，生母王氏。具慶下，兄籥〔引禮官〕、籌、筆、符、䇠、簡、簿、笏，弟笈、答、晷、筵、策、籍、算、䈅、籲、節。娶段氏。湖廣鄉試第八十四名，會試第五十二名。

黃學海〔貫廣寧左屯衛，軍籍，直隸常州府無錫縣人，衛學生，治春秋，字宗于，行三，年二十八，七月十七日生〕。曾祖萱，祖坤〔贈監察御史〕，父正色〔前監察御史〕，母蕭氏〔封孺人〕，繼母薛氏。嚴侍下，兄學女、學道、學文、學夔、學詩、學易、學禮、學憲、學初、學亨、學書，弟學顏。娶龔氏。順天府鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百十四名。

郭夢得〔貫福建泉州府同安縣，鹽籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字甫卿，行二，年二十七，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖尚正〔壽官〕，祖世仰，父榜，前母葉氏，母吳氏。具慶下，兄仁春。娶劉氏。福建鄉試第八十三名，會試第九十一名。
translation_en:
Hou Sigu, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shirui; he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather, Ao, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Bi, was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Dai. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Shanggu, Haogu, Chonggu, Engu, and Guanggu. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhuan, registered in Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruwen; he ranked fifteenth in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Jie, was a Prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather, Sui, was a Left Administrator, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel; and his father was Liangce. His legal mother was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yue, a Ceremonial Usher, and Chou, Bi, Fu, Zhu (䇠), Jian, Bu, and Hu; his younger brothers were Ji, Da, Gui, Yan, Ce, Ji (籍), Suan, Yue (䈅) [?], Yu (籲), and Jie. He married a woman née Duan. He ranked eighty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xuehai was registered in the Guangning Left Garrison Guard in a military household and was originally from Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the guard school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zongyu; he ranked third in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Kun, was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; and his father, Zhengse, was a former Investigating Censor. His mother, née Xiao, had been granted the title Lady (ruren); his stepmother was née Xue. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Xuenü [?], Xuedao, Xuewen, Xuekui, Xueshi, Xueyi, Xueli, Xuexian, Xuechu, Xueheng, and Xueshu; his younger brother was Xueyan. He married a woman née Gong. He ranked thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Mengde, registered in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an auxiliary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Fuqing; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shangzheng, held an honorary official title awarded for longevity; his grandfather was Shiyang; and his father was Bang. His father's former wife was née Ye, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Renchun. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked eighty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.
