translation_en:
Hu Jia 胡價 was registered in Yicheng County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shizhong; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Qi, an honorary official for public benefaction; his father was Zhenpei, a Registrar in a Guard; and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wei 偉, Jie 价, and Zhuo 倬. His wife was née Gong. He placed fourteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Wenlong 史文龍 was registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yinglin; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Lun; his father was Shangcheng; and his mother was née Jiang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Wenfeng. His wife was née Jiang. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Tianfu 莫天賦 was registered in Haikang County, Leizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuliang; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Jiao; and his mother was née Tang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Tianxi and Tianmin, and his younger brother was Tianran. His wife was née Chen; his subsequent wife was also née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Yingchun 喬應春 was registered in the Wuxiang Left Guard in a household of brave warriors and was a native of Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Shuntian Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Renqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Cong; and his father was Wen, a Department Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingshi, Yingjie, and Yingguang. His wife was née Guo. He placed fiftieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Xuegu was registered in an artisan household in Chaoyi County, Tongzhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zihuo; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenmei; his grandfather was Kui, a prefectural Records Examiner; his father was Laizhao; and his mother was née Liang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Xueshi, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His younger brothers were Xuemeng, Xuemo (an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial), Xuewen, Xuemin, Xueban, Xuelang, Xueluo, and Xueyuan. His wife was née Li. He placed sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xuan was registered in an officer household of Changguo Guard, Zhejiang, and was a native of Xiangshan County, Ningbo Prefecture. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boxiang; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Shou, grandfather Ze, and father Mo were all Company Commanders; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lin, and his wife was née Tang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Fupin was registered in a commoner household in Zhouzhi County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shouzhen; he ranked fourth in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang; his grandfather was Ji; his father was Bei; his mother was née Yang; and his stepmother was née Tian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shenyuan, Laipin, and Tan; his younger brothers were Bingran, Huanran, and Fuchu. His wife was née Liu. He placed ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xiang was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mengli; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yugao; his grandfather was Wanping, granted the honorary title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Xuan, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Deng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gang (a student of the Directorate of Education), Ge (an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner), Hang, and De (a student of the Directorate of Education). His younger brothers were Shi (a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year), Cai (a metropolitan graduate of the present examination), Nan (a student of the Directorate of Education), Xuan (a Confucian scholar), Quan (a student admitted by imperial grace), and Zhen. His wife was née Xiong. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zong Hongxian, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jinfu. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue; his grandfather, Ren, was Office Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father, Mu, was an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Hongzao, Hongyuan, Hongshu, Hongxuan, and Hongdi, and his younger brothers were Hongqian and Hongxun. His wife was née Xu. He ranked eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Shangyi, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a supplementary student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ziren. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hu; his grandfather was Zhiren; and his father was Ruxian. His father's former wife was née Wang, his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmothers are listed as née Wu and née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chong, and his younger brother was Shangzhou. His wife was née Mei. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hua Qizhi, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Licheng. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Kai, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, En, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Shunqin, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Qian, was granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qizhong, and his younger brother was Qiduan. His wife was née Zhou. He ranked forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yingchun, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a supplementary student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Youhui. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deji; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Mengda; his mother was née Zhuo; and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingqiu, and his younger brothers were Yingxia, Yingshi, and Yingzhao. His wife was née Zheng. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

席上珍〔貫陝西漢中府南鄭縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字待聘，行一，年三十五，二月二十五日生〕。曾祖浩，祖孟華，父和，母陳氏。永感下，娶白氏，繼娶趙氏。陝西鄉試第二十七名，會試第八十九名。

殷登瀛〔貫直隸寧國府宣城縣，匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字子登，行十，年三十二，三月二十日生〕。曾祖仲昇〔壽官〕，祖崇德〔義官〕，父銘〔監生〕，母嵇氏。慈侍下，兄滄、滋，娶徐氏，繼娶貢氏。應天府鄉試第三十四名，會試第七名。

任春元〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治春秋，字長卿，行一，年三十二，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖澤，祖佐，父正，母潘氏。慈侍下，弟春和，娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第二十一名，會試第二十五名。

鄭欽〔貫直隸寧國府涇縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字堯卿，行一，年二十九，八月十七日生〕。曾祖逾，祖昌，父珏，母汪氏。具慶下，弟汝銳、鑛、銘、鎡、鉞、鎮、鏊，娶洪氏。應天府鄉試第一百十七名，會試第一百四十名。
translation_en:
Xi Shangzhen, courtesy name Daipin, was registered in Nanzheng County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Menghua; his father, He; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Bai and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Dengying, courtesy name Zideng, was registered in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, in an artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was tenth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongsheng, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather, Chongde, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his father, Ming, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Ji. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Cang and Zi. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Gong. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Chunyuan, courtesy name Changqing, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ze; his grandfather, Zuo; his father, Zheng; and his mother, née Pan. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His younger brother was Chunhe. He married a woman née Huang. He ranked twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Qin, courtesy name Yaoqing, was registered in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Chang; his father, Jue; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rurui [?], Kuang, Ming, Zi, Yue, Zhen, and Ao. He married a woman née Hong. He ranked one hundred seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
吳從憲〔貫福建泉州府晋江縣鹽籍，府學附學生，治易經，字惟時，行三，年三十二，二月初六日生〕。曾祖道，祖鑑，父希淵，母林氏。慈侍下，兄從寅，弟從悳、從寬，娶黃氏。福建鄉試第四十八名，會試第七十七名。

朱朋求〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字道元，行四，年二十九，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖顥〔府衞經歷〕，祖蕙〔衞經歷，贈工部郎中〕，父衮〔知府，進階亞中大夫〕，嫡母鄭氏〔封宜人〕，生母陳氏。具慶下，兄朋來〔太僕寺主簿〕、朋溪、朋良、朋信〔醫學官〕，弟朋樂〔監生〕，娶車氏，繼娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第十名，會試第一百三十九名。

王燮〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣匠籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字大理，行二十一，年三十四，十一月初一日生〕。曾祖鉞，祖瑾，父梗，母楊氏。具慶下，兄煒、熠，弟煚，娶許氏。浙江鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百九十名。

張國謙〔貫福建泉州府晋江縣民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字爾光，行二，年三十，十二月初七日生〕。曾祖茂成，祖纓，父仲賢，母陳氏。具慶下，兄國恒、國乾，弟國益、國履，娶王氏。福建鄉試第六十六名，會試第二百二十八名。
translation_en:
Wu Congxian, registered in a salt-producing household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Weishi, he ranked third in his family, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Dao, his grandfather Jian, and his father Xiyuan; his mother, née Lin, was living, while his father was deceased. His elder brother was Congyin, and his younger brothers were Congde and Congkuan; he married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Pengqiu, registered in a military household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Daoyuan, he ranked fourth in his family, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hao, a prefectural or guard Registrar [?]; his grandfather Hui was a guard Registrar, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Works; and his father Gun was a Prefect, advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master of the Lesser Center. His legal mother, née Zheng, held the title of Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Penglai, Chief Clerk of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Pengxi; Pengliang; and Pengxin, a medical official. His younger brother Pengle was a student of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Che and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xie, registered in an artisan household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dali, he ranked twenty-first in his family, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yue, his grandfather Jin, and his father Geng; his mother was née Yang, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wei and Yi, and his younger brother was Jiong; he married a woman née Xu. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Guoqian, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Erguang, he ranked second in his family, and he was aged thirty, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Maocheng, his grandfather Ying, and his father Zhongxian; his mother was née Chen, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guoheng and Guoqian (國乾), and his younger brothers were Guoyi and Guolü; he married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

龍光〔貫湖廣長沙衛軍籍，長沙府學增廣生，治詩經，字國華，行一，年三十四，二月初一日生〕。曾祖霄，祖世聰，父添鑾，母易氏。慈侍下，弟見，娶湯氏。湖廣鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百四十九名。

宋守約〔貫山西潞安府長治縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字崇要，行三，年三十三，三月初五日生〕。曾祖虎，祖大用，父文恭，母張氏。永感下，兄守宣〔散官〕、守曾，弟守孟，娶牛氏。山西鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百八十七名。
translation_en:
Zhou Shixuan, registered in a civilian household in Gucheng County, Jingzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenxian; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jia, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Liangzuo; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Xia. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Shimao, and his wife was née Huang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qi, registered in a military household in Xiajin County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zideng; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Zhang, and his father Jie; his mother was née Xiao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Jiao and She, his younger brothers Zhi and Fu, and his wife was née Gao. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Guang, registered in a military household of Changsha Guard, Huguang, was an added student of the Changsha prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guohua; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiao, his grandfather Shicong, and his father Tianluan; his mother was née Yi. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Jian, and his wife was née Tang. He placed seventy-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Shouyue, registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chongyao; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hu, his grandfather Dayong, and his father Wengong; his mother was née Zhang. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shouxuan〔a prestige official〕and Shouzeng, his younger brother Shoumeng, and his wife was née Niu. He placed forty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳謨〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字子嘉，行一，年二十八，七月二十二日生〕。曾祖孟春，祖珂，父仲載，母柴氏。慈侍下，弟諫，娶胡氏。湖廣鄉試第五名，會試第二百九十二名。
translation_en:
Liu Shiqiu, registered in an officer household of Pengcheng Guard and a native of Baodi County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yifu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhong, grandfather Feng, and father Chengzong were all Assistant Commanders; his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Respect, and his stepmother was née Yu. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Shichun, an Assistant Commander, and Shixia, and his wife was née Ni. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Guanghu, registered in a military household of Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongdu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather was Yue, and his father was Zhenzong, a student of the Directorate of Education; his legal mother was née Yao and his birth mother was née Li. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Guangzuo, Guangzhen, Guangxiang, and Guangzhi, and his wife was née Li. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Biao, registered in a military household of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yisheng, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, a District Magistrate, his grandfather was De, his father was Run, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Liang, and his wife was née Li. He placed twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Mo, registered in a civilian household of Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zijia, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengchun, his grandfather was Ke, his father was Zhongzai, and his mother was née Chai. His father was deceased and his mother was living; his younger brother was Jian, and his wife was née Hu. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

周寀〔貫江西吉安府安福縣民籍，府學附學生，治書經，字濟甫，行九，年二十二，二月十五日生〕。曾祖頡，祖愈〔壽官〕，父祺，母王氏。具慶下，兄進、造、邁、官、達、逢、商、道，弟述、徵、羽，娶王氏。江西鄉試第二十名，會試第七十三名。

丘承祖〔貫四川成都左護衛軍籍，成都府學生，治易經，字克紹，行二，年三十，十一月初三日生〕。曾祖達常，祖嵩，父岳，母金氏。具慶下，兄承業，弟承嗣，娶王氏，繼娶王氏。四川鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百九十五名。

張國彥〔貫直隸廣平府邯鄲縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字煕載，行四，年三十二，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖鸞，祖滕，父繡〔義官〕，前母李氏，母鄭氏。具慶下，兄國君〔散官〕、國臣、國士，娶蔚氏。順天府鄉試第六十二名，會試第四十九名。
translation_en:
Zhao Kerong, courtesy name Rucong, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan, and was a native of Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yicheng; his grandfather, Cong, was a Magistrate; his father was Yuanzhong; his mother was née Pang, and his stepmothers were née Wang and née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kejian and Kequan. He married a woman née Qiao and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Song. He placed sixty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Cai, courtesy name Jifu, was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was ninth in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather, Yu, held an honorary title conferred for longevity; his father was Qi, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Zao, Mai, Guan, Da, Feng, Shang, and Dao; his younger brothers were Shu, Zheng, and Yu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Chengzu, courtesy name Keshao, was registered in a military household of the Chengdu Left Escort Guard, Sichuan. A student of the Chengdu prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dachang; his grandfather was Song; his father was Yue, and his mother was née Jin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chengye, and his younger brother was Chengsi. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently married another woman née Wang. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Guoyan, courtesy name Xizai, was registered in a military household in Handan County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan; his grandfather was Teng; his father, Xiu, held an honorary title conferred for charitable contributions. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guojun, a prestige official, Guochen, and Guoshi. He married a woman née Wei. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhai Xiushang 翟繡裳, courtesy name Ruzhong, was registered in a military household in Wenxi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A government student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather, Liao; his father, Hua; his mother, née Ma; and his stepmother, née Zhang. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Jiao, and his wife was née Li. He ranked eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Sijin 黃思近, courtesy name Yuren, was registered in a civilian household in Nan'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student at the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuzu; his grandfather, Bangyin, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Zan, a Prefect; and his mother, née Qiu, granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sike and Sitong; his younger brothers were Sishu, an Imperial University student, and Sirang. His wife was née Hong. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wenmo 陳文謨, courtesy name Xianqing, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, a Vice Magistrate; his grandfather, Yu, also a Vice Magistrate; his father, Gui; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenyu, a Prefect; Jing, an Office Manager in the Ministry of Rites; Wenyan; Maoyi, an Administration Vice Commissioner; and Wenyi. His younger brothers were Wenji and Maoli, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His wife was née Xu. He ranked seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Jiyuan 鍾繼元, courtesy name Renqing, was registered in a civilian household in Tongxiang County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding; his grandfather, Yun, an Imperial University student; his father, De, an Assistant Instructor; his mother, née Zhao; and his stepmother, née Shi. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Jiheng and Jihe, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cheng Wenzhu, registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Meizhong; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sisheng, his grandfather Zhenqi, his father Tingji, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenzhang and Wenyuan, and his younger brothers Wenzhen and Wenyun. His wife was née Wang. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xiwen, registered in an artisan household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zongzhou; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingfu, his grandfather Zhen, his father Yaoqing, and his mother née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiwu, and his wife was née Sha. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shangxian, registered in a civilian household in Yongqing County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Junjin; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Chang, his father Bo, and his mother née He. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shangdeng, Shangke, and Shangxue, and his wife was née Yuan. He placed 117th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kejiu, registered in a military household in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhide; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Yu held an honorary rank for longevity; his grandfather Sizhong was posthumously appointed Magistrate; his father Zhi was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Liang, had been granted the title Lady for Service. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Keda and Kejiao, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
蕭大亨〔貫山東濟南府泰安州民籍，江西吉安府太和縣人，州學生，治書經，字夏卿，行二，三十一，三月初一日生〕。曾祖敘經，祖勝，父乾，母王氏。慈侍下，兄海、大元，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第六十六名，會試第二百六名。

王叔果〔貫浙江溫州府永嘉縣竈籍，國子生，治禮記，字陽德，行二，年三十六，三月十七日生〕。曾祖封，祖鉦〔封通政司右通政〕，父澈〔布政司左參議，贈朝議大夫〕，母潘氏〔贈恭人〕，繼母張氏〔封恭人〕。慈侍下，兄叔懋〔鴻臚寺署丞〕、叔杲〔布政司右參議〕，弟叔本〔恩生〕，娶吳氏，繼娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百三十五名。

王承芳〔貫陝西寧羌衛軍籍，西安府醴泉縣人，國子生，治詩經，字克濟，行一，年三十九，十月初十日生〕。曾祖讓，祖洪，父義，母孫氏。慈侍下，弟惟賓，娶嚴氏。陝西鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百六十名。

李苘〔貫山東青州府壽光縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字子藎，行三，年二十六，正月十七日生〕。曾祖忠，祖紳〔千戶〕，父校〔縣主簿〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄芝〔監生〕、芊、蓂，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第十三名，會試第二百三十八名。
translation_en:
Xiao Daheng, courtesy name Xiaqing, was registered in a civilian household in Tai’an Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong; his ancestral home was Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-one [?], and was born on the first day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xujing, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Qian; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Hai and Dayuan. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shuguo, courtesy name Yangde, was registered in a salt-producing household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the seventeenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather Zheng received the honorary title of Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission. His father Che was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner and was posthumously awarded the title Grand Master for Court Discussion. His mother, née Pan, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect; his stepmother, née Zhang, received the same title during her lifetime. His father was deceased, and his surviving mother was living. His elder brothers were Shumao, an Office Assistant in the Court of State Ceremonial, and Shugao, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; his younger brother Shuben was a student admitted by imperial favor. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chengfang, courtesy name Keji, was registered in a military household in Ningqiang Guard, Shaanxi; his ancestral home was Liquan County, Xi’an Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Hong, and his father Yi; his mother was née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Weibin, and his wife was née Yan. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qing, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in a military household in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An added-quota student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked third in birth order, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather Shen was a Battalion Commander, and his father Xiao was a County Registrar. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, a student of the Directorate of Education, Qian, and Ming. His wife was née Liu. He placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳鎮〔貫騰驤左衛軍籍，直隸蘇州府常熟縣人，順天府學附學生，治易經，字子靜，行二，年二十四，十月初七日生〕。曾祖啟，祖璽，父思誠，母王氏。具慶下，兄鐸、欽、鑭，弟鈐，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第百十二名，會試第二百十七名。

李學思〔貫直隸保定府易州民籍，國子生，治書經，字充道，行三，年三十五，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖佑〔監生〕，祖穆，父冠〔教授〕，母黃氏。慈侍下，兄學顏、學曾，弟學孟，娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第五十九名，會試第二百四十八名。
translation_en:
Lei Dazhuang, courtesy name Qinlü, was registered in a civilian household in Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Tai, was a master in a School of Yin and Yang; his father was Ping, and his mother was née Tian. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Dayou, Daxu, and Daqian, and his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Chongdao, courtesy name Weizheng, was registered in a civilian household in Fei County, Yizhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Wenyou, was posthumously granted the title of Guard Registrar; his grandfather, Qi, was a Guard Registrar; and his father, Shen, was a Department Magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Yan. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Chongru, Chongxin, Chonggui, Chongxue (a student of the Directorate of Education), Chongli, Chongle (an annual tribute student), Chongwen (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Chongwu. His wife was née Dong. He placed forty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhen, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in a military household of the Tengxiang Left Guard and was a native of Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather, Xi; his father, Sicheng; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Duo, Qin, and Lan; his younger brother was Qian; and his wife was née Wang. He placed 112th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xuesi, courtesy name Chongdao, was registered in a civilian household in Yizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, You, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather was Mu; his father, Guan, was a Prefectural School Instructor; and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xueyan and Xuezeng; his younger brother was Xuemeng; and his wife was née Zhao. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
李崧〔貫陝西秦州衛軍籍，西安府咸寧縣人，秦州學生，治《詩經》，字應嶽，行一，年三十三，七月初五日生。〕曾祖華，祖杲，父侍祥，母張氏。具慶下，弟岑，娶鄭氏。陝西鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百四十名。

王之垣〔貫山東濟南府新城縣匠籍，縣學生，治《詩經》，字爾式，行二，年三十四，六月二十五日生。〕曾祖伍，祖麟〔教授，贈戶部主事〕，父重光〔布政司左參議〕，母劉氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，兄之翰〔監生〕，弟之干〔貢士〕、之城、之猷、之棟，娶于氏。山東鄉試第七名，會試第一百七十九名。

楊子實〔貫直隸河間府河間縣民籍，縣學附學生，治《易經》，字中孚，行一，年三十一，十二月二十五日生。〕曾祖健〔州判官〕，祖緯，父時利，母陳氏。具慶下，兄子成，弟子明、子通，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百十五名，會試第二百五十名。

李貞元〔貫湖廣德安府應山縣軍籍，縣學生，治《詩經》，字淳甫，行五，年三十二，十二月二十一日生。〕曾祖通，祖邦厚，父麟，母戴氏。具慶下，兄承元、粹元、肇元、秉元，弟時元、敏元，娶裴氏。湖廣鄉試第九十名，會試第二百九十六名。
translation_en:
Li Song, courtesy name Yingyue, was registered in a military household of Qinzhou Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture. A student of the Qinzhou school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hua, his grandfather Gao, his father Shixiang, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living. His younger brother was Cen, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhiyuan, courtesy name Ershi, was registered in an artisan household in Xincheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu; his grandfather Lin was an Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father Chongguang was a Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother, née Liu, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Zhihan was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Zhigan, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Zhicheng, Zhiyou, and Zhidong. His wife was née Yu. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zishi, courtesy name Zhongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jian was a Department Judge; his grandfather was Wei, his father Shili, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zicheng, his younger brothers Ziming and Zitong, and his wife née Li. He placed 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhenyuan, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a military household in Yingshan County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Banghou, his father Lin, and his mother née Dai; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengyuan, Cuiyuan, Zhaoyuan, and Bingyuan, and his younger brothers Shiyuan and Minyuan. His wife was née Pei. He placed ninetieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

周希旦〔貫直隸寧國府旌德縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字汝魯，行一，年三十，五月初四日生〕。曾祖伯諒，祖志德，父世祿，母汪氏。具慶下，弟希望、希召、希高、希榮，娶郭氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十二名，會試第九十九名。

郭諫臣〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字子忠，行一，年三十四，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖澄，祖璇，父堂，母奚氏。具慶下，兄澤臣，弟輔臣、世臣，娶徐氏。順天府鄉試第四十二名，會試第三十七名。

李畿嗣〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄水縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字明卿，行二，年三十一，八月初十日生〕。曾祖宗本，祖大睦，父美，母何氏。慈侍下，兄邦嗣，弟龍嗣、豸嗣、祖嗣、紳嗣，娶黃氏。湖廣鄉試第六名，會試第二百九十九名。

滕伯輪〔貫福建建寧府甌寧縣軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字汝載，行五，年三十四，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖庸，祖澍〔州同知〕，父鶴齡〔通判〕，母陳氏。永感下，兄伯棠，娶楊氏。福建鄉試第五十九名，會試第二百六十二名。
translation_en:
Zhou Xidan 周希旦, courtesy name Rulu, was registered in a civilian household in Jingde County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an auxiliary student of the county school, specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty, born on the fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Boliang, his grandfather Zhide, his father Shilu, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Xiwang, Xizhao, Xigao, and Xirong; his wife was née Guo; he placed 132nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 99th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Jianchen 郭諫臣, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a military household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Xuan, his father Tang, and his mother née Xi; both parents were living; his elder brother was Zechen and his younger brothers Fuchen and Shichen; his wife was née Xu; he placed 42nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 37th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jisi 李畿嗣, courtesy name Mingqing, was registered in a military household in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang; he was an auxiliary student of the county school, specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second in birth order, and was aged thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zongben, his grandfather Damu, his father Mei, and his mother née He; his mother alone was living; his elder brother was Bangsi and his younger brothers Longsi, Zhisi, Zusi, and Shensi; his wife was née Huang; he placed sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Teng Bolun 滕伯輪, courtesy name Ruzai, was registered in a military household in Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian; he was a student of the county school, specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked fifth in birth order, and was aged thirty-four, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Shu (Vice Magistrate of a subprefecture), his father Heling (Assistant Prefect), and his mother née Chen; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Botang; his wife was née Yang; he placed 59th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
王廷簡〔貫四川邛州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字汝迪，行一，年三十二，五月初十日生〕。曾祖大端，祖禮冠〔壽官〕，父聘〔監生〕，嫡母李氏，繼母劉氏、彭氏，生母李氏。慈侍下。弟廷符、廷節、廷籌。娶徐氏，繼娶姚氏、余氏。四川鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百十二名。

陳大壯〔貫直隸揚州府通州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字思立，行二，年二十八，二月二十九日生〕。曾祖純德，祖尚忠〔贈工部主事〕，父冠〔七品散官〕，母王氏。重慶下。兄大震，弟大科〔貢士〕、大益、大乾、大器、大升。娶成氏。應天府鄉試第六十九名，會試第二百八名。

李勲〔貫旗手衛軍籍，山東德州衛人，國子生，治詩經，字世臣，行一，年三十三，八月初四日生〕。曾祖貴，祖龍，父鸞，母邵氏。慈侍下。兄安〔百戶〕，弟默。娶張氏，繼娶王氏、鄭氏。順天府鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百八十三名。

張應福〔貫直隸大名府魏縣民籍，山西潞安府襄垣縣人，縣學生，治春秋，字子承，行一，年三十五，十二月二十三日生〕。曾祖泰，祖武，父惟高〔壽官〕，母常氏。具慶下。弟應祿、應禎、應祚。娶崔氏，繼娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第十名，會試第二百九十九名。
translation_en:
Wang Tingjian, courtesy name Rudi, held civilian registration in Qiongzhou, Sichuan, and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daduan; his grandfather, Liguan, held an honorary title for longevity; and his father, Pin, was an Imperial University student. His father's principal wife was née Li; his stepmothers were née Liu and née Peng; and his birth mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Tingfu, Tingjie, and Tingchou. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently women née Yao and née Yu. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dazhuang, courtesy name Sili, held civilian registration in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chunde; his grandfather, Shangzhong, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father, Guan, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Dazhen, and his younger brothers were Dake, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi), Dayi, Daqian, Daqi, and Dasheng. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xun, courtesy name Shichen, held military registration in the Standard Bearer Guard and was a native of Dezhou Guard, Shandong. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Long; his father, Luan; and his mother, née Shao. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was An, a Company Commander, and his younger brother was Mo. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently women née Wang and née Zheng. He placed eighty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yingfu, courtesy name Zicheng, held civilian registration in Wei County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Xiangyuan County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai; his grandfather, Wu; his father, Weigao, who held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother, née Chang. Both his parents were living. His younger brothers were Yinglu, Yingzhen, and Yingzuo. He married a woman née Cui and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhong Chongwen 鍾崇文, courtesy name Zhongmo, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuxian; his grandfather, Guang; his father, Ren; and his mother, née Tian. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother Chongwu was a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. He married a woman née Wan. He placed thirty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rao Renkan 饒仁侃, courtesy name Jingang, was registered in a military household in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. An added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked seventh in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qingshou; his grandfather, Mengzhao; his father, Cang; and his mother, née Sun. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Renru, Renjia, Renfeng, Renjie, Renshi, and Renguan; his younger brother was Renyi. He married a woman née Xu. He placed thirty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yumao 楊愈茂, courtesy name Borong, was registered in a civilian household in Anhua County, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in his family and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ao; his grandfather, Qi; and his father, Zhongchen, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His father’s former wife was née She, and his mother was née He. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yugao, an unranked administrative official, and Yuqiao; his younger brothers were Yuchang and Yusheng. He married a woman née He. He placed sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Gu 鍾穀, courtesy name Xinqing, was registered in an artisan household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shao; his grandfather, Zhen; and his father, Xiang. His father’s former wife was née Shen, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dehua, Dejun (an official awaiting selection for appointment), Dezhou, Deliang, and Decheng; his younger brothers were Dewei and De’ai. He married a woman née Gu. He placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Niu Yinglong 牛應龍 was registered in a civilian household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Shijian and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-nine years old, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather, Fu, was an Instructor in Yin-yang Studies; and his father, Kongchang, was a County Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Zheng, and his stepmothers were née Zhao and née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Youlong, a National University student; Yingjiao; Yulong, a National University student; Tengjiao; Panlong; and Ruilong. He married a woman née Su and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Tingzhi 陳廷芝 was registered in a military household of the Zhongyi Rear Guard and was a native of Huang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An attached student at the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Jixin and ranked second among his brothers. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Gui, was a County Registrar; his grandfather was Zong, and his father was Xiong. His legal mother was née Sun, and his birth mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Tinglan. He married a woman née Ou. He placed 135th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan 張峘 was registered in a civilian household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zijing and ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather was Jie, and his father was Yuanshan. His mother was née Sun, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His mother was deceased, and he attended his surviving father. His elder brothers were Qi and Bo, and his younger brothers were Lun and Dong. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tai 朱泰 was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Liangfu and ranked seventeenth among his brothers. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather was Xu, and his father was Rui. His mother was née Fan. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Fan. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

周思充〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，治書經，字道可，行十一，生二十九，八月十五日生〕，縣學生。曾祖雲，祖景〔贈監察御史〕，父如斗〔巡撫應天都察院右僉都御史〕，母毛氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母張氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄思齊〔貢士〕，弟思彥〔監生〕、思彰〔監生〕、思顏、思曜、思亨，娶夏氏。浙江鄉試第五名，會試第一百六十六名。

劉繼文〔貫直隸鳳陽府宿州靈璧縣民籍，治易經，字永謨，行一，生三十二，五月二十三日生〕，國子生。曾祖通〔遞運所大使〕，祖鎔，父貞，母黃氏。慈侍下，兄繼□，娶王氏，繼娶王氏。應天府鄉試第一百二名，會試第一百二十三名。
translation_en:
Qiu Teng, courtesy name Ziyun, was a student of the prefectural school of Mianyang subprefecture, Chengtian prefecture, Huguang, registered in a military household. He specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked second in birth order, and was aged twenty-six [?]; he was born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sixian, his grandfather Rong, and his father Fu; his father's former wife was née Tang, and his mother was née Yang. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Peng and Sheng, and his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Qi, courtesy name Jizhi, was a county-school student from Daning county, Kuizhou prefecture, Sichuan, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second in birth order, and was aged thirty-five [?]; he was born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Chun was a Command Registrar in a guard; his grandfather was Heng, his father Tingjie, and his mother née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Guang and his younger brother Jie; his wife was née Zheng. He placed forty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Sichong, courtesy name Daoke, was a county-school student from Yuyao county, Shaoxing prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked eleventh in birth order, and was aged twenty-nine [?]; he was born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather Jing was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; and his father Rudou was Grand Coordinator of Yingtian and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Mao, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his stepmother, née Zhang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother Siqi was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Siyan and Sizhang, both Imperial University students, and Siyan (思顏), Siyao, and Siheng. His wife was née Xia. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jiwen, courtesy name Yongmo, was an Imperial University student from Lingbi county, Su subprefecture, Fengyang prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-two [?]; he was born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Tong was Chief of a Transport Office; his grandfather was Rong, his father Zhen, and his mother née Huang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Ji□. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was also née Wang. He placed 102nd in the Yingtian Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

鄧宗孔〔貫廣西太平府崇善縣民籍，府學生，治書經，字惟時，行一，年三十五，十月初四日生〕。曾祖襃，祖政，父召高〔監生〕，母歐氏，繼母方氏。慈侍下，娶岑氏。廣西鄉試第十六名，會試第二百七十五名。

齊康〔貫直隸廣平府永年縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字太和，行一，年三十七，六月二十八日生〕。曾祖盤，祖復勝，父祥，母陳氏。具慶下，弟唐、賡。娶張氏，繼娶李氏。順天府鄉試第二十八名，會試第七十名。

張應治〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣民籍，嘉興縣人，府學生，治書經，字體徵，行二，年二十九，四月初十日生〕。曾祖正，祖世華〔壽官〕，父用，母王氏。具慶下，兄應潮，弟應源、應浚、應濂、應滂。娶錢氏。浙江鄉試第二十四名，會試第八十五名。
translation_en:
Zhang Shouzhong, courtesy name Shuyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Southern Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Sheng; and his father, 𨌆 [reading uncertain], a department magistrate. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Quan, Jun, and Dan, the last a censor; his younger brothers were Shouqian, Shouzheng, Shoufu (守俌), Shoutai, and Shoufu (守甫). He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed ninety-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Zongkong, courtesy name Weishi, was registered in a civilian household in Chongshan County, Taiping Prefecture, Guangxi. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Bao; his grandfather, Zheng; and his father, Zhaogao, a student of the Directorate of Education. His mother was née Ou, and his stepmother née Fang. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Cen. He placed sixteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Kang, courtesy name Taihe, was registered in a civilian household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, Northern Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Pan; his grandfather, Fusheng; his father, Xiang; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tang and Geng. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yingzhi, courtesy name Tizheng, was registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Jiaxing County. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Shihua, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Yong; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingchao; his younger brothers were Yingyuan, Yingjun, Yinglian, and Yingpang. He married a woman née Qian. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ling Guan 凌琯, courtesy name Weihe, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers, was forty years old, and was born on the eighth day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was You; his grandfather, Shesun; his father, Xiang; and his mother, née Jiang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Huan, Chong, Lang, and Wei. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Hong. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yan 趙岩, courtesy name Weishi, was registered in a civilian household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An added-quota student at the county school of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather, Sheng; his father, Cong; and his mother, née Shen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Feng, Gang, and Lun. He married a woman née Pan. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenming 張問明, courtesy name Ziming, was registered in a salt-producing household in Yishi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather, Ru, a County Registrar; his father, Jiahui; and his mother, née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenxing, and his younger brothers were Wenshi, Wenzheng, Wendao, and Wenda. He married a woman née He and subsequently a woman née Zheng. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Jiong 仇炅, courtesy name Wengang, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked seventh among his brothers, was forty-two years old, and was born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yong, who held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Hong; his father, Huan, a National University student; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers are listed as Xun, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Xiu; Jiong 熲; Xi; Feng, a tribute scholar; Guang; and Tuan. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

唐鍊〔貫湖廣常德衛，官籍，常德府學生，治春秋，字純之，行四，年三十五，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖叔謙，祖璽，父杲，母王氏。具慶下，弟鑄、鑛，娶胡氏。湖廣鄉試第八十一名，會試第二百二十二名。
translation_en:
Wang Jiabin, registered in Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Guoguang, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Mei, his father Tianxu, and his mother née Cheng; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Yuanbin and Libin, and his wife was née Zhang; he placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wenchen, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zhengshu, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ze, his grandfather Yi, his father Ming, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Wenren, Wenru, and Wenchong, and he married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Wu; he placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Wenwei, registered in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongtao, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Ji, his father Hui, and his mother née Men; both parents were deceased, and his wife was née Guo; he placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Lian, registered in Changde Guard, Huguang, belonged to an official household and was a Changde prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Chunzhi, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuqian, his grandfather Xi, his father Gao, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Zhu and Kuang, and his wife was née Hu; he placed eighty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

馬明謨〔貫直隸廣平府廣平縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字君獻，行二，年二十八，九月十七日生〕。曾祖雲，祖進，父人慈〔學正〕，母潘氏。慈侍下，兄明典，弟明命，娶張氏，繼娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第一百十名，會試第二百七十一名。

郭崇嗣〔貫直隸廣平府肥鄉縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字承芳，行一，年三十，二月十二日生〕。曾祖忠〔知府，贈中憲大夫〕，祖郛〔監察御史〕，父東，母王氏。慈侍下，兄崇登〔醫官〕，弟崇教，娶白氏。順天府鄉試第十六名，會試第一百七十七名。
translation_en:
Xu Tianqi, courtesy name Dazheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in family birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiong, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Bin; his father was Yuangao; and his mother was née Qiu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Tianxiang and Zongcheng, the latter a government student; his younger brothers were Tianlang and Zonglun. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shang, courtesy name Zhibo, was registered in a military household in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family birth order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dezhong; his grandfather was Rizu; his father was Xing; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Laixiang, and his wife was née Zeng. He placed thirty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Mingmo, courtesy name Junxian, was registered in a civilian household in Guangping County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in family birth order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Renci, an Instructor; and his mother was née Pan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Mingdian, and his younger brother was Mingming. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Chongsi, courtesy name Chengfang, was registered in a civilian household in Feixiang County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a Prefect posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Constitutional Service; his grandfather was Fu, an Investigating Censor; his father was Dong; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Chongdeng, a Medical Officer, and his younger brother was Chongjiao. His wife was née Bai. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Song 李松, courtesy name Zijie, was registered in a civilian household in Dacheng County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather, Xiang; and his father, Huai, a County Registrar. His mother was née Jiao, and his stepmother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother still living. He married a woman née Pei. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lun Wen 倫文, courtesy name Shaozhou, was registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jilin; his grandfather, Zhi; his father, Kesheng; and his mother, née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother still living. His younger brothers were Yu 畬 and Qian 僉. He married a woman née Ou. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Jinkui 馬近奎, courtesy name Wenzheng, was registered in a civilian household in Guichi County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhang; his grandfather, Lun; and his father, Si. His mother was née Jiang, and his stepmother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother still living. His younger brothers were Jinlin and Jinqiao. He married a woman née He. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Zeyi 高則益, courtesy name Ruqian, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenjian; his grandfather, Jiyao, a Prefectural Judge; his father, Qixin, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zedui and Zexun, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brother was Zeshun. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Zhenzong, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Desheng, and he ranked first in family birth order. He was thirty-eight, born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chonggao, his grandfather Fu, his father Rong, and his mother née Yang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Jing, Qian, and Hou; his younger brothers were Yangzong (a military jinshi), Gongzong, Huizong, and Tingzong. He married a woman née Yang. He placed seventy-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yangda, registered in Suiyang Guard, Henan, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Suizhou government school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zili, and he ranked second in family birth order. He was thirty, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Tong, his father Han (a School Instructor), and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yangxiang (a student of the Directorate of Education); his younger brothers were Yanglian, Yangmeng, Yangzheng, and Yangfu. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed seventeenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Tijing, registered in Taigu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Keli, and he ranked first in family birth order. He was thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan, his grandfather Zhongfang, his father Qing, and his mother née Duan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Tigong and Tishu. He married a woman née Wu. He placed fifty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fan, registered in Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shihong, and he ranked third in family birth order. He was thirty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuming, his grandfather Xun, his father Zhongjia, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Lu and his younger brother Zhe. He married a woman née He. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Shikong, registered in a civilian household in Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a supplementary student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixiao; he ranked first in family seniority and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Biao, his father Jue, and his mother née Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased; his wife was née Zhang. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mu Wenxi, registered in a military household in Dongming County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked first in family seniority and was aged thirty, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Jin, his father Chenshi, and his mother née Tao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Nan, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed eighty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yijing, registered in a civilian household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yonghan; he ranked fifteenth in family seniority and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junzhang, his grandfather Ji, his father Su, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yicheng. His wife was née Tan; he subsequently married a woman née Mao. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wensui, registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruxiang; he ranked ninth in family seniority and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuchu, his grandfather Ji, his father Xing, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chi; his younger brothers were Wenhuang, Wenhuan〔tribute scholar (gongshi)〕, Wenyu, and Wenzhao. His wife was née Shuai. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.
