translation_en:
Wei Ruyi, courtesy name Zixing, was registered in a military household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked sixth in the family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather, Zan, was a County Magistrate; his father, Hongren, was also a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Rufu, Rubi, Ruji, Rucheng, and Ruzuo; his younger brothers were Rudeng, Ruke, Rugong, Rumei, Rugou, Ru𦶜 [second character’s reading uncertain], and Rubian. His wife was née Tian. He placed fifty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Nian, courtesy name Zishi, was registered in a civilian household in Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and was a native of Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked first in the family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the thirtieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Zuo, held an honorary office for longevity and was posthumously granted the title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works; his father, Li, was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works. His father’s former wife, née Huo, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Fan, Shi, Ren, and Zai; his younger brothers were Zhen, Gu, Ni, Yue, and Fu. His wife was née Ding. He placed seventy-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shanyan, courtesy name Ziyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Cheng’an County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in the family and was aged twenty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather, Ming; his father, Yuan; and his mother, née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dao, Tian, Le, and Qin. His wife was née Shi. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Wenwei, courtesy name Weizheng, was registered in an official household of the Dingliao Rear Guard in Liaodong and was a native of Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A school student of the Liaodong Regional Military Commission specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked fifth in the family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather, Cong, was posthumously granted the title of Subprefect; and his father, Tang, was a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His father’s former wife, née Miao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Sun, was granted the same title; and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun, Wenxie, Wenshou, who was a Battalion Disciplinary Officer, Wenqi, and Wenchun; his younger brother was Wencai. His wife was née Zhang. He placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟自昔
帝王莫聖於堯舜
史稱堯舜垂衣裳
而天下治矣然當
其時下民猶咨洚
===
水為灾有苗弗率
則猶有未盡治平
者豈二帝固弗之
恤歟抑其臣任之
於下而上可以無

translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: “I consider that, among the emperors and kings of antiquity, none surpassed Yao and Shun in sagehood. The historical records state that Yao and Shun let their robes hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed. Yet in their time the common people still lamented, floods caused devastation, and the Youmiao would not submit. Thus there remained matters in which good government and peace had not been fully achieved. Could it be that these two emperors were truly unconcerned about them? Or did their ministers assume responsibility below, so that the ruler above could refrain from …

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
為不然何以垂衣
而治也三代莫盛
於成周宣王中興
詩稱召伯平淮夷
方叔征蠻荆吉甫
===
伐玁狁惟得其人
以分命之是以不
勞而治朕常嘉之
甚慕之朕撫天下
四十有一年于此

臣對臣聞帝王之御極也體君道以奉天心
而後可以建久安長治之業肅臣紀以奉天
職而後可以成內修外攘之功何則人君者
天之所授以統一萬方而臨馭兆民者也其
位尊其任重故君道常主乎逸人臣者天之
所命以左右一人而分理庶政者也其分卑
其事蹟故臣道常主乎勞君能奉天以端拱
於上而以其事責諸臣則無爲而化成不言
而功著若於穆之運玄機之宰不假於推遷
===

安長治之業可建也臣能奉君以奔走於下
而以其身致之君則同心以共濟協忠以體
國若四時之佐五行之吏各效其宣布之能
而罔有違天者矣是謂能奉天職而內修外
攘之功可成也不然則一人之身萬幾攸萃
安能一一而理之而庶官之衆各有司存能

和氣溢而宇宙清寧理道昌而民物康乂順

translation_en:
Your servant Xu Shixing.

Your servant replies: I have heard that when emperors occupy the supreme throne, only by embodying the Way of the ruler to honor Heaven’s intent can they establish lasting peace and enduring government; only by enforcing discipline among their ministers to fulfill Heaven’s charge can they achieve good order within and repel threats from without. Why is this? The ruler is one whom Heaven has invested with authority to unite the myriad regions and govern the countless people. His position is exalted and his responsibility weighty; thus the Way of the ruler rests principally upon repose. Ministers are those whom Heaven has appointed to assist the One Man and share the administration of the many affairs of government. Their station is subordinate, and their duties are [?]; thus the Way of the minister rests principally upon toil. If the ruler can serve Heaven by sitting upright with folded hands above, while holding his ministers responsible for their tasks, transformation will be accomplished without his acting, and achievements will become manifest without his speaking. He will resemble the workings of profound Heaven and the governance of its mysterious mechanism, which naturally brings things into being without requiring the exertion of moving them along. This is what it means to honor Heaven’s intent, whereby lasting peace and enduring government can be established. If ministers can serve their ruler by exerting themselves below and devoting their persons to him, they will work with one mind toward common accomplishment and unite in loyalty to care for the state. They will resemble the assistants of the four seasons and the officers of the Five Phases, each exercising its capacity to disseminate Heaven’s operations, with none acting contrary to Heaven. This is what it means to fulfill Heaven’s charge, whereby good order within and the repulsion of threats from without can be achieved. Otherwise, when the myriad affairs of government converge upon the person of the One Man, how can he manage them individually? And how can the multitude of officials, each with his assigned responsibilities, avoid the blame of neglecting their offices? Thus the ruler must lead his ministers in seeking lasting peace and enduring government, and ministers must assist their ruler in achieving good order within and repelling threats from without. Then harmonious influences will abound and the universe will be clear and peaceful; the Way of good government will flourish, and the people and all things will enjoy well-being and order; orderly …

…worthy are the limbs; all affairs prosper!” This means that when an enlightened ruler stands above and worthy ministers assist him, all affairs can be properly ordered. It also says: “Heaven hears and sees; the sage takes this as his model; ministers reverently follow.” This means that when the ruler models himself on Heaven, those who serve as ministers naturally obey him with reverence, none daring to act contrary to him. Thus the ruler, as the head, models himself on Heaven above. Taking Heaven as his model in hearing, he dwells on high yet hears those below, and can sit and hear all under Heaven without toil. Taking Heaven as his model in vision, he shines resplendently upon those below, and can sit and illuminate the four quarters without toil. Thus the ruler follows Heaven’s Way [?] through nonaction. Ministers, as the limbs, reverently obey below. Exercising the ruler’s hearing on his behalf, they ensure that information about every benefit and affliction in the realm reaches him without obstruction. Exercising his vision on his behalf, they thoroughly discern the people’s joys and sorrows, overlooking nothing. Thus ministers carry out Heaven’s appointed duties through active service.
Therefore, in the age of Tang and Yu, the myriad states were brought into harmony, the four quarters were stirred as by the wind, and an age of luminous culture flourished. Yao and Shun, rulers whose hearing and vision attained the utmost sageliness, silently conducted government through nonaction. They also had such ministers as Yu, Gao, Ji, Xie, and Bo Yi to assist together in the work of bringing about Great Peace. When the common people lamented, when the flood brought disaster, and when the Miao refused obedience, it was not that Yao and Shun were unconcerned. Rather, their loyal and worthy assistants were sufficient to further their imperial plans, and their close ministers, who corrected and guided them, were sufficient to extend the imperial Way. To relieve those afflicted by hunger, there were ministers who nurtured all; to rescue those submerged in the flood, there were ministers capable of tireless exertion; to bring into submission those who relied on their strongholds, there were ministers who furthered the rulers’ virtue. These ministers served their rulers as they served Heaven. Diligently, with shared reverence and united respect, none dared to be idle or take his ease. Thus, although Yao and Shun had cares that delayed their meals until late in the day, yet…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
終得以享垂衣之治至今稱中天之盛者必
曰唐虞此堯舜得臣之明驗也周宣之世海
內乂安矣國勢寢隆矣文武之業復矣宣王
以聰明有道之君嗣守無疆之業而又有召
虎方叔吉甫之臣夾輔中興之治故淮夷之
猖亂也荆蠻之不靖也獫狁之虔劉也宣王
非不之慮也惟其位元宰者才兼乎文武總
元戎者勳聯乎將相有宣威江漢之臣而淮
夷率俾有壮猷南國之臣而荆蠻来威有薄
伐太原之臣而獫狁于襄諸臣者其事君亦
===
如事天也惴惴焉矢心協力罔敢戲豫也故
宣王有繼述之思而終以成再造之績至今
稱中興之盛者必曰成周此宣王得臣之明
驗也堯舜宣王之為君法天道以無為而唐
虞成周之臣奉天職以有事則所以建久安
長治之業成內修外攘之功者豈偶然哉臣
伏觀
陛下臨御以来四十有一年矣
上帝之申眷不為不隆而誠敬愈篤
祖宗之成業不為不固而仁孝愈純

punctuated:
終得以享垂衣之治。至今稱中天之盛者，必曰唐虞，此堯舜得臣之明驗也。周宣之世，海內乂安矣，國勢寢隆矣，文武之業復矣。宣王以聰明有道之君，嗣守無疆之業，而又有召虎、方叔、吉甫之臣，夾輔中興之治。故淮夷之猖亂也，荆蠻之不靖也，獫狁之虔劉也，宣王非不之慮也。惟其位元宰者，才兼乎文武；總元戎者，勳聯乎將相。有宣威江漢之臣，而淮夷率俾；有壮猷南國之臣，而荆蠻来威；有薄伐太原之臣，而獫狁于襄。諸臣者，其事君亦如事天也，惴惴焉矢心協力，罔敢戲豫也。故宣王有繼述之思，而終以成再造之績。至今稱中興之盛者，必曰成周，此宣王得臣之明驗也。堯舜宣王之為君，法天道以無為，而唐虞成周之臣，奉天職以有事，則所以建久安長治之業，成內修外攘之功者，豈偶然哉？
臣伏觀陛下臨御以来，四十有一年矣。上帝之申眷，不為不隆，而誠敬愈篤；祖宗之成業，不為不固，而仁孝愈純。
translation_en:
…in the end they were able to enjoy government in which they merely let their robes hang down, ruling without exertion. To this day, those who speak of an age of supreme flourishing invariably name Tang and Yu, the eras of Yao and Shun. This is clear proof that Yao and Shun obtained worthy ministers.
In the time of King Xuan of Zhou, all within the seas was orderly and peaceful, the strength of the state gradually increased, and the achievements of Kings Wen and Wu were restored. An intelligent and enlightened ruler who followed the Way, King Xuan inherited and preserved an enduring royal enterprise. He also had ministers such as Shao Hu, Fang Shu, and Jifu to assist him in restoring good government. Thus, when the Huai Yi rose in disorder, the Jing Man remained unsettled, and the Xianyun wrought slaughter, it was not that King Xuan felt no concern. Rather, those who occupied the position of chief minister possessed both civil and military talents, while those who commanded the great armies combined the meritorious achievements of generals and chief ministers. There was a minister who displayed royal might in the Jiang and Han regions, and the Huai Yi submitted; there was a minister whose mighty plans extended to the southern lands, and the Jing Man came in awe; there was a minister who campaigned at Taiyuan, and the Xianyun were driven away. These ministers, too, served their ruler as they served Heaven. In anxious vigilance, they pledged their hearts and joined their efforts, never daring to indulge in amusement or ease. Thus King Xuan, intent on continuing and carrying forward his predecessors’ work, ultimately accomplished the restoration of the dynasty. To this day, those who speak of the splendor of a restoration invariably name the Zhou. This is clear proof that King Xuan obtained worthy ministers.
As rulers, Yao, Shun, and King Xuan modeled themselves on the Way of Heaven and governed without exertion, while the ministers of Tang, Yu, and Zhou fulfilled their Heaven-appointed duties through active service. Could it, then, have been mere chance that they established lasting peace and enduring good government, and achieved both internal cultivation and the repulsion of external threats?
Your servant humbly observes that it has now been forty-one years since Your Majesty ascended the throne. The Supreme Lord’s repeated favor has been abundant, yet your sincerity and reverence grow ever deeper; the enterprise established by your ancestors has been secure, yet your benevolence and filial devotion grow ever purer.

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
欽天有記以表昭事之忱
祖德有詩以發聿追之念至於慮切民恫任專吏
職内責成於守令矣而巡督之臣歲不絕遣
外付托於將帥矣而總制之命任必加隆無
一念不在於民瘼無一言不軫乎國慮臣有
以仰窺
陛下之心即堯舜之心而周宣不足侔也於今諸
瑞咸集四靈畢至固足以彰
陛下之峻德鴻勳超卓百代矣然淫潦為灾則塍
畦有墊溺之苦亢旱為虐則阡陌有枯槁之
===
憂倭夷竊發於東南而海波弗靖醜虜跳梁
於西北而邊塵屢驚甚則遼薊之勢日就孤
危而江右之賊歲成延蔓殊非聖世之所宜
有者正堯舜憂民之時周宣勵精之日也臣
伏讀
聖制有曰間者水旱為灾黎民阻饑戎狄時警邊
圉弗靖而南賊尤甚歷時越歲尚未底寧豈有
司莫體朕心皆殘民以逞有以致之與
陛下之言及此萬國萬民之福也臣竊觀内外諸
臣凡析圭儋爵結綬分符者孰非

punctuated:
欽天有記，以表昭事之忱；祖德有詩，以發聿追之念。至於慮切民恫，任專吏職，内責成於守令矣，而巡督之臣歲不絕遣；外付托於將帥矣，而總制之命任必加隆。無一念不在於民瘼，無一言不軫乎國慮。臣有以仰窺陛下之心，即堯舜之心，而周宣不足侔也。於今諸瑞咸集，四靈畢至，固足以彰陛下之峻德鴻勳，超卓百代矣。然淫潦為灾，則塍畦有墊溺之苦；亢旱為虐，則阡陌有枯槁之憂。倭夷竊發於東南，而海波弗靖；醜虜跳梁於西北，而邊塵屢驚。甚則遼薊之勢日就孤危，而江右之賊歲成延蔓，殊非聖世之所宜有者。正堯舜憂民之時，周宣勵精之日也。
臣伏讀聖制，有曰：「間者水旱為灾，黎民阻饑，戎狄時警，邊圉弗靖，而南賊尤甚，歷時越歲，尚未底寧。豈有司莫體朕心，皆殘民以逞，有以致之與？」陛下之言及此，萬國萬民之福也。臣竊觀内外諸臣，凡析圭儋爵、結綬分符者，孰非
translation_en:
…You have composed an account on revering Heaven to express your sincerity in illustriously serving it, and a poem on ancestral virtue to voice your resolve to follow your forebears. Your concern extends keenly to the people’s suffering, and you assign officials specific responsibilities. Within the realm, you hold prefects and county magistrates accountable for results, yet every year you continue to dispatch officials to inspect and supervise them. On the frontiers, you entrust affairs to generals, yet invariably confer heightened authority on those appointed supreme commanders. Not a single thought of yours strays from the people’s afflictions; not a single utterance fails to express concern for the state. Your servant can thus perceive, with reverence, that Your Majesty’s heart is the very heart of Yao and Shun, which even King Xuan of Zhou could not equal. Now auspicious signs gather and all four numinous creatures have appeared. These surely suffice to manifest Your Majesty’s lofty virtue and great achievements, surpassing those of a hundred generations. Yet when excessive rains bring disaster, the cultivated fields suffer inundation; when severe drought wreaks havoc, the farmlands face withering and desiccation. Japanese raiders launch sudden attacks in the southeast, leaving the seas unsettled; vile enemies run rampant in the northwest, repeatedly alarming the frontier. Worse still, the position of Liao and Ji grows more isolated and precarious by the day, while the bandits of Jiangyou spread farther year after year. Such things ought never to occur in a sage’s reign. This is precisely a time for concern for the people such as Yao and Shun showed, a day for strenuous exertion such as King Xuan of Zhou displayed.
Your servant has reverently read the imperial composition, which says: “Of late, floods and droughts have brought disaster, and the common people have suffered hunger. The Rong and Di repeatedly threaten us, and the frontiers are unsettled; the southern bandits are especially troublesome. Seasons and years have passed, yet peace has still not been attained. Could it be that the responsible officials fail to understand My heart, and that all indulge their own desires at the people’s expense, thereby bringing this about?” That Your Majesty speaks of these matters is a blessing for all lands and all people. Your servant humbly observes that, among officials at court and in the provinces, all who have received jade tablets and noble rank, tied on official seal-ribbons, and been entrusted with tallies of authority—who among them has not…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
陛下之寵榮乎凡擁旄杖鉞制閫握兵者孰非
陛下之威靈乎謂宜夙夜匪懈寢處不遑布寧謐
之化於域中揚振肅之威於閫外不負
天子而勿為聖世之瘝官也然各私其身者罔致
恤於民依各利其家者莫究心於國事內而
守令藩臬固必有旬宣惠和憂勤撫字之臣
矣然而肥已瘠民營私蠹國以催科聚斂為
能以簿書期會為急者亦多有之也外而營
屯督府固必有敵愾鷹揚嚴明果毅之臣矣
然而坐失機宜輕損威重隱敗衄以為捷幸
安靜以為福者亦恒有之也人臣咸若是則
何以成內脩外攘之功而佐久安長治之業
哉蓋
陛下愛民之心容保如天地而諸臣不能承宣
德意以弘康國之猷
陛下遏亂之志果决如雷霆而諸臣不能奉揚
威命以茂肅清之烈是自負於堯舜周宣之主
而有愧於唐虞成周之臣多矣及讀
聖制終篇有曰茲欲使上下協慮政事具修兵足
而寇患以除民安而邦本以固灾咎可弭困窮

punctuated:
陛下之寵榮乎？凡擁旄杖鉞、制閫握兵者，孰非陛下之威靈乎？謂宜夙夜匪懈，寢處不遑，布寧謐之化於域中，揚振肅之威於閫外，不負天子，而勿為聖世之瘝官也。然各私其身者，罔致恤於民依；各利其家者，莫究心於國事。內而守令藩臬，固必有旬宣惠和、憂勤撫字之臣矣；然而肥已瘠民、營私蠹國，以催科聚斂為能，以簿書期會為急者，亦多有之也。外而營屯督府，固必有敵愾鷹揚、嚴明果毅之臣矣；然而坐失機宜，輕損威重，隱敗衄以為捷，幸安靜以為福者，亦恒有之也。人臣咸若是，則何以成內脩外攘之功，而佐久安長治之業哉？蓋陛下愛民之心，容保如天地，而諸臣不能承宣德意，以弘康國之猷；陛下遏亂之志，果决如雷霆，而諸臣不能奉揚威命，以茂肅清之烈。是自負於堯舜周宣之主，而有愧於唐虞成周之臣多矣。
及讀聖制終篇，有曰：「茲欲使上下協慮，政事具修，兵足而寇患以除，民安而邦本以固，灾咎可弭，困窮
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s favor and honors? Of all those who bear command banners and battle-axes, exercise command beyond the palace gates, and control troops, who does not wield Your Majesty’s awe-inspiring authority? They ought, one would think, to be tireless morning and night, allowing themselves no leisure for sleep or rest, spreading the transforming influence of peace within the realm and displaying a stern, commanding might beyond its borders. Thus they would not fail the Son of Heaven or become negligent officials in this sagely age. Yet those who seek only their own advantage give no thought to the people’s livelihood; those who seek profit for their own households devote no care to affairs of state. Among the prefects, magistrates, provincial administration commissioners, and provincial surveillance commissioners serving within the realm, there must certainly be ministers who spread benevolent and harmonious government and diligently care for the people. Yet many also enrich themselves [?] while impoverishing the people, pursue private interests while undermining the state, regard pressing tax collections and amassing revenue as marks of ability, and treat registers, documents, and reporting deadlines as their most urgent business. Among those serving outside in military camps, garrisons, and governors-general’s headquarters, there must certainly be ministers who confront the enemy with the soaring valor of hawks, who are strict, discerning, resolute, and courageous. Yet there are also invariably those who let strategic opportunities slip away, recklessly diminish their authority and prestige, conceal defeats and present them as victories, and count themselves fortunate if they happen to enjoy quiet and peace. If ministers all act thus, how can they accomplish internal reform and the repulsion of external enemies, and assist in establishing lasting peace and enduring good government? Your Majesty’s love for the people embraces and protects them like Heaven and Earth, yet your ministers cannot transmit and carry out your benevolent intentions so as to advance your plans for the well-being of the state. Your Majesty’s determination to quell disorder is as decisive as thunder, yet your ministers cannot uphold and proclaim your commanding authority so as to achieve greater success in restoring order. Thus they fail a ruler equal to Yao, Shun, and King Xuan of Zhou, and fall far short of the ministers of Tang and Yu and of the flourishing Zhou.
When I reached the end of the imperial decree, I read: “Now I wish those above and below to deliberate in concert, all affairs of government to be put in order, military strength to be sufficient to eliminate the scourge of bandits, and the people to be secure so that the foundations of the state may be firm, disasters and calamities to be averted, and hardship and destitution…”

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
可復以媲美虞周之治其何道而可臣愚以為
上者下之表也政事者臣之紀也足兵以除
寇將帥之責任也安民以固國守令之職業
也灾咎之有無困窮之復否皆由此出者也
為
今日計莫先於任人尤莫要於擇人夫
國家分職命官衆矣即列郡專城遐陬僻壤莫
不置吏盖未嘗不任人也臣以為任之而未
當也
國家舉賢斂才舊矣即銓司法曹明黜顯擢罔
===
有違例盖未嘗不擇人也臣以為擇之而未
精也任之未當與擇之未精而欲得人以裨
聖治是猶楩梓未充而需棟梁之用穡蓘弗
習而希稼穡之成臣知其弗能也故夫欲修
内治者在慎擇乎守令而已矣欲平外患者
在慎擇乎將帥而已矣董仲舒曰守令者民
之師帥所使承流而宣化者也守令而不得
其人雖日布蠲恤之令時厪惠鮮之思民猶
不被其澤也今也闔郡無文翁之化而漁獵
民資者接踵邑里無魯恭之風而朘剥民膏
alt_text:
可復以媲美虞周之治其何道而可臣愚以為
上者下之表也政事者臣之紀也足兵以除
寇將帥之責任也安民以固國守令之職業
也災眚之有無困窮之復否皆由此出者也
為
今日計莫先於任人尤莫要於擇人夫
國家分職命官衆矣即列郡專城遐陬僻壤莫
不置吏蓋未嘗不任人也臣以爲任之而未
當也
國家舉賢歛才𥨸矣即銓司法曹明黜顯擢罔
有違例蓋未嘗不擇人也臣以爲擇之而未
精也任之未當與擇之未精而欲得人以裨
聖治是猶楩梓未充而需棟梁之用穮蔉弗
習而希稼穡之成臣知其弗能也故夫欲修
內治者在愼擇乎守令而已矣欲平外患者
在愼擇乎將帥而已矣董仲舒曰守令者民
之師帥所使承流而宣化者也守令而不得
其人雖日布蠲恤之令時厪惠鮮之恩民猶
不被其澤也今也闔郡無文翁之化而漁獵
民資者接踵邑里無魯恭之風而朘剝民膏
punctuated:
可復，以媲美虞周之治，其何道而可？」臣愚以為，上者，下之表也；政事者，臣之紀也。足兵以除寇，將帥之責任也；安民以固國，守令之職業也。灾咎之有無，困窮之復否，皆由此出者也。
為今日計，莫先於任人，尤莫要於擇人。夫國家分職命官衆矣，即列郡專城、遐陬僻壤，莫不置吏，盖未嘗不任人也。臣以為任之而未當也。國家舉賢斂才舊矣，即銓司法曹，明黜顯擢，罔有違例，盖未嘗不擇人也。臣以為擇之而未精也。任之未當與擇之未精，而欲得人以裨聖治，是猶楩梓未充而需棟梁之用，穡蓘弗習而希稼穡之成，臣知其弗能也。
故夫欲修内治者，在慎擇乎守令而已矣；欲平外患者，在慎擇乎將帥而已矣。董仲舒曰：「守令者，民之師帥，所使承流而宣化者也。」守令而不得其人，雖日布蠲恤之令，時厪惠鮮之思，民猶不被其澤也。今也，闔郡無文翁之化，而漁獵民資者接踵；邑里無魯恭之風，而朘剥民膏
translation_en:
…may be relieved, so that our government may rival that of Yu and Zhou: by what means can this be achieved?” In my humble judgment, those above are the example for those below, and affairs of government are the guiding framework for ministers. Making the armed forces sufficient to eliminate bandits is the responsibility of commanders; bringing peace to the people to secure the state is the duty of prefects and county magistrates. Whether calamities occur and whether hardship is relieved all follow from these things.
In planning for the present, nothing takes precedence over appointing men, and nothing is more essential than selecting them. The state has established numerous offices with distinct duties and appointed officials to them. Even throughout the prefectures and their cities, and in distant corners and remote districts, officials are stationed everywhere. Thus it has certainly not failed to appoint men. Your servant believes, however, that its appointments have not been appropriate. The state has long promoted the worthy and gathered talent. Even in the personnel-selection and judicial offices, dismissals and promotions are openly carried out, without departing from established rules. Thus it has certainly not failed to select men. Your servant believes, however, that its selection has not been sufficiently discerning. To hope to obtain men who will assist Your Majesty’s sagely government when appointments are inappropriate and selection insufficiently discerning is like expecting timber to serve as ridgepoles and beams before the pian and zi trees have grown sufficiently, or hoping for a successful harvest without having learned cultivation and earthing up. Your servant knows that this cannot succeed.
Thus, to put internal government in order requires only the careful selection of prefects and county magistrates; to quell external troubles requires only the careful selection of commanders. Dong Zhongshu said: “Prefects and county magistrates are the people’s teachers and leaders, charged with receiving the influence of government and spreading its transforming instruction.” If the wrong men serve as prefects and county magistrates, then even if orders for tax remission and relief are issued daily, and thought is constantly devoted to benefiting the needy, the people will still not receive those blessings. Today, throughout the prefectures there is none of Wen Weng’s transforming influence, while those who prey upon the people’s resources follow one another in succession; in the towns and villages there is none of Lu Gong’s exemplary conduct, while those who strip away the people’s sustenance…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
者比肩以狼牧羊而暴政日聞以齒焚身而
敗官弗恤郡縣之民幾何不流離而攘竊也
必也精選用之法嚴舉劾之科其未任也試
以經濟之畧必求諳練民情通達治體而不
拘選用之途如唐之試理人策可也其既任
也責以久任之功必使吏安其官民狎其政
而不拘遷轉之格如漢之為吏長子孫可也
其任而獲效也優以格外之賞必旌之車服
崇之階銜以彰卓異之勳如漢之爵至關內
侯可也如是則有民有土之寄不輕數遷數
===
易之弊可免而人知淬勵以期不負乎優渥
之恩矣寧有守令失人之患哉孫武曰將者
三軍之命國之重任不可不知也將帥而不
得其人雖決策於
九重定計於千里猶未可以臨敵也今也操練之
律雖嚴而士無投石超距之勇衣糧之給如
故而將無搴旗陷陣之能論戰闘則縮頸而
股栗聞調遣則掩耳而口噤邊圉之寇幾何
不肆行而竊發也必也慎武舉之選嚴比試
之條有洞識兵機明習邊務者材可任也則

敗官弗恤郡縣之民幾何不流離而擾竊也

崇之階銜以彰卓異之勳如漢之爵至關內
侯可也如是則有民有土之寄不輕數遷數
===
易之弊可免而人知淬勵以期不負乎渙渥
之恩矣寧有守令失人之患哉孫武曰將者
三軍之命國之重任不可不知也將帥而不
得其人雖決策於
九重定計於千里猶未可以臨敵也今也操練之
律雖嚴而士無投石超距之勇衣糧之給如
故而將無搴旗陷陣之能論戰鬬則縮頸而
股栗聞調遣則掩耳而口噤邊圉之寇幾何
不肆行而竊發也必也慎武舉之選嚴比試
之條有洞識兵機明習邊務者材可任也則
punctuated:
者比肩。以狼牧羊，而暴政日聞；以齒焚身，而敗官弗恤。郡縣之民，幾何不流離而攘竊也？必也精選用之法，嚴舉劾之科。其未任也，試以經濟之畧，必求諳練民情、通達治體，而不拘選用之途，如唐之試理人策可也。其既任也，責以久任之功，必使吏安其官、民狎其政，而不拘遷轉之格，如漢之為吏長子孫可也。其任而獲效也，優以格外之賞，必旌之車服、崇之階銜，以彰卓異之勳，如漢之爵至關內侯可也。如是，則有民有土之寄不輕，數遷數易之弊可免，而人知淬勵，以期不負乎優渥之恩矣。寧有守令失人之患哉？
孫武曰：「將者，三軍之命，國之重任，不可不知也。」將帥而不得其人，雖決策於九重、定計於千里，猶未可以臨敵也。今也操練之律雖嚴，而士無投石超距之勇；衣糧之給如故，而將無搴旗陷陣之能。論戰闘，則縮頸而股栗；聞調遣，則掩耳而口噤。邊圉之寇，幾何不肆行而竊發也？必也慎武舉之選，嚴比試之條。有洞識兵機、明習邊務者，材可任也，則
translation_en:
…such men stand shoulder to shoulder. Wolves are set to shepherd sheep, and reports of oppressive government arrive daily; they bring destruction upon themselves through their own teeth [?], yet care nothing for their failures in office. How can the people of the prefectures and counties avoid displacement and theft? We must refine the methods of selection and appointment and enforce strict rules for recommendation and impeachment. Before appointment, candidates should be tested on their plans for governing. We must seek men thoroughly familiar with the people's circumstances and well versed in the principles of government, without restricting the avenues of recruitment. The Tang practice of testing candidates with policy questions on governing the people would serve. Once appointed, they should be held responsible for what sustained tenure can accomplish. Officials must be allowed to settle into their offices and the people to become accustomed to their administration, without rigid adherence to rules governing promotion and transfer. The Han practice whereby officials remained in office long enough to raise children and grandchildren would serve. When their service produces results, they should receive exceptional rewards: carriages and robes to honor them, and higher ranks and titles to recognize outstanding achievements. The Han practice of granting noble rank as high as Marquis within the Passes would serve. Thus, responsibility for people and territory would not be treated lightly, and the abuses of repeated transfers and replacements could be avoided. Men would know to temper and spur themselves on, hoping not to disappoint such generous favor. How could there then be any concern that unsuitable men served as prefects and magistrates?
Sun Wu said: “The general holds the life of the armies in his hands and bears a weighty responsibility for the state; this must be understood.” If unsuitable men are made commanders, even decisions reached within the imperial palace and plans laid for operations a thousand li away will not suffice to confront the enemy. Today, although the rules for training are strict, the soldiers lack the valor to hurl stones and leap distances; although clothing and provisions are supplied as before, the generals lack the ability to seize enemy banners and storm their ranks. At talk of battle, they draw in their necks and their thighs tremble; on hearing orders for deployment, they cover their ears and keep their mouths shut. How can raiders on the frontier fail to run rampant and launch sudden attacks? We must exercise care in selection through the military examinations and enforce strict rules for competitive testing. Where there are men who thoroughly understand military opportunities and are well acquainted with frontier affairs, whose abilities qualify them for service, then…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
不拘以騎射之習如任杜預以平吳可也有
摧鋒陷敵決勝先登者功可錄也則不繩以
文法之細如赦魏尚於雲中可也有保障一
方折衝萬里者權可假也則不牽以中制之
命如委充國於金城可也如是則真材不耻
於武弁良將不苦於約束而人得展布以自
效夫捍禦之能矣安有將帥失人之患哉有
賢守令以宣德化於域中則政治畢舉而內
有順治之休有名將帥以揚威靈於閫外則
紀律章明而外有威嚴之烈由是民生舉安
===
則邦本有磐石之固由是兵威日振則寇患
無潢池之虞和氣交蒸於海宇而災害不興
頌聲流布於黔黎而困窮以復尚何不足以
成久安長治之業而追唐虞成周之盛哉抑
臣又聞之
朝廷者四方之極也純心者用人之樞也惟
陛下常存敬一之心以端拱於上而已敬則存其
心而不放一則純乎理而不雜深宮燕閒之
中而不忘乎知人安民之慮齋居邃密之際
而日嚴夫敬

punctuated:
不拘以騎射之習，如任杜預以平吳可也。有摧鋒陷敵、決勝先登者，功可錄也，則不繩以文法之細，如赦魏尚於雲中可也。有保障一方、折衝萬里者，權可假也，則不牽以中制之命，如委充國於金城可也。如是，則真材不耻於武弁，良將不苦於約束，而人得展布以自效夫捍禦之能矣，安有將帥失人之患哉？有賢守令以宣德化於域中，則政治畢舉，而內有順治之休；有名將帥以揚威靈於閫外，則紀律章明，而外有威嚴之烈。由是民生舉安，則邦本有磐石之固；由是兵威日振，則寇患無潢池之虞。和氣交蒸於海宇，而災害不興；頌聲流布於黔黎，而困窮以復。尚何不足以成久安長治之業，而追唐虞成周之盛哉？

抑臣又聞之：朝廷者，四方之極也；純心者，用人之樞也。惟陛下常存敬一之心，以端拱於上而已。敬則存其心而不放，一則純乎理而不雜。深宮燕閒之中，而不忘乎知人安民之慮；齋居邃密之際，而日嚴夫敬
translation_en:
…then they should not be restricted by requirements of proficiency in mounted archery; appointing them as Du Yu was appointed to pacify Wu would be fitting. For those who can break through the enemy’s vanguard and ranks, secure victory, and lead the assault, their achievements merit recognition. They should therefore not be constrained by the minutiae of legal regulations; pardoning them as Wei Shang was pardoned at Yunzhong would be fitting. For those who can safeguard a region and repel aggression ten thousand li away, discretionary authority may be granted. They should therefore not be hampered by commands issued from the court; entrusting them with responsibility as Chongguo was entrusted at Jincheng would be fitting. Thus, men of true ability would not feel ashamed to serve as military officers, and capable generals would not suffer under restrictions. Each could deploy his abilities and demonstrate his capacity for defense. How, then, could there be any concern about appointing unsuitable commanders? With worthy prefects and magistrates spreading moral instruction throughout the realm, all affairs of government would be attended to, and the interior would enjoy the blessings of orderly rule. With renowned commanders displaying imperial might beyond the military gates, discipline would be clearly established, and imperial authority would exert its force abroad. With the people’s livelihoods thereby universally secured, the foundation of the state would be as firm as a great rock. With military might thereby strengthened daily, there would be no fear of bandit disturbances, even of the sort likened to playing with weapons in a stagnant pool. Harmonious influences would rise and mingle throughout the realm, and calamities would not arise. Songs of praise would spread among the common people, and those in distress and poverty would recover. What, then, would be lacking for achieving enduring peace and lasting order, and matching the flourishing ages of Tang and Yu and the perfected Zhou?

Your servant has also heard this: the court is the pole toward which the four quarters turn, and purity of mind is the pivot of employing men. Your Majesty need only preserve constantly a mind of reverence and unity, sitting upright with hands folded above all. Through reverence, the mind is kept present and does not wander; through unity, it remains wholly aligned with principle, without admixture. Amid the leisure of the inner palace, do not forget the concern to discern men’s worth and bring peace to the people; in the secluded depths of your residence of ritual purification, daily strengthen your reverence …

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
天法
祖之忱則心正而朝廷百官皆一於正矣文武大
吏有不奉承而守令將帥有不奮勵者哉臣
不識忌諱干冒
天威無任戰慄隕越之至臣謹對

吏有不奉承而守令將帥有不奮勵者哉臣

punctuated: 天法祖之忱，則心正而朝廷百官皆一於正矣。文武大吏有不奉承而守令將帥有不奮勵者哉？臣不識忌諱，干冒天威，無任戰慄隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: …Heaven and emulating the ancestors: with this devotion, Your Majesty’s heart will be upright, and all the officials of the court will be united in uprightness. Could the high civil and military officials fail to carry out Your Majesty’s will, or the prefects, magistrates, and military commanders fail to exert themselves? Your servant, ignorant of taboos, has dared to offend Your Majesty’s awe-inspiring authority. I am overcome with trembling and the utmost dread. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
臣王錫爵
臣對臣聞帝王之御世也必文武並用而後
天下之治法以行必仁智相須而後天下之
治人以得何謂治法興天下之利除天下之
害使遠邇胥匡中外禔福而順治威嚴永孚
于休者皆法也何謂治人以天下之才任天
下之事使明良一德事使同心而奔走禦侮
各稱其職者皆人也人固緣法而舉法必待
人而行是故欲行治法則修文以布懷柔之
德經武以彰撻伐之威而安內攘外之功兼
===
舉之矣欲得治人則本仁以弘翕受之公盡
智以昭旌別之典而輔理承化之績恒賴之
矣自古太平之世君逸於上臣勞於下而四
方為之嚮風八表為之順則者特有此具也
不然上雖有仁聖之主而下無忠良之佐君
雖有願治之志而民不得被至治之澤非惟
官失其人而法亦因之以不舉是豈可無轉
移之術哉欽惟
皇帝陛下以
聖神文武之資立仁義中正之極恭己垂裳而百

Your servant Wang Xijue.

Your servant replies: I have heard that when emperors and kings govern the world, they must employ both civil and military means before methods of governing the realm can be put into practice; benevolence and wisdom must complement one another before men capable of governing the realm can be obtained. What are methods of government? Promoting what benefits the realm and eliminating what harms it, bringing places far and near alike into proper order, ensuring peace and blessings within and beyond the realm, and making both gentle governance and stern authority enduringly accord with goodness—all these belong to methods. What are men of government? Employing the realm’s talents to undertake its affairs, so that an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers share one virtue, those who serve and those who direct them share one purpose [?], and those who exert themselves in service and repel aggression each fulfill their duties—all these depend on men. Men are indeed brought into service through methods, but methods necessarily await men to carry them out. Thus, to put methods of government into practice, one must cultivate civil affairs to spread the virtue that wins allegiance, and attend to military affairs to display the might of punitive campaigns; the achievements of securing the interior and repelling external threats will then both be accomplished. To obtain men capable of governing, one must take benevolence as the foundation, broadening the impartiality with which all are received, and exercise wisdom to the fullest, making clear the standards for recognition and discrimination; enduring achievements in assisting government and carrying forward its transforming influence depend upon these.

Since antiquity, in ages of great peace, the ruler has been at ease above while his ministers have labored below, and the four quarters have inclined toward his influence while the eight outer regions have obeyed his standards, solely because these means were in place. Otherwise, though there may be a benevolent and sagely ruler above, there are no loyal and worthy assistants below; though the ruler may aspire to good government, the people cannot receive the blessings of consummate order. title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
富庶之休夷狄厎蕩平之績又何其不勞而
成功之若是也蓋當是時有吉甫方叔諸臣
矢心戮力以弘濟時艱而宣王特委任責成
爾已所以然者豈堯舜宣王無憂天下之心
而專屬之臣與蓋人君所履者天位也所治
者天職也天何言哉以一氣運於上而四時
五行為之節宣於其間者分也君何為哉以
一德宰於上而百司庶府為之協理於其下
者亦分也唐虞成周之世君法天道而握樞
以馭其臣臣代天工而勤職以事其君此所
===
以化災沴為禎祥轉兵車為玉帛當時頌聖
後世垂休良有以也由是觀之水旱盜賊之
災固不足以為盛世之累其所以斡旋氣化
保衛生靈者則在乎奮庸熈載之有人而折
衝禦侮之有賴耳洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇丕顯之謨無以加矣然軍
旅之後旱暵相仍而湖南辰貴之間時猶揚
塵鳴鏑屡犯王誅則水旱盜賊之警不盡無
也然而患不及民者則以內有劉宋諸臣為
之經理其文事外有徐常諸臣為之振揚其

富庶之休，夷狄厎蕩平之績，又何其不勞而成功之若是也！蓋當是時，有吉甫、方叔諸臣矢心戮力，以弘濟時艱，而宣王特委任責成爾已。所以然者，豈堯舜宣王無憂天下之心，而專屬之臣與？蓋人君所履者天位也，所治者天職也。天何言哉？以一氣運於上，而四時五行為之節宣於其間者，分也。君何為哉？以一德宰於上，而百司庶府為之協理於其下者，亦分也。唐虞成周之世，君法天道而握樞以馭其臣，臣代天工而勤職以事其君。此所以化災沴為禎祥，轉兵車為玉帛，當時頌聖，後世垂休，良有以也。由是觀之，水旱盜賊之災，固不足以為盛世之累。其所以斡旋氣化、保衛生靈者，則在乎奮庸熈載之有人，而折衝禦侮之有賴耳。

…the blessings of prosperity and abundance, and the achievement of bringing the Yi and Di peoples to peace: how could such success have been attained with so little exertion! At that time, ministers such as Jifu and Fang Shu pledged their hearts and joined their efforts to overcome the difficulties of the age, while King Xuan merely entrusted them with responsibilities and held them accountable for results. Was this because Yao, Shun, and King Xuan had no concern for the realm and left it entirely to their ministers? The position occupied by the ruler is Heaven’s position, and the duties he administers are Heaven’s duties. What does Heaven say? The single vital force moves above, while the four seasons and five phases regulate and distribute it in their midst: this is their allotted function. What does the ruler do? His unified virtue governs above, while the many offices and bureaus coordinate affairs below: this, too, is their allotted function. In the ages of Tang and Yu and of the flourishing Zhou, rulers modeled themselves on Heaven’s Way and held the pivot of authority to direct their ministers; ministers performed Heaven’s work and diligently discharged their duties in service to their rulers. Thus calamities were transformed into auspicious signs, and war chariots gave way to jade and silk offered in peaceful relations. There was good reason why their sageliness was praised in their own time and their glory handed down to later generations. Viewed in this light, floods, droughts, and brigandage need not mar a flourishing age. The means of guiding the transformations of vital forces and protecting living beings lie in having men who apply their abilities and advance the work of government, and dependable servants who repel aggression and resist insult.

…must reach you; concerned about armed resistance in Min and Guang, you tirelessly seek counsel. Your benevolent heart and benevolent government truly rival those of Tang and Yu and put even the accomplished Zhou to shame, though you claim no credit. Surely officials should therefore be equal to their duties and the people at peace, moral transformation flourishing and customs admirable; the foundations of the realm should be secure within, with no calamities or ominous anomalies arising, and the state's prestige should extend abroad, with no need to employ arms. Yet recently the common people have suffered famine, and the rebels in the south have grown increasingly fierce. Seasons and years have passed without relief from Your Majesty's anxiety. Your servant is deeply perplexed by this. Having privately pondered its causes, I believe that, although Your Majesty's concern for the people is earnest, those charged with carrying out and proclaiming your beneficent intentions may include many selfish, self-serving ministers. Although Your Majesty diligently strives to suppress disorder, those charged with extending your awe-inspiring authority may not be men who exert themselves in loyal service. This is why your beneficence has not reached everywhere and the desired results of government have not been attained.
Your servant has heard that achievements in securing peace within and repelling threats from without depend upon civil and military affairs, and that those entrusted with civil and military responsibilities are generals and officials. The plans by which the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity secured lasting peace and enduring order invariably proceeded from this principle. Leaving aside the time of Tang and Yu and earlier, the Rites of Zhou describes Officers of Reserves, who managed the provisions accumulated in the xian and du domains against famine; Granary Directors, who kept accounts of the nine grains to report abundance or scarcity; District Preceptors, who made seasonal rounds among the people; and Relief Officers, who dispensed assistance at the king's command. Above them were ministers who toured the realm to spread benevolent and harmonious government, tending the common people day and night and reporting their administration to the court. Thus ministers actually bore responsibility for bringing peace to the people; the ruler did not undertake it himself. Investigation of wrongdoing was entrusted to the Masters of Justice, and inquiries into killings to the Court Officers. …bring order to their ranks and repel aggression on the frontiers: thus the responsibility for suppressing disorder is truly borne by the ministers, and the ruler likewise does not undertake it himself. The ruler does not act himself; his ministers act for him. The ministers act in the ruler’s stead, and the ruler entrusts them with these duties. Toil and repose each fall to their proper place, and civil and military officials alike fully exercise their talents. Under such circumstances, it would be impossible for the realm to remain ungoverned.
Those who now fasten on their seals’ ribbons and receive tallies of authority to serve as Your Majesty’s officials have certainly been charged by Your Majesty with bringing peace to the people. Yet, examining these men dispassionately, can they truly share their salaries to relieve the people, as Fu Zhan did? Can they truly dam waters and construct reservoirs, as Xiahou Dun did? Can they truly relax prohibitions to benefit the people, as Cai Qi did, or open granaries to save the starving, as Wang Wang did? Such men exist, but some cannot put their abilities into effect, while those who drain the pond to catch its fish, enriching their private purses, are everywhere. Worse still, they fail to report floods and droughts truthfully, leaving clerks to inflate or reduce the figures. The common people consequently cry out in distress and begin to contemplate rebellion.
Those who now bear banners and wield battle-axes to serve as Your Majesty’s generals have certainly been charged by Your Majesty with suppressing disorder. Yet, upon examining these men, can they truly take cities with a riding whip, as Zhang Er did? Can they truly move an army with the ease of resting upon pillows and mats, as Chongguo did [?]? Can they truly tread through blood in an enemy court, as Li Jing did, or pour a libation on the banks of the Yangzi, as He Ruobi did? Such men exist, but some cannot rouse themselves to action, while those who are weak, fearful, and cowardly, squandering their official provisions and salaries, are everywhere. Worse still, they arbitrarily appropriate credit for enemy heads taken and withhold regular allowances. The soldiers consequently grow resentful and begin to hold the Central Kingdom in contempt. Now, because the people are impoverished, bandits arise…

text:
匪仁則推求太過而賢才不樂于嚮用是故
欲為擇吏計則莫若廣選舉之途如古之孝
弟賢良與文學並進可也嚴考課之典如古
之大明黜陟歲終奏舉殿最可也行久任之
法如古之居官長子孫有績則進爵加秩可
也而又申勅銓曹使之選任有司務求端良
修潔之士而儇薄好名者無所容焉將見百
司競勸廉賢彙征旬宣者為曾鞏之去疾廉
謹者為羊續之懸魚雖有水旱之災而困窮
之民且將還定而安集矣唐虞風動之休成
===
周順治之化不可以復見乎欲為擇將計則
莫若畧世裔以求真才如古之起自行陣而
拜為大將者可也專委任以需實效如古之
便宜行事而不從中制者可也信賞罰以勵
頹靡如古之謗書盈篋而不問揮淚斬將而
不恤可也而又嚴責本兵使之選任將帥務
求沉毅果敢之士而庸懦無能者弗得與焉
將見策士效謀勇夫效力督撫者皆良平之
器授鉞者皆韓白之才雖有竊發之警而烏
集之眾且將喙息之不暇矣唐虞來王之化

欲為擇將計，則莫若畧世裔以求真才，如古之起自行陣而拜為大將者可也；專委任以需實效，如古之便宜行事而不從中制者可也；信賞罰以勵頹靡，如古之謗書盈篋而不問，揮淚斬將而不恤可也。而又嚴責本兵，使之選任將帥，務求沉毅果敢之士，而庸懦無能者弗得與焉。將見策士效謀，勇夫效力，督撫者皆良平之器，授鉞者皆韓白之才，雖有竊發之警，而烏集之眾且將喙息之不暇矣。唐虞來王之化
translation_en:
…without benevolence, scrutiny becomes excessive, and worthy men are unwilling to enter service. Thus, in planning the selection of officials, nothing is better than broadening the avenues of recommendation and selection: one might follow antiquity in advancing men of filial devotion, fraternal respect, worthiness, and goodness alongside men of literary learning. One should make the regulations for evaluating performance rigorous: one might follow antiquity in clearly determining demotions and promotions and reporting the lowest and highest assessments at year’s end. One should institute long tenure in office: one might follow antiquity in allowing officials to remain in office long enough to raise sons and grandsons, advancing their noble rank and increasing their official grade when they achieve results. Furthermore, renewed injunctions should be issued to the personnel authorities, requiring them, when selecting administrative officials, to seek upright, good men of cultivated and unsullied conduct, leaving no place for frivolous men who chase reputation. Then we shall see officials in every office striving to distinguish themselves, and incorruptible and worthy men advancing together. Those charged with disseminating imperial governance will remove the people’s afflictions as Zeng Gong did; those of incorruptible and scrupulous conduct will emulate Yang Xu in hanging up the fish offered to him. Even if floods and droughts occur, the impoverished people will regain stability and settle in peace. Could we not witness again the blessings of virtue spreading like the wind under Tang and Yu, and the harmonious transformation achieved under the flourishing Zhou?

In planning the selection of commanders, nothing is better than setting aside hereditary lineage to seek genuine talent: one might follow antiquity in appointing men who rose from the ranks as great generals. One should entrust them with undivided authority and await tangible results: one might follow antiquity in allowing them to act as circumstances require without control from the court. One should make rewards and punishments dependable, to rouse the dispirited: one might follow antiquity in disregarding a chest full of slanderous letters, yet shedding tears while executing a commander without sparing him. Furthermore, the Minister of War should be held strictly responsible, requiring him, when selecting commanders, to seek men who are composed, resolute, bold, and decisive, excluding the mediocre, timid, and incompetent. Then we shall see strategists contributing their plans and brave men exerting their strength. Supreme commanders and grand coordinators will all possess the capacity of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, while those invested with the battle-axe of command will all possess the talent of Han Xin and Bai Qi. Even if sudden outbreaks of rebellion are reported, those crow-like gatherings of rebels will scarcely have time to catch their breath. The transforming influence of Tang and Yu that brought others to acknowledge their kingship…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
周室于襄之威又不可以復見乎要之廣求
賢才以備國家之用者皆仁也旌别淑慝以
昭勸懲之典者皆智也仁以運乎其智故内
外文武之臣咸欣欣焉戴
陛下之恩而不忍自負乎知遇之隆智以濟乎其
仁故内外文武之臣咸兢兢焉畏
陛下之明而不敢自蹈于欺罔之咎由是而民安
寇息由是而災消祥降萬世治平之業恒必
賴之矣抑臣又聞之圖事者貴謀之于豫而
斂才者貴養之于初今
===
朝廷以科貢取士士固多良矣然飾文華而鮮
為己之功爭進取而乏恬退之節者亦時時
有之則教化不可以不敦也請於天下學校
申明道術擇操履端純者為之長使孝弟忠
信之理廉耻禮讓之節知之既明守之既定
然後取之以科貢而委之以民社之寄則幼
學壯行不患無術窮經致用可以旁通如是
而憂天下之無良吏者未之有也
朝廷以武舉擇將將固多良矣然力足以挽強
而適用則疎辯足以警愚而臨事輒亂者亦

punctuated:
周室于襄之威，又不可以復見乎？要之，廣求賢才以備國家之用者，皆仁也；旌别淑慝以昭勸懲之典者，皆智也。仁以運乎其智，故内外文武之臣咸欣欣焉戴陛下之恩，而不忍自負乎知遇之隆；智以濟乎其仁，故内外文武之臣咸兢兢焉畏陛下之明，而不敢自蹈于欺罔之咎。由是而民安寇息，由是而災消祥降，萬世治平之業恒必賴之矣。抑臣又聞之，圖事者貴謀之于豫，而斂才者貴養之于初。
今朝廷以科貢取士，士固多良矣。然飾文華而鮮為己之功，爭進取而乏恬退之節者，亦時時有之，則教化不可以不敦也。請於天下學校申明道術，擇操履端純者為之長，使孝弟忠信之理、廉耻禮讓之節，知之既明，守之既定，然後取之以科貢，而委之以民社之寄。則幼學壯行，不患無術；窮經致用，可以旁通。如是而憂天下之無良吏者，未之有也。
朝廷以武舉擇將，將固多良矣。然力足以挽強而適用則疎，辯足以警愚而臨事輒亂者，亦
translation_en:
…and the awe-inspiring might that upheld the house of Zhou—could these not be seen again? In sum, seeking worthy talent far and wide to meet the needs of the state is benevolence; distinguishing the good from the wicked to make clear the rules of encouragement and punishment is wisdom. When benevolence guides wisdom, civil and military officials, both at court and outside it, all joyfully receive Your Majesty’s grace and cannot bear to prove unworthy of the great favor of being recognized and employed. When wisdom assists benevolence, these officials all stand in reverent fear of Your Majesty’s discernment and dare not incur the guilt of deceit. Through this, the people will be secure and banditry will cease; through this, calamities will disappear and auspicious signs descend. The achievement of orderly and peaceful government for ten thousand generations must always depend upon this. Your servant has also heard that, in undertaking affairs, what matters is planning beforehand, and in gathering talent, what matters is nurturing it from the outset.
Today the court recruits scholars through the examinations and the tribute recommendation system, and there are certainly many good men among them. Yet there are also, from time to time, those who embellish their literary accomplishments but do little to cultivate themselves, and those who compete for advancement but lack the integrity to remain content in retirement. Moral instruction must therefore be strengthened. I ask that the principles of the Way be clearly expounded in schools throughout the realm, and that men of upright and pure conduct be chosen to head them. Let students clearly understand and firmly uphold the principles of filial piety, respect for elder brothers, loyalty, and trustworthiness, and the virtues of integrity, a sense of shame, ritual propriety, and deference. Only then should they be recruited through examinations and tribute recommendation and entrusted with responsibility for the people and the altars of the soil. Thus, having studied in youth, they will put their learning into practice in maturity, and there need be no fear that they lack the means to do so. By thoroughly studying the Classics and applying their learning, they will be able to extend their understanding to other matters. Under such circumstances, there has never been cause to fear that the realm would lack good officials.
The court selects commanders through the Military Examinations, and there are certainly many good men among them. Yet there are also those whose strength suffices to draw a powerful bow but whose practical abilities are deficient, and whose eloquence suffices to awaken the ignorant but who invariably fall into confusion when faced with affairs…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
時時有之則訓習不可以不慎也請於天下
郡縣增設武學擇諳通韜畧為之師使坐作
進退之方虛實堅瑕之勢耳習所聞目熟所
見然後試之以武舉而授之以鈇鉞之任則
籌敵制勝洞如指掌戡亂鋤奸易若轉樞如
是而憂將之不良者未之有也將良矣吏良
矣天下無事
陛下無憂矣
萬幾閒暇之際
九重深邃之中其將何所事事乎臣聞天下國家
===
之本在人君一心而已自此心之至公則為
仁自此心之至明則為智以是至公至明之
心而乂安天下則文德修以是至公至明之
心而肅清天下則武功振斯道也
陛下敬一之箴固已該括而無餘矣臣愚芹曝之
私惟願益新
聖德祗慎厥終盛滿弗矜則為舜之無怠無荒幽
獨必謹則為文之亦臨亦保立綱陳紀則守
之以不愆不忘之訓任賢去邪則决之以勿
疑勿貳之明察天人理欲之幾則不邇不殖

時時有之，則訓習不可以不慎也。請於天下郡縣增設武學，擇諳通韜畧為之師，使坐作進退之方、虛實堅瑕之勢，耳習所聞，目熟所見，然後試之以武舉，而授之以鈇鉞之任，則籌敵制勝，洞如指掌；戡亂鋤奸，易若轉樞。如是而憂將之不良者，未之有也。將良矣，吏良矣，天下無事，陛下無憂矣。
萬幾閒暇之際，九重深邃之中，其將何所事事乎？臣聞天下國家之本，在人君一心而已。自此心之至公則為仁，自此心之至明則為智。以是至公至明之心而乂安天下，則文德修；以是至公至明之心而肅清天下，則武功振。斯道也，陛下敬一之箴固已該括而無餘矣。臣愚芹曝之私，惟願益新聖德，祗慎厥終。盛滿弗矜，則為舜之無怠無荒；幽獨必謹，則為文之亦臨亦保；立綱陳紀，則守之以不愆不忘之訓；任賢去邪，則决之以勿疑勿貳之明；察天人理欲之幾，則不邇不殖
translation_en:
…such men are also found from time to time; therefore, care must be taken in their training. I ask that additional military schools be established in the prefectures and counties throughout the realm, with men thoroughly versed in military strategy selected as their teachers. Let the students become accustomed, through hearing and seeing, to the methods of sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating, and to configurations of weakness and strength, solidity and vulnerability. Only then should they be tested through the military examinations and entrusted with the command symbolized by the battle-axe. They will then understand how to assess the enemy and secure victory as clearly as they see their own palms; suppressing disorder and rooting out evildoers will be as easy as turning a pivot. With this accomplished, there has never been cause to fear that the generals would lack ability. With able generals and able officials, the realm will be free of trouble, and Your Majesty will be free of care.
In moments of respite from the myriad affairs of government, within the secluded depths of the imperial palace, to what will Your Majesty devote yourself? Your servant has heard that the foundation of the realm and the state lies solely in the ruler’s heart. Its utmost impartiality constitutes benevolence; its utmost discernment constitutes wisdom. When this utterly impartial and discerning heart brings peace and order to the realm, civil virtue is cultivated; when it purges the realm of disorder, military achievement flourishes. Your Majesty’s Admonition on Reverent Unity already encompasses this Way in its entirety. In my humble desire to offer what little I can—as one offering celery or the warmth of the sun—I wish only that you further renew your sagely virtue and remain reverently cautious to the end. If, at the height of prosperity, you refrain from pride, you will exemplify Shun’s freedom from indolence and neglect. If you remain vigilant even in solitude, you will exemplify King Wen’s sense that Heaven both watches over and protects him. In establishing the guiding principles and regulations, uphold them through the injunction to commit no error and forget nothing. In employing the worthy and dismissing the wicked, act decisively with the discernment that permits neither doubt nor vacillation. In discerning the subtle distinctions between Heaven and man, moral principle and desire, then the injunction neither to draw near [to what is improper] nor to accumulate [wealth]…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
之戒常惕然於吾之心考古今得失之監則
未危未亂之防常惺然於吾之念將見百官
庶吏莫不精白以承休而細奸小醜亦且回
心而向善恩從祥風翔德與和氣游上以答
天心之景貺下以綿
國脉于靈長董子所謂君心正而福祥集詩所
謂天保定爾亦孔之固且為
今日頌之矣至治之盛豈特比隆虞周而已哉
疎狂之論不識忌諱無任隕越之至臣謹對

踈狂之論不識忌諱無任隕越之至臣謹對
punctuated:
之戒，常惕然於吾之心；考古今得失之監，則未危未亂之防，常惺然於吾之念。將見百官庶吏莫不精白以承休，而細奸小醜亦且回心而向善。恩從祥風翔，德與和氣游，上以答天心之景貺，下以綿國脉于靈長。董子所謂「君心正而福祥集」，詩所謂「天保定爾，亦孔之固」，且為今日頌之矣。至治之盛，豈特比隆虞周而已哉！
疎狂之論，不識忌諱，無任隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en:
…may that admonition ever keep my heart vigilant; and when examining the successes and failures of past and present as a mirror, may the need to take precautions before danger or disorder arises remain ever wakeful in my thoughts. Then we shall see all officials and their subordinate functionaries purify their intentions to receive your beneficence, while even petty miscreants and lesser villains will change their hearts and turn toward goodness. Your grace will soar with auspicious winds, and your virtue will move with the harmonious breath of nature: above, answering Heaven’s magnificent blessings; below, extending the life of the dynasty into an enduring future. Master Dong’s saying, “When the ruler’s heart is upright, blessings and auspicious signs gather,” and the words of the Book of Odes, “Heaven protects and establishes you, with exceeding firmness,” will serve as praises of this very day. Would the splendor of such consummate government merely equal that of Yu and Zhou?
These rash and unrestrained remarks show no awareness of what must not be spoken. I am overwhelmed with trepidation. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
臣余有丁
臣對臣聞人君代天以理物常秉天下之大
權以成無爲之治人臣代君以協理當明天
下之大分以建匪懈之功何也君之尊猶天
也操乾綱以獨斷於上一乾元之統天焉而
凝神端拱於以享其逸而不勞臣之事君猶
事天也守坤貞以疏附於下一坤順之承天
焉而竭力圖惟於以任其勞而不避君享其
逸匪自豫也無心而成化天道本如是也人
君奉若天道嵬然臨御於九重而委任以責
===
之臣焉斯有以得大君之宜臣任其勞匪自

Your servant, Yu Youding.

Your servant replies: I have heard that the ruler acts on Heaven’s behalf to order all things, ever holding the supreme authority over the realm in order to achieve government through nonaction. Ministers assist in governing on the ruler’s behalf and should clearly understand the great distinctions of station in the realm, so as to accomplish their work without flagging. Why is this? The ruler’s exalted position resembles Heaven. He holds the guiding authority of Qian, the Creative, and decides alone above, just as the primal power of Qian presides over Heaven. Concentrating his spirit and sitting upright with hands folded, he thus enjoys repose without toil. Ministers serve their ruler as they serve Heaven. Upholding the steadfastness of Kun, the Receptive, they assist and cleave to him below, just as Kun obediently serves Heaven. Exerting all their strength in planning and deliberation, they thus undertake the toil without shirking it.

The ruler enjoys repose, but not for his own pleasure: transformation is accomplished without deliberate striving, for such is inherently the Way of Heaven. The ruler follows Heaven’s Way, presiding majestically within the ninefold palace, entrusting duties to his ministers and holding them responsible. In this way he fulfills what befits a great sovereign. Ministers undertake the toil, but not merely to exhaust themselves: they claim no achievement of their own, but bring undertakings to completion on another’s behalf, for such is inherently the Way of Earth. Ministers model themselves upon Earth’s Way, reverently and diligently attending to their various duties and offering their utmost loyalty in service to the ruler. In this way they fulfill the obligation of wholly devoted ministers.

Only when the ruler takes Heaven as the model for his own position can he take Heaven’s heart as his heart. His government can therefore conform to Heaven; even sage emperors and enlightened kings cannot depart from this in attaining the balance of reverent silence. Only when ministers serve their ruler as Heaven can they take his heart as their hearts. Their loyalty can therefore win his trust; even worthy chief ministers and loyal servants cannot depart from this in achieving harmonious and reverent service. When ruler and ministers fulfill their respective roles, the myriad transformations proceed, and their efforts to assist in affairs and bring concord to their various offices achieve complete success. title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
靈純龐之風可以坐致雍熈悠久之業自茲
有成矣欽惟
皇帝陛下稟神聖之資撫熈明之運敬一紹帝王
之道統倫制立古今之治極恭默通於
上載聲教布於遐陬禮樂明備而大車書一統之
盛華夏率俾而洽干羽兩階之休嘉靖萬邦
迄今四十有一年如一日矣臣竊伏草茅幸
際
陛下久道成化
壽考作人叨與有司之選親承
===
大廷之對而
清問下及首焉嘉慕帝王致治之盛既而軫念災
寇荐至之警深有慨於文武庶職之難其人
焉將求弭變以安民遏亂以固本且責臣等
悉心陳列勿憚勿欺也顧臣愚陋猥謭何所
知識得以少裨
陛下麻德之萬一乎然恭承
温旨仰體
淵衷敢不披瀝誠悃以對臣聞之書曰天佑下民
作之君師以對上帝是天之所以寵綏乎君

寇薦至之警深有慨於文武庶職之難其人
焉將求弭變以安民遏亂以固本且責〔臣〕等

陛下厤德之萬一乎然恭承

作之君師以對上帝是天之所以寵綏乎君
punctuated:
靈純龐之風可以坐致，雍熈悠久之業自茲有成矣。欽惟皇帝陛下，稟神聖之資，撫熈明之運，敬一紹帝王之道統，倫制立古今之治極，恭默通於上載，聲教布於遐陬。禮樂明備，而大車書一統之盛；華夏率俾，而洽干羽兩階之休。嘉靖萬邦，迄今四十有一年如一日矣。
臣竊伏草茅，幸際陛下久道成化，壽考作人，叨與有司之選，親承大廷之對。而清問下及，首焉嘉慕帝王致治之盛，既而軫念災寇荐至之警，深有慨於文武庶職之難其人焉。將求弭變以安民，遏亂以固本，且責臣等悉心陳列，勿憚勿欺也。顧臣愚陋猥謭，何所知識，得以少裨陛下麻德之萬一乎？然恭承温旨，仰體淵衷，敢不披瀝誠悃以對！
臣聞之，《書》曰：「天佑下民，作之君師，以對上帝。」是天之所以寵綏乎君
translation_en:
…a spirit of numinous purity and fullness can readily be brought about, and an enduring achievement of harmony and prosperity will henceforth be accomplished. Reverently considering Your Majesty the Emperor: endowed with divine sagacity, you preside over an age of brilliance. Through reverent singleness of purpose, you continue the transmission of the Way from the ancient emperors and kings; through ordered institutions [?], you establish the supreme standard of government for all ages. Your reverent silence communicates with Heaven above, and your civilizing influence reaches the remotest corners. Rites and music are illustrious and complete, magnifying the splendor of a realm unified in carriage gauges and writing. The people of Huaxia all obey, sharing fully in the blessings symbolized by the dance with shields and plumes between the two stairways. You have brought good order and peace to the myriad states, remaining constant as a single day throughout these forty-one years.
Your servant has dwelt obscurely among the common people, fortunate to encounter Your Majesty’s enduring Way bringing transformation and your cultivation of worthy men over a long life. Having undeservedly been selected by the responsible officials, I have personally received the opportunity to answer in the great court. Your august inquiry has reached down to us: first you expressed admiration for the flourishing government achieved by the ancient emperors and kings; then you voiced anxious concern over the warnings presented by successive disasters and bandit incursions, deeply lamenting the difficulty of finding suitable men for the many civil and military offices. You seek to quell calamities and bring peace to the people, to check disorder and secure the foundations of the state. Moreover, you charge us to present our views with utmost care, neither shrinking back nor deceiving you. Yet your servant is ignorant, uncultivated, and shallow: what knowledge could I possess that might contribute even the smallest fraction to Your Majesty’s virtue [?]? Nevertheless, having reverently received your gracious instructions and sought to comprehend your profound intentions, how could I dare withhold my sincerest feelings in replying?
Your servant has heard this saying in the Book of Documents: “Heaven aids the people below, creating for them rulers and teachers to assist the Lord on High.” Thus, Heaven’s purpose in favoring and protecting the ruler…

而君之所以受命於天者意有在也故履大
寶握中樞位曰天位焉膺歷數纘帝極統曰
天統焉以至心代天意口代天言身代天事
莫非天也則當以天自處矣禮曰惟王建國
設官分職以為民極是君之所以委任乎臣
而臣之所以承命於君者責有歸也故論定
而爵以馭其貴惟君所詔焉位定而祿以馭
其富惟君所予焉以至治君之民理君之事
分君之憂莫非君也則當以天事君矣夫以
一人而欽承昊天之明命一日萬幾不能獨
===
理后克艱厥后矣使日孜孜焉政事是親以
下同於臣則耳目不逮志慮未周而欲帝載
之咸熈也其可得乎以一身而奉若天子之
明威百僚庶府各有專成臣克艱厥臣矣使
徒泄泄然尸素是安以上負其君則職業不
修機務不理而欲臣紀之罔虧也其可得乎
粵稽古昔語帝之盛者莫過於堯舜固嘗隆
垂衣之化矣而其始焉洚水滔天思以治之
下民艱食思以康之有苗弗率思以格之而
堯舜未嘗自勞也讀書而得典謨諸篇若治

而君之所以受命於天者，意有在也。故履大寶，握中樞，位曰天位焉；膺歷數，纘帝極，統曰天統焉。以至心代天意，口代天言，身代天事，莫非天也，則當以天自處矣。《禮》曰：「惟王建國，設官分職，以為民極。」是君之所以委任乎臣，而臣之所以承命於君者，責有歸也。故論定而爵，以馭其貴，惟君所詔焉；位定而祿，以馭其富，惟君所予焉。以至治君之民，理君之事，分君之憂，莫非君也，則當以天事君矣。
夫以一人而欽承昊天之明命，一日萬幾，不能獨理，后克艱厥后矣。使日孜孜焉，政事是親，以下同於臣，則耳目不逮，志慮未周，而欲帝載之咸熈也，其可得乎？以一身而奉若天子之明威，百僚庶府，各有專成，臣克艱厥臣矣。使徒泄泄然，尸素是安，以上負其君，則職業不修，機務不理，而欲臣紀之罔虧也，其可得乎？
粵稽古昔，語帝之盛者，莫過於堯舜，固嘗隆垂衣之化矣。而其始焉，洚水滔天，思以治之；下民艱食，思以康之；有苗弗率，思以格之。而堯舜未嘗自勞也。讀《書》而得《典》《謨》諸篇，若治
translation_en:
…and there is a purpose behind the ruler’s receiving the mandate from Heaven. Thus, when he ascends the great throne and holds the central pivot of government, his position is called Heaven’s position; when he receives the allotted succession and continues the imperial sovereignty, his succession is called Heaven’s succession. His heart expresses Heaven’s intentions, his mouth speaks Heaven’s words, and his person performs Heaven’s work. All of these pertain to Heaven, so he should conduct himself as Heaven’s representative. The Rites says: “The king establishes the state, institutes offices, and divides their duties, thereby providing a standard for the people.” Thus, when the ruler entrusts responsibilities to his ministers and the ministers receive commands from their ruler, responsibility has its proper bearer. Once assessments are settled, ranks are conferred to regulate their honorable standing, solely as the ruler commands; once positions are determined, stipends are granted to regulate their wealth, solely as the ruler bestows. They govern the ruler’s people, manage the ruler’s affairs, and share the ruler’s cares. All of these pertain to the ruler, so they should serve him as they would Heaven.
One man reverently receives August Heaven’s luminous mandate, yet the myriad affairs arising each day cannot be managed by him alone: the sovereign must understand the difficulty of being sovereign. If he works diligently every day, personally attending to governmental affairs and thereby descending to perform the same work as his ministers, his eyes and ears will not reach far enough, and his deliberations will not encompass everything. Could he then hope for all the imperial undertakings to flourish? Each minister, in his own person, respectfully obeys the Son of Heaven’s manifest authority; the many officials and offices each have particular tasks to accomplish: the minister must understand the difficulty of being a minister. If ministers merely idle away their time, content to occupy office and draw stipends without service, thereby failing their ruler above, their official duties will go unfulfilled and essential affairs will remain unmanaged. Could they then hope that the proper order of ministerial service would remain unimpaired?
Looking back to antiquity, none surpass Yao and Shun when speaking of the splendor of emperors. They indeed brought to its height the transforming rule of sovereigns who merely let their robes hang down. Yet at the outset, when floodwaters rose to the sky, they sought a way to control them; when the common people struggled to obtain food, they sought a way to bring them well-being; when the Youmiao would not obey, they sought a way to bring them into submission. 洪水則有禹以底平成若教稼穡則有稷以
粒烝民若明刑罰則有皐陶以弼教化曰翼
爲曰明聽各效其職於中天之際而凡政有
未修德有未正用有未利當時諸臣皆有以
代其終是以堯舜得享無爲之逸而協和而
風動古今稱極治者唐虞爲莫及焉語王之
賢者莫過於周宣固嘗建中興之業矣而其
始焉淮夷是叛思以討之荆蠻爲讎思以征
之玁狁匪茹思以伐之而宣王亦未嘗自勞
也誦詩而得采薇諸章若平淮夷則有旬宣
===
之召伯若征荆蠻則有元老之方叔若伐玁
狁則有文武之吉甫曰奔奏曰禦侮各展其
能於多事之日而凡王賦之未進車徒之未
實綜理之未周當時諸臣皆有以共其職是
以宣王得享不勞之治而順治而威嚴古今
稱中興者成周爲難繼焉嗣是而降無翼爲
明聽之臣安望治之比隆於二帝無奔奏禦
侮之臣安望治之駕美於周王耶是宜
陛下嘉之慕之而陋三代以降於不足言也惟我
陛下篤明禋之敬而心乎

洪水，則有禹以底平成；若教稼穡，則有稷以粒烝民；若明刑罰，則有皐陶以弼教化。曰翼爲，曰明聽，各效其職於中天之際。而凡政有未修、德有未正、用有未利，當時諸臣皆有以代其終。是以堯舜得享無爲之逸，而協和，而風動。古今稱極治者，唐虞爲莫及焉。語王之賢者，莫過於周宣，固嘗建中興之業矣。而其始焉，淮夷是叛，思以討之；荆蠻爲讎，思以征之；玁狁匪茹，思以伐之。而宣王亦未嘗自勞也。誦《詩》而得《采薇》諸章，若平淮夷，則有旬宣之召伯；若征荆蠻，則有元老之方叔；若伐玁狁，則有文武之吉甫。曰奔奏，曰禦侮，各展其能於多事之日。而凡王賦之未進、車徒之未實、綜理之未周，當時諸臣皆有以共其職。是以宣王得享不勞之治，而順治，而威嚴。古今稱中興者，成周爲難繼焉。嗣是而降，無翼爲明聽之臣，安望治之比隆於二帝？無奔奏禦侮之臣，安望治之駕美於周王耶？是宜陛下嘉之慕之，而陋三代以降於不足言也。

惟我陛下篤明禋之敬，而心乎
translation_en:
…the flood, there was Yu to bring the land and waters into order; for teaching sowing and reaping, there was Ji to provide grain for the multitudes; for making punishments clear, there was Gao Yao to assist moral instruction. Whether assisting in action or bringing discernment to what was heard, each discharged his duties when the sovereign stood like the sun at its zenith. Wherever government remained imperfect, virtue unrectified, or practical provision ineffective, the ministers of that time brought the work to completion on their sovereigns’ behalf. Thus Yao and Shun enjoyed the ease of governing without action: all were brought into harmony, and their influence moved the people like the wind. Among those acclaimed throughout history for consummate government, none could equal Tang and Yu.

Among kings praised for their worthiness, none surpassed King Xuan of Zhou, who indeed accomplished a restoration. At its outset, when the Huai Yi rebelled, he sought to chastise them; when the Jing Man became enemies, he sought to campaign against them; when the Xianyun showed no restraint, he sought to attack them. Yet King Xuan, too, never had to undertake these labors himself. Reciting the Book of Odes, we encounter such poems as “Gathering Bracken”: to pacify the Huai Yi, there was the Earl of Shao, who toured the realm and proclaimed royal commands; to campaign against the Jing Man, there was the elder statesman Fang Shu; to attack the Xianyun, there was Jifu, accomplished in both civil and military affairs. Whether hastening about in royal service or resisting aggression, each displayed his abilities in those troubled days. Wherever royal military levies had not been supplied, chariots and troops had not reached full strength, or overall administration remained incomplete, the ministers of that time all fulfilled their duties. Thus King Xuan enjoyed government that required no toil of him: order prevailed, and royal authority inspired awe. Among restorations acclaimed throughout history, that of Zhou was difficult to match.

After that time, without ministers who assisted in action and brought discernment to what was heard, how could one hope for government as flourishing as that of the Two Emperors? Without ministers who hastened about in royal service and resisted aggression, how could one hope for government surpassing the excellence of the king of Zhou? Your Majesty therefore rightly commends and admires them, regarding the ages after the Three Dynasties as too inferior to merit discussion.

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
穹昊茂熈洽之化而光紹
祖宗以言其安内也
内苑耕籍重稼穡之艱難
殿工擬竣蠲各省之徵派憂下民之易虐則申
嚴考察之令慮犯法之無知則時重恤刑之
典發倉廪以賑民乏施藥餌以療民痾其恩
澤之溥及於遐邇者不啻如雲雨之行施沛
乎沾濡而無物之弗被矣以言其攘外也内
立三營開戎府以固京師之本外重九邊慎
將帥以嚴疆場之防醜虜内侵則
===
神謨密運即以驅逐于塞漠島夷外寇則
天威奮迅即以勦截於海濱意出而鬼神率從令
行而姦宄懾伏其威武之震疊於邊陲者不
啻如雷霆之鼓舞肅乎烜耀而無遠之不服
矣
身居九重而慮周四海之外
尊臨五位而威制八荒之遐天下臣民方仰協和
風動順治威嚴之治軼唐虞而越有周矣夫
何邇年以來旱潦頻仍而倉箱無卒歲之儲
公私俱困而杼軸有其空之患北虜乗飈舉

translation_en:
…the vast heavens, bringing harmonious transformation to fullness and gloriously continuing the work of your ancestors. As for securing order within the realm, Your Majesty ritually plows in the inner park, honoring the hardships of sowing and harvesting; with construction of the palace halls nearing completion, you remit the levies imposed on the provinces. Concerned that the common people may easily suffer abuse, you reiterate and strengthen the orders for evaluating officials. Fearing that people break the law through ignorance, you repeatedly emphasize the provisions for compassionate administration of punishments. You open the granaries to relieve the people's want and distribute medicines to cure their illnesses. Your beneficence reaches far and near like clouds spreading rain, drenching all abundantly and leaving nothing untouched.

As for repelling external enemies, within the realm you establish the Three Training Divisions and military headquarters to strengthen the capital's foundations; along the frontiers you give weight to the Nine Border Commands and take care in selecting commanders, making frontier defenses strict. When the vile northern foes invade, your divine plans operate in secret, and they are promptly driven back into the frontier deserts. When the island barbarians raid from abroad, your heavenly might moves swiftly, and they are promptly destroyed and intercepted along the coast. When your intention is expressed, ghosts and spirits all obey; when your orders are issued, evildoers cower in submission. Your military might shakes the borderlands like the stirring force of thunder, awesome and resplendent, leaving no place so distant that it does not submit.

Though you dwell within the ninefold palace, your concern extends beyond the Four Seas; occupying the exalted fifth position of sovereignty, your might commands even the distant Eight Wildernesses. The officials and people throughout the realm now look up to a government that brings concord, transforms like the wind, orders affairs smoothly, and inspires awe—a government surpassing those of Tang and Yu and exceeding that of Zhou. Why, then, have droughts and floods recurred so frequently in recent years, leaving granaries and bins without enough reserves to last the year? Why are public and private resources alike exhausted, and the looms threatened with standing empty? The northern foes ride the force of a rising whirlwind…

title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
之勢而不時擾我邊鄙南賊鼓烏集之羣而
連歲犯我海壖誠如
聖制所謂水旱爲災黎民阻饑戎狄自警南賊尤
甚有以厪
宵旰之懷矣臣以爲天地之大也不能必寒暑災
祥之正堯舜之聖也猶且病博施濟衆之難
今日水旱之災是即二帝儆予其咨之嘆也
南北之寇是即周時夷蠻獫狁之侵也然二
帝有儆予其咨之憂而卒不憂者以翼爲明
聽之各得其人耳周王有夷蠻獫狁之患而
===
卒不患者以奔奏禦侮之各盡其職耳今
陛下以天之心爲心而臣之陳力就列者未必能
仰體是心以亮天之工
陛下以民之心爲心而臣之專城長邑者未必能
各存是心以分民之牧臺閣之臣有誠盡翊
賛者矣而承宣之臣果皆誠盡疏附乎近侍
之臣有誠盡論思者矣而折衝之臣果皆誠
盡捍禦乎持節剖符膺民社之託者非不多

驥足者恒鮮乎羔羊之節稱催科之善者未

…with that momentum, they harass our frontiers at unpredictable times; the southern marauders rally their crow-like assemblies and invade our seacoast year after year. It is indeed as Your Majesty’s sacred decree says: “Floods and droughts bring disaster; the common people suffer hunger; the Rong and Di themselves give cause for alarm [?], and the southern marauders are especially troublesome.” These matters burden Your Majesty’s thoughts as you rise before dawn and eat only after nightfall.
Your servant believes that even Heaven and Earth, vast as they are, cannot ensure the proper course of cold and heat, calamities and auspicious events. Even Yao and Shun, sages though they were, found it difficult to extend benefits widely and bring relief to the multitude. Today’s floods and droughts are precisely what prompted the two emperors’ sighs of “Admonish me!” The raiders in the south and north are like the invasions of the Yi, Man, and Xianyun in Zhou times. Yet although the two emperors felt the anxiety expressed in “Admonish me!”, they ultimately had no cause for anxiety, because they found the right men to assist them in governing, seeing clearly, and hearing fully [?]. Although the Zhou kings suffered incursions by the Yi, Man, and Xianyun, they ultimately had no cause for distress, because those who hastened to serve and resisted aggression each fully discharged their duties.
Now Your Majesty takes Heaven’s heart as your own, yet the ministers who take office to exercise their abilities may not necessarily embody that heart and thereby assist in Heaven’s work. Your Majesty takes the people’s heart as your own, yet the ministers who govern cities and head counties may not necessarily preserve that heart and thereby share the task of shepherding the people. Among the ministers of the central government, there are those who sincerely give their utmost in assisting you; but do the ministers charged with transmitting and carrying out your commands all sincerely give their utmost in bringing the distant into allegiance? Among your close attendants, there are those who sincerely give their utmost in deliberation and reflection; but do the ministers charged with repelling the enemy all sincerely give their utmost in defense? There is no shortage of men who bear credentials of authority and receive divided tallies, entrusted with the people and the altars of the soil. title: 嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
嘉靖四十一年進士登科錄
text:
而寇患以除民安而邦本以固災咎可弭困窮
可復以媲美虞周之治其何道而可臣愚以為
吏有之今之郡守民之師帥也所當重也是
必嚴考覈之典申久任之規循良悃愊者增
秩以示榮久之若卓茂之封而不以為驟闒
茸貪墨者重罰以示辱甚則若阿大夫之烹
而不以為苛然後甄別殿最之典明吏將砥
礪以自勉而撫字之陽城寬和之黃覇自輩
出矣而以是牧民民困其少蘇乎志有之將
者國之輔也所當重也是必專委任之柄隆
===
駕馭之權有功必賞不間於羣言如任樂羊
而無有於二志有罪必懲不牽於私故如戮
馬謖而罔萌夫貸心然後鼓舞振作之用行
將皆激昂以求試而良平之督撫韓白之統
率自𠒋起矣而以是除盜盜患其少息乎如
是則得文臣以宣惠惠無不浹而國家之元
氣自固足以安內而紓鴻鴈之憂得武將以
揚威威無不奮而國家之神氣自振足以攘
外而免墉隼之害
陛下可端冕服而神不顯之德可寧黼扆而成顯

punctuated: 而寇患以除，民安而邦本以固，災咎可弭，困窮可復，以媲美虞周之治，其何道而可？臣愚以為，吏有之：「今之郡守，民之師帥也，所當重也。」是必嚴考覈之典，申久任之規，循良悃愊者增秩以示榮，久之若卓茂之封而不以為驟；闒茸貪墨者重罰以示辱，甚則若阿大夫之烹而不以為苛。然後甄別殿最之典明，吏將砥礪以自勉，而撫字之陽城、寬和之黃覇自輩出矣。而以是牧民，民困其少蘇乎？志有之：「將者，國之輔也，所當重也。」是必專委任之柄，隆駕馭之權，有功必賞，不間於羣言，如任樂羊而無有於二志；有罪必懲，不牽於私故，如戮馬謖而罔萌夫貸心。然後鼓舞振作之用行，將皆激昂以求試，而良平之督撫、韓白之統率自𠒋起矣。而以是除盜，盜患其少息乎？如是，則得文臣以宣惠，惠無不浹，而國家之元氣自固，足以安內而紓鴻鴈之憂；得武將以揚威，威無不奮，而國家之神氣自振，足以攘外而免墉隼之害。陛下可端冕服而神不顯之德，可寧黼扆而成顯
translation_en:
…and the scourge of marauders would be eliminated; the people would be secure and the foundations of the state strengthened. Calamities could be averted and deprivation remedied, so that government might rival that of Yu and Zhou. By what means can this be achieved? Your foolish servant considers the saying concerning officials [?]: “The prefects of today are the teachers and leaders of the people; they must be accorded importance.” It is therefore essential to enforce rigorous performance evaluations and reaffirm the rules for long tenure. Upright, benevolent, and sincere officials should be advanced in rank to signal honor; in time, even enfeoffment like that of Zhuo Mao should not be considered precipitous. Base, incompetent, and corrupt officials should receive severe punishment to signal disgrace; in extreme cases, even boiling alive, as in the case of the grand master of A, should not be considered harsh. Then the standards for distinguishing the worst from the best in office would be clear. Officials would strive to improve themselves, and men like Yang Cheng in nurturing the people and Huang Ba in generosity and mildness would emerge in succession. If such men tended the people, might the people's distress not find some relief?

The records say: “Generals are the supports of the state; they must be accorded importance.” It is therefore essential to vest authority firmly in those entrusted with command and enhance their power to direct their forces. Merit must invariably be rewarded, without allowing the words of others to sow distrust—as when Yue Yang was employed without any wavering of purpose. Guilt must invariably be punished, without yielding to personal ties—as when Ma Su was executed without entertaining any thought of pardon. Then measures to inspire and invigorate would take effect. Generals would all be stirred to seek opportunities to prove themselves, and governors-general and grand coordinators like Liang and Ping, and commanders like Han and Bai, would arise [?]. If such men were used to eliminate bandits, might the scourge of banditry not abate somewhat?

Thus, by obtaining civil officials to spread beneficence, that beneficence would reach everywhere, and the state's vital energies would naturally be strengthened—sufficient to secure the interior and relieve the distress of the “wild geese,” the displaced people. By obtaining military commanders to display might, that might would be exerted everywhere, and the state's spirit would naturally be invigorated—sufficient to repel external enemies and avert the danger of the “falcon upon the wall.” Your Majesty could sit upright in ceremonial cap and robes and give numinous expression to your illustrious virtue; you could rest peacefully before the embroidered throne screen and accomplish manifest…
